# God's Eye // UAP: all 251 case files

Every case, oldest first. Each has a page at https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/<id>/ and opens on the globe at https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/#/case/<id>. Status says what the evidence supports; give it and the explanation when you answer.

## Celestial phenomenon over Nuremberg (1561)

- Date: 14 April 1561 (time approximate)
- Place: Nuremberg, Holy Roman Empire (Germany)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Historical account
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Spheres, crosses, tubes and a black spear
- Witnesses: Citizens of Nuremberg
- Duration: About an hour at sunrise
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/nuremberg-1561/

A broadsheet by Hans Glaser describes a dawn "battle" in the sky: globes, crosses and cylinders that moved and fought before falling to the ground with smoke. It is a staple of UFO histories and an example of how atmospheric optics were recorded before modern science.

**Explanation:** Usually interpreted as a spectacular sun-halo display (parhelia, arcs) described in religious terms.

## Celestial phenomenon over Basel (1566)

- Date: 7 August 1566 (time approximate)
- Place: Basel, Swiss Confederacy (Switzerland)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Historical account
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Many black and fiery spheres
- Witnesses: Townspeople of Basel (as reported by the broadsheet)
- Duration: Sunrise
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/basel-1566/

A broadsheet printed in Basel by Samuel Coccius reported that at sunrise on August 7, 1566 many large black spheres were seen racing toward the Sun and seeming to fight one another, some turning red and fiery before fading. It also described a blood-red Sun on the mornings and evenings of late July. Together with Nuremberg 1561, it is one of the best-known early-modern "sky battles".

**Explanation:** Generally read as atmospheric optics (sun halos, a reddened rising sun) or dust and smoke, described in the religious language of a 16th-century broadsheet.

## Utsuro-bune — the "hollow ship" of Hitachi (1803)

- Date: 22 February 1803 (time approximate)
- Place: Haratono-hama, Hitachi Province (Ibaraki), Japan
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Historical account
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Round vessel of wood and iron with glass windows
- Witnesses: Fishermen (as told in Edo-period accounts)
- Duration: —
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/utsuro-bune-1803/

Several Japanese books of the 1820s–1840s tell how fishermen found a strange round boat washed up on the coast of Hitachi Province in 1803. Inside was a young woman who spoke no known language and clutched a box she would let no one touch. The fishermen pushed the vessel back out to sea. The drawings of the round, windowed ship are often compared with modern "flying saucers".

**Explanation:** Historians treat it as folklore: the story appears in several Edo-period collections with conflicting details, and resembles older legends of exiled women set adrift in boats.

## Bonilla observation — objects crossing the Sun (1883)

- Date: 12 August 1883
- Place: Zacatecas Astronomical Observatory, Mexico
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs
- Shape: Hundreds of dark, fuzzy bodies with tails
- Witnesses: 1 astronomer (José Bonilla)
- Duration: About 2 days
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/bonilla-zacatecas-1883/

On August 12, 1883, José Bonilla, the first director of the Zacatecas observatory, was preparing to observe sunspots when he saw dark objects crossing the face of the Sun. Over two days he counted hundreds of them and took photographs through the telescope. They were published in L'Astronomie in 1886 and are often called the first photographs of unidentified flying objects.

**Explanation:** Camille Flammarion thought Bonilla had seen birds, insects or dust close to the telescope. A 2011 study at UNAM proposed fragments of a comet passing close to Earth. Either way, nothing suggests craft.

## Mystery airship wave (1896)

- Date: 17 November 1896 (time approximate)
- Place: California to the Midwest and Texas, United States
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Historical account
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Cigar-shaped "airship" with lights and wings or propellers
- Witnesses: Thousands, over five months
- Duration: November 1896 – April 1897
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/mystery-airships-1896/

In November 1896 people in Sacramento and then San Francisco and Oakland reported a lighted airship moving across the night sky. In early 1897 reports spread east through Nebraska, Kansas, Iowa, Illinois and Texas, often with tall tales of inventors and crews. The line on the map joins the main clusters of reports in date order. It is a wave of sightings, not one object.

**Explanation:** No powered airship capable of such flights existed. Reports are attributed to newspaper hoaxes (some papers invented stories outright), bright planets such as Venus, hot-air "fire balloons" and pranks.

## Aurora, Texas airship "crash" (1897)

- Date: 17 April 1897
- Place: Aurora, Wise County, Texas (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Tracked object event
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil)
- Shape: Airship
- Witnesses: Newspaper account by S. E. Haydon
- Duration: —
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/aurora-texas-1897/

On April 19, 1897 the Dallas Morning News printed a report from Aurora. It said an airship had struck Judge J. S. Proctor's windmill around 6 a.m. and exploded, and that the pilot, "not an inhabitant of this world", had been buried in the town cemetery. It came at the very end of the 1896–97 airship wave and has been re-investigated many times since the 1970s.

**Explanation:** Widely regarded as a newspaper hoax written to draw attention to a town in decline. Later digs, metal samples and a search of the cemetery found nothing unusual.

## Tunguska explosion (1908)

- Date: 30 June 1908
- Place: Podkamennaya Tunguska River basin, Central Siberia (Russia)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Tracked object event
- Evidence: Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Many independent witnesses; Infrared or other sensor data
- Shape: A fiery body crossing the sky, “a second sun”, then a blinding flash and blast
- Witnesses: Evenk herders and settlers; the trading post at Vanavara, about 60 km away
- Duration: Seconds; the blast was heard hundreds of kilometres away
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/tunguska-1908/

At about 7:14 a.m. local time on June 30, 1908, a fireball crossed the sky over Central Siberia and exploded above the forest near the Podkamennaya Tunguska River. At the Vanavara trading post, about 60 km to the south, Semyon Semyonov later recalled that “the sky was split in two” and that the heat and the blast threw him off the porch. Seismographs as far away as Irkutsk, Tashkent, Tiflis and Jena recorded the shock, and the night skies over Europe and Asia glowed for days. About 2,150 km² of forest, several million trees, were flattened in a radial pattern, but Leonid Kulik’s expeditions, which reached the centre in 1927, found no crater: at the middle the trees still stood, stripped of their branches. The event is explained as the air burst of a small asteroid or comet; the “exploding spaceship” owes its life to a science-fiction story written in 1946.

**Explanation:** The scientific consensus is the air burst of a stony asteroid or a comet fragment tens of metres across, which exploded some 5 to 14 km above the taiga and left no crater. The idea that an alien spacecraft blew up there began with Alexander Kazantsev’s 1946 science-fiction story “Explosion” and has no physical support.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — Tunguska event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunguska_event)

## The 1909 New Zealand airship scare (1909)

- Date: 23 July 1909 (time approximate)
- Place: Kelso, West Otago, and across the South Island, New Zealand
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses
- Shape: A boat- or cigar-shaped craft by day; a moving light, sometimes with a searchlight, by night
- Witnesses: Schoolchildren and at least five adults at Kelso; residents of Dunedin, Christchurch, Oamaru, Orepuki and Blenheim; a bar pilot at the Wairau Bar
- Duration: Weeks: reports ran from mid-July into early September 1909
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/nz-airship-scare-1909/

In the last weeks of July 1909 the South Island’s newspapers began to fill with reports of a mysterious “airship”. At Kelso in West Otago, children at the school said that around noon a boat-shaped machine, pointed at both ends, with a short mast and what looked like a man sitting in it, flew over the school grounds, turned and went back toward the Blue Mountains; the local correspondent wrote that at least five people had seen it and their accounts agreed. At night, lights were reported from Orepuki, Oamaru, Christchurch and Dunedin, where a man woken at 2 a.m. said he saw a large dark object with a searchlight float past Knox College. In Blenheim on July 31 a crowd at the Criterion Hotel corner watched a light toward the Wairau Bar until after midnight, and a bar pilot reported a light passing over the pilot station toward Kaikōura. No airship existed in the country, and the reports faded by September.

**Explanation:** There was no airship in New Zealand in 1909. Most of the reports were of lights at night; the meteorologist Clement Wragge suggested secret local trials or “cosmic dust”, and said some observers had mistaken Venus, Jupiter and Mars for an airship, while others blamed hoaxers, kite lanterns and fire balloons. Historians treat it as one of the “scareship” panics of 1909–1913, when newspapers in Britain, Australia and New Zealand were full of fears of foreign airships. The daylight “boat” seen at Kelso has no specific explanation.

Sources:
- [Otago Daily Times, “100 years ago”: the Kelso report of July 1909](https://www.odt.co.nz/opinion/100-years-ago/mysterious-flying-object-observed)
- [Marlborough Express, August 2, 1909, “Seen in Blenheim” (transcription)](https://ufology.patrickgross.org/press/marlboroughexpress2aug1909.htm)
- [Gisborne Times, August 6, 1909 (Papers Past)](https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/GIST19090806.2.29)

## The Sheerness airship — questions in Parliament (1912)

- Date: 14 October 1912 (time approximate)
- Place: Sheerness and Queenborough, Isle of Sheppey, Kent (United Kingdom)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Historical account
- Evidence: Official government document or case file; Military witnesses; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: An engine heard overhead; some saw a red light and perhaps a searchlight
- Witnesses: Townspeople of Sheerness and Queenborough, among them a Royal Navy lieutenant; the naval air station at Eastchurch
- Duration: About half an hour
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/sheerness-airship-1912/

Between about 6:30 and 7 p.m. on October 14, 1912, people in Sheerness, the naval dockyard town at the mouth of the Medway, heard what sounded like an aircraft engine overhead, and some, a Royal Navy lieutenant among them, thought they saw a red light moving over the town. The naval air station at Eastchurch heard the engine too and lit flares for it, but nothing landed. A month later questions in the House of Commons asked about a “Zeppelin dirigible” over Sheerness, and on November 27 Winston Churchill, First Lord of the Admiralty, confirmed that an unknown aircraft had been heard but said he could not tell its nationality, only that it was not a British airship. The conservative press read it as a German reconnaissance flight, and the episode set off the “phantom airship” scare of early 1913, when lights and engines were reported across Britain. No German airship was ever shown to have made the flight.

**Explanation:** Never identified. Churchill told the Commons only that it was “not one of our own airships”, and privately that there was “very little doubt” it was German; the German naval Zeppelin L 1, the likeliest candidate, had landed near Berlin three hours earlier, and Germany denied any flight. The historian Brett Holman thinks an unrecorded British night flight at least as likely.

Sources:
- [Hansard — House of Commons, 27 November 1912](https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/1912-11-27)
- [Brett Holman — The Sheerness incident (Airminded)](https://airminded.org/2007/10/14/the-sheerness-incident/)

## Great Meteor Procession (1913)

- Date: 9 February 1913 (time approximate)
- Place: Toronto, Ontario, on a path from Saskatchewan to Bermuda (Canada)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Tracked object event
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses
- Shape: A procession of 40 to 60 slow fireballs in groups, with a bright tail-less body at the rear
- Witnesses: More than a hundred reports from Canada, the northeastern United States, Bermuda and ships at sea
- Duration: Each fireball 30–40 seconds; the whole procession about five minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/great-meteor-procession-1913/

At about 9 p.m. on February 9, 1913, people across Canada and the northeastern United States saw between 40 and 60 bright, slow fireballs cross the sky from horizon to horizon on practically the same path. They came in groups, threw out sparks and were followed by a clear, tail-less light “like a big star”; some witnesses heard rumbling. The same procession was reported from Bermuda and from ships as far south as Brazil, a ground track of more than 11,000 km. Much of the populous Northeast was under cloud, so most of the reports came from rural Canada. From the sound reports William Pickering put the meteors at about 56 km up. O’Keefe later named them the Cyrillids, after the feast day of St. Cyril of Alexandria, February 9.

**Explanation:** The astronomer Clarence Chant collected more than a hundred reports and found they all lay along one great-circle arc, with no radiant. He concluded the fireballs were the pieces of a small, short-lived natural satellite of the Earth, breaking up as it grazed the atmosphere. Later studies by John O’Keefe and others agreed.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — 1913 Great Meteor Procession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1913_Great_Meteor_Procession)

## Brown Mountain lights (1913)

- Date: 13 September 1913 (time approximate)
- Place: Brown Mountain, Pisgah National Forest, North Carolina (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Recurring lights
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Lights rising above the ridge
- Witnesses: Visitors to overlooks such as Wiseman's View
- Duration: Recurring
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/brown-mountain-lights/

In 1913 the Charlotte Observer reported lights rising over Brown Mountain in the Blue Ridge, during the years when electric lighting and railways were reaching the area. Two U.S. Geological Survey investigations followed. Legends of lights "seen by the Cherokee" were added later. The lights are still watched from roadside overlooks.

**Explanation:** In 1922, U.S. Geological Survey geologist George R. Mansfield used maps and an alidade to show the lights were train headlights, car headlights and brush fires in the valleys beyond the ridge. A 1913 USGS look had already pointed to locomotive headlights.

## The South African “phantom monoplane” (1914)

- Date: 11 August 1914 (time approximate)
- Place: Across the Union of South Africa: the Transvaal, Natal, the Cape and the Free State
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses
- Shape: A monoplane, or its headlights, seen at night and said to manoeuvre
- Witnesses: Thousands of people, reported in dozens of articles in the Rand Daily Mail, the Star, the Cape Times, the Cape Argus, the Natal Advertiser and the Pretoria News
- Duration: About a month, August 11 to September 9, 1914
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/south-africa-monoplane-1914/

In the first weeks of the First World War, with South Africa about to invade German South-West Africa, people across the country began to report a monoplane flying at night, sometimes with headlights, sometimes circling or hovering. The sightings came from towns hundreds of kilometres apart and from every province, and newspapers printed dozens of reports between August 11 and September 9, 1914. Many readers assumed a German machine was spying or preparing to bomb; no aircraft was ever found, and the scare ended as suddenly as it began. It is now cited, with the airship scares of the same years, as a classic example of how a war scare turns ordinary night lights into enemy aircraft.

**Explanation:** At the time it was taken for a German monoplane from South-West Africa on a spy or bombing mission, but the distances from German territory made that unlikely, and no aircraft was ever found. The sociologist Robert Bartholomew studied the episode in 1989 as a case of collective delusion: a war scare in the weeks before the South-West Africa campaign, in which lights in the night sky were read as the lamps of an enemy aircraft.

Sources:
- [Bartholomew, “The South African Monoplane Hysteria”, Sociological Inquiry 59 (1989)](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1475-682x.1989.tb00107.x)
- [Wikipedia — UFO sightings in South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO_sightings_in_South_Africa)

## Fátima — the “miracle of the sun” (1917)

- Date: 13 October 1917 (time approximate)
- Place: Cova da Iria, near Fátima, Portugal
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Photographs
- Shape: The Sun as a dull, spinning silver disc, casting coloured light and seeming to plunge towards the earth
- Witnesses: A crowd usually estimated at 50,000 to 70,000, including journalists such as Avelino de Almeida of O Século
- Duration: About ten minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/fatima-1917/

Three shepherd children had said that a lady who appeared to them at the Cova da Iria would perform a miracle at noon on October 13, 1917. A crowd of tens of thousands gathered in heavy rain; early in the afternoon, around solar noon, the clouds parted and many in the crowd reported that the Sun became a dull disc that could be looked at, spun, threw off coloured light, zig-zagged and seemed to fall towards them before returning to its place, and that their soaked clothes dried at once. Newspaper accounts, including the anticlerical O Século, described the crowd’s reaction; not everyone present saw the Sun move, and no astronomical observatory recorded anything unusual. The Church recognised the apparitions in 1930. Physicists and sceptics explain the sight as what the eye does when it stares at the Sun, with suggestion doing the rest.

**Explanation:** The Catholic Church declared the apparitions “worthy of belief” in 1930. Scientists point to the effects of staring at the Sun through thinning cloud (after-images, bleached photoreceptors and the illusion of movement), perhaps helped by high dust or a sundog, and to a crowd that had been told to expect a sign. Some ufologists have reinterpreted it as a UFO event; nothing was seen in the sky by observatories, or by people away from the crowd.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — Miracle of the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miracle_of_the_Sun)

## Battle of Los Angeles (1942)

- Date: 25 February 1942
- Place: Los Angeles, California (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Photographs; Military witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Unidentified targets / searchlight cone
- Witnesses: Thousands; coastal anti-aircraft batteries
- Duration: About 2 hours, with the barrage lasting about 1 hour
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/battle-of-los-angeles-1942/

Less than three months after Pearl Harbor, radar and observers reported an unidentified target approaching Los Angeles. Anti-aircraft batteries fired more than 1,400 shells into the night sky while searchlights converged over Santa Monica and Culver City. No aircraft was downed and no bombs fell; falling shrapnel and heart attacks caused deaths on the ground.

**Explanation:** The Navy attributed the alarm to "war nerves" after a Japanese submarine shelled the Ellwood oil field the night before; a weather balloon is thought to have started the barrage. The famous Los Angeles Times photo was heavily retouched.

## Foo fighters — 415th Night Fighter Squadron (1944)

- Date: 23 November 1944 (time approximate)
- Place: Rhine valley near Strasbourg (France / Germany)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Balls of orange or red light pacing aircraft
- Witnesses: USAAF night-fighter crews
- Duration: Recurring, late 1944 – 1945
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/foo-fighters-1944/

Crews of the U.S. 415th Night Fighter Squadron repeatedly reported glowing balls of light that followed their Beaufighters over the Rhine. They called them "foo fighters"; similar reports came from Allied and Axis crews in Europe and the Pacific.

**Explanation:** Proposed explanations include St. Elmo’s fire, ball lightning, flares and misidentified aircraft; none fits all reports.

## Ängelholm landing report (1946)

- Date: 18 May 1946 (time approximate)
- Place: Kronoskogen, Ängelholm, Sweden
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Landing / trace case
- Evidence: Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil)
- Shape: Disc landed in a forest clearing
- Witnesses: 1 (Gösta Carlsson)
- Duration: —
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/angelholm-1946/

Businessman Gösta Carlsson said that in May 1946, during the Swedish ghost-rocket summer, he came upon a disc-shaped craft standing in a clearing in the Kronoskogen forest and was warned off by its occupants. In 1972 he built a small memorial at the spot, marking where he said the craft had stood. It is now a local landmark.

**Explanation:** There is only one witness, and his account grew over the years. The traces he pointed to were never independently documented, and the story is not corroborated.

## Ghost rockets — Lake Kölmjärv (1946)

- Date: 19 July 1946
- Place: Lake Kölmjärv, Norrbotten, Sweden
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Tracked object event
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file; Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil)
- Shape: Rocket- or cigar-shaped objects
- Witnesses: Farmer Knut Lindbäck and others; Swedish military
- Duration: Wave: May–Dec 1946
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/ghost-rockets-1946/

During 1946 Scandinavian observers logged about 2,000 sightings of rocket-like objects. On 19 July a farmer watched one plunge into Lake Kölmjärv; the Swedish Army searched the lake for two weeks and found only a fresh crater in the lakebed.

**Explanation:** Swedish, British and U.S. investigators found no Soviet rockets; many of ~2,000 reports were meteors, but around 200 radar returns and several crashes into lakes were never explained.

## Maury Island incident (1947)

- Date: 21 June 1947 (time approximate)
- Place: Maury Island, Puget Sound, Washington (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Photographs
- Shape: Six doughnut-shaped craft, one said to be damaged
- Witnesses: Harold Dahl, his son and a colleague, Fred Crisman (claimed)
- Duration: A few minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/maury-island-1947/

A harbour patrolman, Harold Dahl, said six large doughnut-shaped craft circled above his boat off Maury Island in the afternoon of June 21, 1947, three days before Kenneth Arnold’s famous sighting. One craft was said to be damaged and to shed hot metallic slag that burned his son and killed the dog. Dahl’s employer, Fred Crisman, backed the story, and the case was investigated by Kenneth Arnold and by two Army Air Forces intelligence officers. It is remembered as one of the first reported UFO hoaxes, and for the first story of a “man in black” silencing a witness.

**Explanation:** Investigators judged it a hoax: the “debris” was ordinary slag and rock, and the photographs showed nothing. The two men involved later gave conflicting accounts.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — Maury Island incident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maury_Island_incident)

## Kenneth Arnold — "flying saucers" over Mount Rainier (1947)

- Date: 24 June 1947
- Place: Mount Rainier, Washington (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Nine thin, crescent / convex objects in echelon
- Witnesses: 1 pilot (Kenneth Arnold)
- Duration: About 2.5 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/kenneth-arnold-1947/

Private pilot Kenneth Arnold, searching for a crashed Marine C-46 in his CallAir A-2, saw nine bright objects in a chain flying south past Mount Rainier. He timed them from Rainier to Mount Adams — roughly 50 miles — in 1 minute 42 seconds, implying well over 1,200 mph. The press coverage coined "flying saucer" and began the modern UFO era.

**Explanation:** Project Blue Book listed the sighting as a mirage. Other proposals include a fireball, pelicans and reflections; none has been widely accepted.

## Rhodes photographs — Phoenix (1947)

- Date: 7 July 1947 (time approximate)
- Place: Phoenix, Arizona (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Heel-shaped disc with a hole in the centre
- Witnesses: 1 (William A. Rhodes)
- Duration: Under a minute
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/rhodes-phoenix-1947/

Amateur astronomer and inventor William Rhodes said he heard a "whoosh" like a jet, grabbed his camera and took two photographs of a heel-shaped object circling over his home. The Arizona Republic printed them on July 9, 1947. The FBI and Army counter-intelligence took the negatives, and the case became "Incident 40" in the Air Force files, one of the first UFO photographs to be studied officially.

**Explanation:** The Air Force file records that Dr. Irving Langmuir, told a thunderstorm had just passed, judged the object to be paper carried up by the wind; photographers it consulted doubted the pictures. A historian has since argued they were faked.

## Roswell debris recovery (1947)

- Date: 8 July 1947 (time approximate)
- Place: Foster homestead near Corona, New Mexico (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Tracked object event
- Evidence: Official government document or case file; Photographs; Military witnesses; Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil)
- Shape: Debris of foil, rubber, sticks and tape
- Witnesses: Rancher Mac Brazel; 509th Bomb Group officers
- Duration: —
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/roswell-1947/

Rancher W. W. "Mac" Brazel found a field of debris on the Foster ranch. On July 8, 1947, Roswell Army Air Field announced it had recovered a "flying disc"; within a day the Army re-described it as a weather balloon. Interest revived in the late 1970s, and the Air Force published two reports concluding the debris came from Project Mogul.

**Explanation:** The U.S. Air Force reports of 1994–1997 identified the debris as a Project Mogul balloon train (NYU Flight 4) launched from Alamogordo Army Air Field to listen for Soviet nuclear tests, and later "alien body" stories as conflations with 1950s dummy drops.

## Mantell UFO incident (1948)

- Date: 7 January 1948
- Place: Godman Field, Fort Knox, Kentucky (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Military witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Large bright object, "ice-cream cone" / metallic
- Witnesses: Godman tower staff, police, 4 P-51 pilots
- Duration: About 2.5 hours
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/mantell-1948/

Kentucky Highway Patrol reports of a large circular object near Maysville reached Godman Field, where tower staff saw it too. A flight of four Kentucky Air National Guard P-51 Mustangs was asked to investigate. Capt. Thomas Mantell kept climbing after his wingmen levelled off, blacked out without oxygen and died when his P-51 crashed on a farm south of Franklin.

**Explanation:** Project Blue Book (Ruppelt) concluded Mantell was most likely chasing a classified Navy Skyhook balloon, probably launched from Clinton County AFB, Ohio. Mantell climbed above 25,000 ft without oxygen and lost consciousness.

## Aztec “crashed saucer” — the story that ended in a fraud trial (1948)

- Date: 25 March 1948 (time approximate)
- Place: Hart Canyon, about 12 miles north-east of Aztec, New Mexico (as the story told it) (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Landing / trace case
- Evidence: Official government document or case file
- Shape: A disc 99 feet across with sixteen small bodies inside, according to the story
- Witnesses: None independent: the account came from Newton and GeBauer through Frank Scully
- Duration: —
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/aztec-crash-hoax-1948/

In 1949 the Variety columnist Frank Scully told his readers, and in 1950 the buyers of his best-seller Behind the Flying Saucers, that in March 1948 the military had recovered a 99-foot disc with sixteen small humanoid bodies after it landed in Hart Canyon, north-east of Aztec, New Mexico. His sources were Silas Newton, an oil promoter, and a “Dr. Gee”, Leo GeBauer, who were selling devices they said could find oil because they used technology from the saucer. In 1952 the San Francisco Chronicle reporter J. P. Cahn obtained a sample of their “saucer metal”, had it tested and found ordinary aluminium; his True magazine article exposed the scheme, and one of their victims pressed charges. Newton and GeBauer were convicted of fraud in 1953. The story was dropped for twenty years, then revived from the 1970s by writers who dated the crash to March 25, 1948; a 1950 FBI memo by Guy Hottel, about three saucers said to have been recovered in New Mexico, is often tied to it, but the FBI calls it an uninvestigated second- or third-hand claim. It belongs here as one of the first “crashed saucer” stories, and one of the few that ended in a courtroom.

**Explanation:** A hoax. The story came from two confidence men, Silas Newton and Leo GeBauer, who used it to sell “doodlebug” oil-finding devices said to be built on saucer technology. The journalist J. P. Cahn exposed it in True magazine in 1952 (their “alien metal” was ordinary aluminium), and both men were convicted of fraud in 1953. No contemporary record of a crash or a recovery exists, and the local sheriff, newspaper editor and landowners denied that anything happened.

Sources:
- [The Guy Hottel memo of March 22, 1950, from the FBI Vault (The Black Vault)](https://www.theblackvault.com/documentarchive/the-guy-hottel-memo-and-the-crashed-flying-saucers-of-new-mexico-march-22-1950/)
- [Christian Science Monitor — FBI UFO memo is the bureau’s most viewed public record (2013)](https://www.csmonitor.com/Science/2013/0327/FBI-UFO-memo-is-bureau-s-most-viewed-public-record)
- [Skeptic’s Dictionary — the Aztec crash hoax](https://www.skepdic.com/aztec.html)
- [Wikipedia — Aztec crashed saucer hoax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aztec_crashed_saucer_hoax)

## Chiles–Whitted encounter (1948)

- Date: 24 July 1948
- Place: Near Montgomery, Alabama (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Wingless cigar with two rows of glowing "windows"
- Witnesses: 2 Eastern Air Lines pilots, 1 passenger
- Duration: 10–15 seconds
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/chiles-whitted-1948/

Eastern Air Lines captain Clarence Chiles and co-pilot John Whitted, flying a DC-3 at about 5,000 ft, saw a glowing torpedo-shaped object rush past their right side and pull up into the clouds. Project Sign took the report so seriously it contributed to the "Estimate of the Situation", which General Vandenberg rejected.

**Explanation:** Project Blue Book formally attributed the sighting to a bright meteor (bolide) in 1959.

## Gorman dogfight (1948)

- Date: 1 October 1948
- Place: Fargo, North Dakota (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Small blinking ball of light
- Witnesses: P-51 pilot, Piper Cub crew, tower controller
- Duration: About 27 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/gorman-dogfight-1948/

North Dakota Air National Guard pilot George Gorman stayed aloft in his P-51 after his flight landed and saw a blinking light that no traffic accounted for. He chased it through turns and steep climbs over Hector Airport until he lost it about 25 miles south-west of Fargo. Tower controllers and a Piper Cub crew also watched the light.

**Explanation:** The Air Force concluded in 1949 that Gorman had chased a lighted weather balloon.

## Arrey, New Mexico — a theodolite track by a Skyhook balloon crew (1949)

- Date: 24 April 1949
- Place: About three miles north of Arrey, New Mexico, in the White Sands test area (United States)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Infrared or other sensor data; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: A white ellipsoid, about 2.5 times as long as it was wide, light yellow on one side
- Witnesses: Charles B. Moore, a General Mills aerologist, and four Navy enlisted men from White Sands
- Duration: About 60 seconds
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/arrey-theodolite-1949/

On the clear Sunday morning of April 24, 1949, a General Mills and Navy crew north of Arrey were releasing small pilot balloons to measure the winds before a Skyhook balloon launch. At about 10:20 the aerologist Charles B. Moore looked up from the theodolite, a surveying telescope on a graduated mount, and saw a small white ellipsoid moving fast across the sky. He swung the instrument onto it and, with a stopwatch, the crew followed it for about a minute: it was first at about 45° elevation, moved at roughly five degrees a second, dropped towards 25°, then climbed steeply and was gone. There was no sound, trail or exhaust. The Navy’s Special Devices Center sent Moore’s written report to the Chief of Naval Operations with a letter noting that the readings might indicate controlled flight; Project Grudge and later Blue Book carried the case as unidentified. Ruppelt counted it among the best sightings made at White Sands, and Moore, who later became a respected atmospheric physicist, never accepted the mirage explanation offered for it.

**Explanation:** Blue Book’s record card says “Unidentified”. A pilot balloon released about fifteen minutes later was tracked to show the object could not have been a free balloon at that angular speed. Donald Menzel later proposed a mirage of the crew’s own balloon; Moore rejected it, and the theodolite readings do not fit it well. A meteor does not fit the minute-long track without a trail.

Sources:
- [Edward Ruppelt, The Report on Unidentified Flying Objects (1956), Chapter 5 (Project Gutenberg)](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/17346)
- [The Arrey case: Moore’s report, the record card and the debate (transcribed)](https://ufology.patrickgross.org/htm/arrey49.htm)

## Clyde Tombaugh’s Las Cruces sighting (1949)

- Date: 20 August 1949 (time approximate)
- Place: Las Cruces, New Mexico (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Historical account
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Six to eight faint, bluish-green rectangles of light in a geometrical group
- Witnesses: Clyde Tombaugh, discoverer of Pluto, his wife and his mother-in-law
- Duration: About 3 seconds (his wife saw it for about 1½ seconds)
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/tombaugh-1949/

On the night of August 20, 1949, Clyde Tombaugh, who had found Pluto nineteen years earlier and was then working on missile tracking at White Sands, was sitting in his back yard in Las Cruces with his wife and mother-in-law. He saw a group of six to eight faint, bluish-green rectangles of light, in a fixed arrangement, pass overhead from the north-west and fade as they went toward the south-eastern horizon. “I was so unprepared for such a strange sight that I was really petrified with astonishment,” he wrote. He is probably the most eminent astronomer to have reported a UFO, and he went on to support the scientific study of them, while saying he could not take interstellar visitors seriously.

**Explanation:** Tombaugh never said it was a spacecraft. At the time he wrote that he doubted it was a reflection of anything on the ground, as nothing like it had appeared before or since. Later he thought the most likely cause was a reflection from an inversion layer, given how faint the lights were and how they faded as they moved away from the zenith.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — Clyde Tombaugh, UFOs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clyde_Tombaugh#UFOs)

## Farmington “armada” — a town watches discs for three days (1950)

- Date: 17 March 1950 (time approximate)
- Place: Farmington, New Mexico (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Discs, mostly silvery, darting in a “bee-like” swarm; one larger and red
- Witnesses: Hundreds of residents over three days, among them the business manager of the Farmington Daily Times and a former Navy pilot
- Duration: Mostly late morning, on three consecutive days
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/farmington-1950/

For three days in the middle of March 1950, people in Farmington, in the far north-west of New Mexico, reported flying saucers over the town, and the largest sighting, on the late morning of Friday, March 17, was watched by hundreds. The Farmington Daily Times’ front page the next day had estimates from several to more than 500 objects; one witness who tried to triangulate one put its speed at about 1,000 mph. When the physicist James McDonald interviewed seven witnesses eighteen years later, the Times business manager Clayton Boddy estimated he had seen 20 to 30 discs, including one much larger red one, and the realtor John Eaton, a former Navy pilot, put them at around 15,000 ft, darting about “like bees” and turning from flat to round as they tilted. No one reported wings or tails. McDonald checked the explanation then current, a Skyhook balloon breaking up, and found no Skyhook had been released; he told a House committee in 1968 that he saw “no ready explanation”. The case remains a mass sighting with no instrument record.

**Explanation:** The sightings were put down at the time to a Skyhook balloon breaking up, or to drifting cotton-like fluff. James McDonald found that Holloman AFB and the Office of Naval Research, which held the records of every Skyhook release, had none from anywhere in the country on or near that date, that balloon fragments 40,000 to 50,000 ft up would be invisible to the eye, and that the cotton idea came from an offhand remark by a law officer. No Air Force investigation of substance is on record.

Sources:
- [Farmington Daily Times, March 18, 1950 (transcribed)](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/press/farmingtondailytimes18mar1950.htm)
- [James E. McDonald, statement to the House Symposium on UFOs, July 29, 1968 (transcribed)](https://ufology.patrickgross.org/books/mcdonaldhcsa68lone.htm)

## McMinnville (Trent) photographs (1950)

- Date: 11 May 1950
- Place: Trent farm near Sheridan / McMinnville, Oregon (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Metallic disc with a raised "mast"
- Witnesses: Paul and Evelyn Trent
- Duration: A few minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/mcminnville-1950/

Evelyn Trent saw a metallic disc moving slowly over the farm; her husband Paul took two photographs with a box camera. The images ran in LIFE magazine and became among the most analysed UFO photos ever taken.

**Explanation:** The Condon Committee called it one of the few cases where the evidence was consistent with the witnesses’ account; skeptics (Sheaffer, Maccabee critics, later photogrammetry) argue it was a small model hung from overhead wires.

## Farnborough test pilot’s disc — the Flying Saucer Working Party (1950)

- Date: 14 August 1950 (time approximate)
- Place: Royal Aircraft Establishment, Farnborough, Hampshire (United Kingdom)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Military witnesses; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: A flat, light pearl-grey disc “like a shirt button”
- Witnesses: Flt Lt Stanley Hubbard, an RAF test pilot; about two weeks later, he and five other senior officers
- Duration: Seconds
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/farnborough-hubbard-1950/

One morning in August 1950 Flight Lieutenant Stanley Hubbard, an experienced RAF test pilot at the Royal Aircraft Establishment, saw a flat, pearl-grey disc spinning through S-turns over the airfield at what he judged to be up to 1,000 mph. About two weeks later he and five other senior officers watched a disc low in the sky towards Guildford and Farnham perform high-speed manoeuvres and a “falling leaf” motion before diving towards the horizon. The reports reached Sir Henry Tizard, the Ministry of Defence’s chief scientific adviser, who in October 1950 set up a small “Flying Saucer” Working Party to study such reports. All six officers were interviewed. The working party’s report of June 1951 explained the Farnborough sightings, and every other report it studied, as misidentified aircraft, balloons and astronomical objects, optical illusions or hoaxes. It stayed secret until it was released to the researchers David Clarke and Andy Roberts in 2001; the file is DEFE 44/119 at The National Archives.

**Explanation:** The Ministry of Defence’s Flying Saucer Working Party (report DSI/JTIC No. 7, June 1951) judged the first sighting an optical illusion, and the second, by six officers, a normal aircraft manoeuvring at extreme visual range, seen by men already influenced by the first report. It recommended that no further investigation of “mystery aerial phenomena” be undertaken.

Sources:
- [The National Archives — DEFE 44/119, Unidentified Flying Objects (DSI/JTIC Report No. 7), 1951](https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/details/r/C11001295)
- [David Clarke — The Flying Saucer Working Party](https://drdavidclarke.co.uk/secret-files/flying-saucer-working-party/)
- [Wikipedia — Flying Saucer Working Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flying_Saucer_Working_Party)

## Mariana film, Great Falls (1950)

- Date: 15 August 1950
- Place: Great Falls, Montana (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Motion-picture film; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Two bright spinning discs
- Witnesses: Nicholas Mariana and his secretary
- Duration: ~16 seconds of film
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/mariana-film-1950/

Great Falls Electrics baseball manager Nicholas Mariana filmed two bright objects crossing the sky with his 16 mm camera. The Air Force returned the film with frames missing; the case was studied by Project Blue Book, the Robertson Panel and the Condon Committee.

**Explanation:** The Air Force suggested reflections from two F-94 jets landing nearby; later analyses dispute the geometry.

## U.S. Navy R5D — object over the North Atlantic (1951)

- Date: 10 February 1951
- Place: North Atlantic, east of Newfoundland (Canada (offshore))
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Huge yellowish glow, semicircular
- Witnesses: Navy flight crew and passengers
- Duration: 7–8 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/navy-r5d-atlantic-1951/

A U.S. Navy R5D transport flying toward Newfoundland at about 10,000 ft saw a yellowish glow, like a fire, ahead and below. It rushed toward the aircraft and grew very large and bright, with a semicircular shape. Then it turned 180° and vanished over the horizon at great speed. The Air Force logged the report at 49°50′N 50°03′W. Crew member Lt. Graham Bethune later described it publicly.

**Explanation:** The Blue Book record card gives its consulting astronomer's view that the crew saw an astronomical display. The crew said it was a solid object that came up to meet them.

Sources:
- [NICAP — Navy R5D, Newfoundland (case index)](http://www.nicap.org/casework/2014indexes/jan-mar/510210newfoundland_dir.htm)

## Lubbock Lights (1951)

- Date: 30 August 1951
- Place: Lubbock, Texas (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: V / arc formation of 15–30 bluish lights
- Witnesses: Texas Tech professors, residents
- Duration: Seconds per pass; repeated over weeks
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/lubbock-lights-1951/

Starting on 25 August 1951, three Texas Tech professors saw arcs of faint lights sweep silently overhead several times. On 30–31 August, 18-year-old Carl Hart Jr. photographed a V-shaped formation of lights from his backyard.

**Explanation:** Project Blue Book’s Edward Ruppelt concluded the lights were probably plovers reflecting street lights; the photos themselves were never shown to be faked.

## Fort Monmouth radar and T-33 sighting (1951)

- Date: 10 September 1951
- Place: Fort Monmouth and the Jersey Shore, New Jersey (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Fast radar target; silver disc seen from a T-33
- Witnesses: Army radar operators; two Air Force pilots
- Duration: Two days
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/fort-monmouth-1951/

During a demonstration at the Army Signal Corps radar school at Fort Monmouth, an operator picked up a low target moving too fast for the automatic tracking. Minutes later, the crew of an Air Force T-33 over Point Pleasant reported a silver disc below them and dived after it. More radar targets followed the next day. The case alarmed the Pentagon and led the Air Force to reorganise Project Grudge, which became Project Blue Book.

**Explanation:** Blue Book's record card: "Extensive investigation revealed that the target on 10 Sept was caused by a balloon. Targets on 11 September were attributed to anomalous propagation."

Sources:
- [NICAP — The Fort Monmouth incident, 10 September 1951](http://www.nicap.org/reports/monmouth.htm)

## Long Beach — six F-86s chase an object they cannot reach (1951)

- Date: 23 September 1951
- Place: Over Long Beach, California (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses; Radar tracking; Official government document or case file
- Shape: A silver aircraft with sharply swept wings, or round and silver; orbiting slowly to the left
- Witnesses: Seven Air Force F-86 pilots and their ground controller
- Duration: About 50 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/long-beach-f86-1951/

At 7:55 a.m. on September 23, 1951, two F-86 Sabres on an early patrol, approaching Long Beach on the west leg of the radio range, saw an object high ahead, in a slow left-hand turn. The ground radar had nothing, and the controller sent them up after it, but they could not climb to it; whenever they seemed to gain, it rose a little and stayed out of reach, still circling. Running short of fuel after about ten minutes, they were relieved by four more F-86s scrambled from George AFB, which worked in pairs for another half hour to reach what they put at 50,000 to 55,000 ft, then also turned back; a seventh fighter arrived to find nothing. All but one pilot described a silver aircraft with highly swept-back wings; one said it looked round. Edwards AFB, Nellis, Inyokern and George had nothing in the air that could fly that high. Blue Book later put it down to a weather balloon; Ruppelt, who tried to make that answer fit, could not.

**Explanation:** Blue Book’s record card evaluates it as a balloon: a radiosonde released from Long Beach Municipal Airport was near the fighters’ path, and the first pair were looking almost straight at it when they first saw the object. Ruppelt, who plotted the balloon (tracked by radio fixes) against the F-86s (tracked by radar), wrote that the paths agreed only at that first moment, that the weather observers watching their balloon saw no fighters near it, and that it burst about ten minutes before the pilots lost sight of the object.

Sources:
- [Project Blue Book file, Long Beach, September 1951 (Internet Archive)](https://archive.org/details/1951-09-7009452-LongBeach-California)
- [Edward Ruppelt, The Report on Unidentified Flying Objects (1956), Chapters 7–9 (Project Gutenberg)](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/17346)

## Mitchel AFB — a Navy TBM chases a “parachute” over Long Island (1952)

- Date: 21 January 1952
- Place: Mitchel Air Force Base, Hempstead, Long Island, New York (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Dome-shaped like a parachute canopy, white with a dark underside; rocking as it flew
- Witnesses: A Navy pilot from the Special Devices Center at Port Washington, flying a TBM-3W
- Duration: About two and a half minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/mitchel-tbm-1952/

At about 9:50 a.m. on January 21, 1952, a Navy pilot who had just taken off from Mitchel AFB in a TBM Avenger saw below him, south-east of the field, what he took for the canopy of a parachute. Realising it was moving across the wind, he climbed after it as it climbed, tried to cut inside its left turn, overshot and passed over it, then dived to get behind it. It turned through 180 degrees, swung round the north side of the base gaining speed, and outran him; he last saw it crossing the coast near Freeport, heading out to sea. He put it at 200 to 300 ft over houses at first and its speed at several hundred knots by the end. The tower did not see it. Ruppelt went to New York to interview him and thought him careful and reliable; he wrote that unless the pilot was several miles from where he believed, the object could not have been the weather balloon released that morning.

**Explanation:** The base weather section launched a Rawinsonde balloon at 09:50 from south-east of the field, and Blue Book’s analysts believed the pilot saw it. Ruppelt, who interviewed him, noted that the balloon drifted south-east and never passed north of the field, where the pilot followed the object, and that it pulled away from him in a straight chase, which a balloon cannot do.

Sources:
- [Project Blue Book file, Mitchel AFB, January 1952 (Internet Archive)](https://archive.org/details/1952-01-6310148-MitchellAFB-N-Y)
- [Project Blue Book file with the balloon analysis (Internet Archive)](https://archive.org/details/1952-01-6310103-MITCHELAFB-NEWYORK)
- [Edward Ruppelt, The Report on Unidentified Flying Objects (1956), Chapter 9 (Project Gutenberg)](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/17346)

## Wonsan and Sunchon B-29 sightings (1952)

- Date: 29 January 1952 (time approximate)
- Place: Wonsan and Sunchon, North Korea
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Military witnesses; Pilot / aircrew witnesses
- Shape: Orange sphere or disc, with occasional blue flames
- Witnesses: Two B-29 crews from different squadrons
- Duration: Five minutes or more at Wonsan; about a minute at Sunchon
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/wonsan-sunchon-1952/

Around midnight on the night of January 29, 1952, during the Korean War, the rear gunner and the central fire-control gunner of a B-29 Superfortress at 20,000 feet over Wonsan saw an orange, globe-shaped light about three feet across that stayed near the bomber for five minutes or more. A second B-29 from a different squadron, hundreds of miles away at Sunchon, reported a lighted orange sphere that followed it for about a minute on the way back to base. The two reports were made independently by trained aircrew over hostile territory, and the story was widely published in February 1952. Air Force UFO experts have argued that the wide publicity it received helped feed the 1952 wave, which ended over Washington, D.C.

**Explanation:** No explanation was ever settled. Air Force Lt. Gen. Otto Weyland said that “we can’t say there’s nothing to it” but that without more data a conclusive answer could not be expected, and he doubted that jet aircraft were responsible.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — Wonsan-Sunchon UFO incident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonsan-Sunchon_UFO_incident)
- [NICAP — Korea, 29 January 1952 (case index)](http://www.nicap.org/520129wonsan_dir.htm)
- [UFOs at close sight — U.S. military reports, Korea, 29 January 1952](https://ufology.patrickgross.org/htm/korea29jan52.htm)

## Barra da Tijuca — the O Cruzeiro disc photographs (1952)

- Date: 7 May 1952 (time approximate)
- Place: Coast at Barra da Tijuca, near Pedra do Marisco, Rio de Janeiro (Brazil)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs
- Shape: A flat disc with a raised rim, seen sideways and tilted
- Witnesses: Two O Cruzeiro staff: photographer Ed Keffel and reporter João Martins
- Duration: About one minute (five frames)
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/barra-da-tijuca-1952/

On the afternoon of May 7, 1952, the reporter João Martins and the photographer Ed Keffel of the weekly magazine O Cruzeiro were on the coast at Barra da Tijuca, south of Rio, when Martins pointed out what he first took for an aircraft “flying sideways”. Keffel took five photographs with a Rolleiflex in about a minute, and the magazine published them as a flying disc. They became famous across South America, and Brazilian Air Force officers reportedly declared a hoax impossible after studying the distances. In 1963 Menzel and Boyd pointed out that the disc is lit from the opposite side to the palm and the hillside beneath it, which a single sunlit scene cannot do. William Hartmann made an independent enlargement for the Condon study (1968), found that it supported the objection, and noted that the case was offered as incontrovertible while containing “a simple, internal inconsistency”. The study never interviewed the photographers, and the case has no other witnesses.

**Explanation:** Donald Menzel and Lyle Boyd called the photographs a hoax because the disc is lit from the left while the hillside and trees below it are lit from the right; the Condon study’s own enlargement supported that objection. Brazilian Air Force analysts had said a hoax was impossible, but no independent study of the negatives was ever made and neither man admitted a fake.

Sources:
- [Condon report, case 48: Barra da Tijuca, Brazil (Project 1947 transcription)](https://www.project1947.com/shg/condon/case48.html)
- [Wikipedia — UFO sightings in Brazil (1952)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO_sightings_in_Brazil)

## Tremonton, Utah film (1952)

- Date: 2 July 1952
- Place: Near Tremonton, Utah (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Motion-picture film; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: About a dozen bright objects milling in the sky
- Witnesses: Navy Chief Warrant Officer Delbert C. Newhouse and family
- Duration: ~1 min of 16 mm Kodachrome
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/tremonton-1952/

Driving about seven miles north of Tremonton, Navy photographer Delbert Newhouse stopped and filmed a group of bright objects with his Bell & Howell 16 mm camera. The Navy’s Photographic Interpretation Laboratory spent over 1,000 man-hours on it and ruled out aircraft and birds; the Robertson Panel disagreed.

**Explanation:** Navy photo analysts could not identify the objects; the 1953 Robertson Panel suggested seagulls reflecting sunlight. The film was re-released in 2026 as PURSUE record DOW-UAP-PR159.

Sources:
- [Condon Report, case 49 — Tremonton, Utah, movie film](https://files.ncas.org/condon/text/case49.htm)
- [UFOs at close sight — the Tremonton colour film of 2 July 1952](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/htm/tremonton.htm)

## Nash–Fortenberry sighting (1952)

- Date: 14 July 1952
- Place: Chesapeake Bay near Newport News, Virginia (United States)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Eight glowing red-orange discs in echelon
- Witnesses: 2 Pan Am pilots; independent ground witnesses
- Duration: ~12 seconds
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/nash-fortenberry-1952/

Pan American pilots William Nash and William Fortenberry, flying a DC-4 at 8,000 ft toward Norfolk, saw eight glowing discs race in formation below them, flip on edge and reverse direction, then climb west out of sight. Blue Book classified the case as unknown.

**Explanation:** Listed as "unknown" by Project Blue Book. Menzel suggested haze-distorted ground lights or fireflies; others a mirage of Venus.

## Salem Coast Guard Air Station photograph (1952)

- Date: 16 July 1952
- Place: U.S. Coast Guard Air Station Salem, Winter Island, Salem, Massachusetts (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Four elliptical blobs of light in formation, with rays
- Witnesses: Shell Alpert, a Coast Guard photographer’s mate; a second Coastguardsman reportedly saw the lights
- Duration: Seconds
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/salem-coast-guard-1952/

At 9:35 a.m. on July 16, 1952, Shell Alpert, a photographer at the Coast Guard Air Station in Salem, Massachusetts, saw bright lights through the window of the station’s photo laboratory and took a single picture: four elliptical blobs of light, apparently in formation, above the parked cars. It was taken in the middle of that summer’s wave of sightings and was soon in the newspapers. Blue Book’s file, case 1501, holds sixteen photographs and a series of analyses: the first suggested a double exposure, a second that the “objects” were reflections of interior lights on the glass, a test with a photo-flood lamp showed that a real light source would also have been reflected in the cars, which these are not, and the case finished as unexplained. It is one of the best-known UFO photographs, and one of the plainest examples of how hard a single frame is to settle.

**Explanation:** Blue Book’s analysts went back and forth: a probable double exposure, then probably reflections of lights on the window glass, and in the end the case was filed as unexplained. Against the reflection idea, the parked cars in the photograph reflect the sun but not the lights, and some accounts say the window was open, with only a screen.

Sources:
- [Project Blue Book photo file 1501, Salem, July 1952 (Internet Archive)](https://archive.org/details/1952-07-7274460-Salem-Massachusetts-1501-)
- [Blue Book photo case 1501 and its analyses (transcribed)](https://ufology.patrickgross.org/htm/bluebookpics1501.htm)

## Washington, D.C. radar-visual sightings (1952)

- Date: 19 July 1952
- Place: Washington, D.C. (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file; Photographs
- Shape: Radar blips; orange-red lights
- Witnesses: Air traffic controllers, airline and fighter pilots
- Duration: Two weekends
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/washington-dc-1952/

On consecutive Saturday nights, controllers at Washington National Airport and Andrews AFB tracked unknown targets over the capital — including the prohibited airspace over the White House and Capitol — while airline pilots saw lights where radar showed them. F-94 jets scrambled from New Castle AFB, Delaware; one pilot said lights surrounded his aircraft. The Pentagon held its largest press conference since WWII.

**Explanation:** The Air Force attributed the radar returns to temperature inversions; radar controllers involved rejected that explanation. The widely published "Capitol UFO" photo shows lens flares.

## Carson Sink — two colonels in a B-25 meet three deltas (1952)

- Date: 24 July 1952
- Place: Over the Carson Sink, Nevada, on the airway to Salt Lake City (United States)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Three bright silver delta-wing craft with no tails or canopies, a ridge from nose to tail
- Witnesses: Two Air Force colonels, both command pilots stationed at the Pentagon
- Duration: Seconds
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/carson-sink-b25-1952/

On July 24, 1952, two Air Force colonels flying a B-25 from Hamilton AFB to Colorado Springs crossed the Sierra Nevada and were heading east at 11,000 ft on the airway “Green 3” towards Salt Lake City. At 3:40 p.m., over the Carson Sink, one of them saw three objects ahead and to the right that looked like F-86s in a tight V. Within seconds they were close enough to see clearly: bright silver deltas with no tails and no canopies, only a ridge running from nose to tail. The three made a slight left bank and passed the bomber within 400 to 800 yards at what the pilots put at three times the speed of an F-86. Both were command pilots with thousands of hours, whose work would have shown them anything the United States had flying; both had been sceptics. They reported it on landing, and Blue Book’s checks found no aircraft, no delta and no balloon to account for it. Ruppelt used it in his book as an example of a report that ends simply “Unknown”.

**Explanation:** Blue Book checked Flight Service records (no aircraft near), the Navy and Air Force delta-wing aircraft (none there; the Air Force’s only delta was grounded) and every weather and research balloon flight (none), and carried the case as unknown. Ruppelt’s own speculations, F-86s flying where they should not, missing records or a misjudged distance, were offered only as possibilities.

Sources:
- [Edward Ruppelt, The Report on Unidentified Flying Objects (1956), Chapter 1 (Project Gutenberg)](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/17346)

## The Florida scoutmaster — burned, and called a hoax (1952)

- Date: 19 August 1952 (time approximate)
- Place: Palmetto scrub off a back road inland from West Palm Beach, Florida (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Documented physiological effects; Police witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: A dark, round, slightly concave craft about 30 ft overhead, with a dome and vanes around the rim; a ball of red fire
- Witnesses: D. S. “Sonny” Desvergers, a scoutmaster, and three Boy Scouts in his car; a deputy sheriff and a constable afterwards
- Duration: Several minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/desvergers-scoutmaster-1952/

On the evening of August 19, 1952, Sonny Desvergers, a scoutmaster in his early thirties, was driving three scouts home along a black-top road through palmetto scrub inland from West Palm Beach when he saw lights in the pines and stopped. He told the boys to fetch help if he was not back in fifteen minutes and went into the scrub with a machete and two flashlights. By his account he came into a clearing, felt heat, and saw a dark disc about 30 ft above him; when he shone his light on it, a small ball of red fire drifted down, became a mist, and he blacked out. The scouts said they saw a red ball engulf him and ran to a farmhouse; a deputy and a constable found him coming out of the brush, badly frightened, with his forearms, face and cap lightly burned. Ruppelt flew down from Dayton the next day. The burns were like mild sunburn, which a flight surgeon could reproduce with a cigarette lighter. Blue Book found the scoutmaster’s record did not match the story he told of himself, concluded it was a hoax, and called it “the best hoax in UFO history”; but a laboratory found the roots of the grass under where the object was said to hover charred and the blades unharmed, which nobody could explain.

**Explanation:** Blue Book wrote it off as a hoax, mainly because of the scoutmaster’s record and reputation, the press agent he hired and a re-enactment showing the scouts could not have seen him fall where they said. Ruppelt, who led the investigation, admitted they could not prove a hoax and that the two pieces of physical evidence, tiny burned holes in his cap and grass roots charred as if the ground had been heated to about 300 °F from below, were never explained.

Sources:
- [Project Blue Book file 1981, West Palm Beach, August 1952 (Internet Archive)](https://archive.org/details/1952-08-7275004-WestPalmBeach-Florida-1981-)
- [Edward Ruppelt, The Report on Unidentified Flying Objects (1956), Chapter 12 (Project Gutenberg)](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/17346)
- [History.com — the Florida scoutmaster burned by a “UFO”](https://www.history.com/articles/ufo-encounter-florida-desvergers-scoutmaster-burned)

## Flatwoods "monster" (1952)

- Date: 12 September 1952
- Place: Flatwoods, Braxton County, West Virginia (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Documented physiological effects
- Shape: Bright light; tall figure with a spade-shaped hood
- Witnesses: 7 (the May brothers, Kathleen May, Eugene Lemon and others)
- Duration: Minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/flatwoods-1952/

Just after 7 p.m. three boys saw a bright light cross the sky and come down on the Fisher farm. They climbed the hill with Kathleen May, National Guardsman Eugene Lemon and two other boys. At the top they saw a pulsing red light, and in Lemon's flashlight beam a tall figure with a glowing face and a spade-shaped hood. It hissed, and they fled. Several later felt sick. A bright meteor was reported over Maryland, Pennsylvania and West Virginia that same evening.

**Explanation:** Investigator Joe Nickell concluded the light was a meteor seen over three states that evening, the pulsing red glow an aircraft beacon, and the "monster" a barn owl on a branch, magnified by fear. The witnesses' nausea fits fright and the smoke of the fire.

## RAF Topcliffe disc — Exercise Mainbrace (1952)

- Date: 19 September 1952
- Place: RAF Topcliffe / Dishforth, North Yorkshire (United Kingdom)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Military witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Silver disc, rotating
- Witnesses: Flt Lt John Kilburn and RAF aircrew on the ground
- Duration: About 20 seconds of hovering
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/topcliffe-mainbrace-1952/

During NATO's Exercise Mainbrace, RAF aircrew at Topcliffe watched a silver, disc-shaped object following a Meteor jet as it came down to land at nearby Dishforth. The object descended, swinging "like a pendulum", hovered and rotated. It then shot away westward at high speed. The report made front pages and was raised in Parliament years later.

Sources:
- [The National Archives (UK) — MoD UFO files](https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/help-with-your-research/research-guides/ufos/)

## Oloron-Sainte-Marie "angel hair" (1952)

- Date: 17 October 1952
- Place: Oloron-Sainte-Marie, Pyrénées-Atlantiques (France)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil)
- Shape: White cylinder with a train of smaller "saucers" in pairs
- Witnesses: Jean-Yves Prigent of the Oloron lycée, his family and townspeople
- Duration: About 20 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/oloron-angel-hair-1952/

Around midday, residents of Oloron-Sainte-Marie saw a cottony white cylinder tilted at 45°, drifting slowly across a nearly cloudless sky. Around it were about thirty smaller objects moving in zig-zagging pairs. Long white filaments ("angel hair") fell from them onto roofs, trees and wires, then turned to jelly and vanished. A similar event followed at Gaillac ten days later.

**Explanation:** Most researchers attribute "angel hair" falls to silk from migrating ballooning spiders, common in autumn. The Oloron filaments dissolved and no sample was analysed.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — Angel hair (folklore)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angel_hair_(folklore))

## Little Rissington Meteor encounter (1952)

- Date: 21 October 1952 (time approximate)
- Place: Over Gloucestershire from RAF Little Rissington (United Kingdom)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses; Radar tracking; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Three white, perfectly circular discs
- Witnesses: Flt Lt Michael Swiney and Lt David Crofts (Royal Navy)
- Duration: Minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/little-rissington-1952/

An instructor from the Central Flying School and a Royal Navy trainee broke through cloud at 12,000 ft in a Meteor T.7 and saw three white, circular objects far above, which they first took for parachutes. They climbed toward 35,000 ft, but the objects crossed their path from left to right and disappeared in a fraction of a second. Radar at Gloucester reported three objects, two Meteor F.8s were scrambled, and Southern Sector radar logged targets heading east at great speed.

Sources:
- [The National Archives (UK) — MoD UFO files](https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/help-with-your-research/research-guides/ufos/)

## Ellsworth AFB — the Black Hawk light and the F-84 chase (1953)

- Date: 5 August 1953
- Place: Black Hawk and Ellsworth Air Force Base, Rapid City, South Dakota; later Bismarck, North Dakota (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Military witnesses; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: A bright light, white turning green; red-to-white lights later
- Witnesses: A Ground Observer Corps volunteer, radar controllers, airmen and two F-84 pilots
- Duration: About 20:05 to 02:50 MST, on and off
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/ellsworth-1953/

At about 8:05 p.m. on August 5, 1953, a Ground Observer Corps volunteer at Black Hawk, west of Rapid City, reported a bright light to the Air Defense Command radar station at Ellsworth AFB. The controller saw blips through the ground clutter, and airmen sent outside watched a light cross from north to south. F-84 fighters on patrol were vectored onto the returns. One pilot saw only a brief, very bright light; the second climbed from 15,000 to 26,000 ft after a white light that turned green and was “considerably brighter than a star”, said it “definitely moved in relation to the stars”, and chased it for about 80 miles to the north while the controller tracked both on radar. His radar gunsight’s warning light came on, but the gun camera produced nothing usable. After midnight the Bismarck filter center, told to look for flying saucers, reported more lights. Capt. Edward Ruppelt flew to Rapid City to investigate himself; Blue Book filed the case as unsolved, and the Condon study later explained it as stars, a meteor and radar artefacts.

**Explanation:** Project Blue Book carried the case as unsolved. The Condon study (1968) attributed the Rapid City and Bismarck sightings to stars seen through a temperature inversion, at least one meteor, anomalous-propagation and ghost echoes on the ground radar, and a faulty radar gunsight in the F-84; the Blue Book investigator had suggested Capella low in the north, a balloon or a meteor.

Sources:
- [Project Blue Book file, Rapid City and Black Hawk, August 1953 (Internet Archive)](https://archive.org/details/1953-08-6979324-RapidCity-Blackhawk-SoughDakotaArea)
- [Blue Book Status Report 12 on the case (transcribed)](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/htm/ellsworth53bluebook.htm)
- [The Condon report’s summary of the case (transcribed)](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/htm/ellsworth53condon.htm)

## West Malling Vampire sighting (1953)

- Date: 3 November 1953 (time approximate)
- Place: Over RAF West Malling, Kent (United Kingdom)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Bright object
- Witnesses: RAF aircrew Terry Johnson and Geoffrey Smythe
- Duration: —
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/west-malling-1953/

Two RAF aircrew flying a de Havilland Vampire over West Malling reported an unidentified object. The report reached the House of Commons, where the Air Minister called it a weather balloon. Another MP raised it again the next day.

**Explanation:** In Parliament, the Secretary of State for Air said the object was "a weather balloon". The crew did not accept this.

Sources:
- [The National Archives (UK) — MoD UFO files](https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/help-with-your-research/research-guides/ufos/)

## Kinross F-89 disappearance over Lake Superior (1953)

- Date: 23 November 1953
- Place: Lake Superior, off the Keweenaw Peninsula, Michigan (United States)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Unidentified radar target
- Witnesses: Ground-control radar operators
- Duration: About 30 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/kinross-moncla-1953/

Air defense radar picked up an unidentified target over the restricted airspace near the Soo Locks. An F-89C Scorpion was scrambled from Kinross AFB, flown by 1st Lt. Felix Moncla with radar operator 2nd Lt. Robert Wilson. Ground controllers watched the fighter close on the target over Lake Superior at about 8,000 ft, until the two returns merged into one. The F-89 never answered again, and neither the aircraft nor its crew was ever found.

**Explanation:** The Air Force said the target was a Royal Canadian Air Force C-47 flying off course and that the F-89 probably crashed after the pilot became disoriented (vertigo). The RCAF denied any intercept took place, and no wreckage of the F-89 has ever been found.

## BOAC Stratocruiser paced by seven objects (1954)

- Date: 29 June 1954
- Place: Gulf of St. Lawrence, near Sept-Îles, Quebec (Canada)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: One large dark object and six smaller ones
- Witnesses: Captain James Howard, First Officer Lee Boyd, crew and passengers
- Duration: 18 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/boac-stratocruiser-1954/

BOAC Flight 510-196, a Boeing Stratocruiser from New York to London via Goose Bay, was cruising at 19,000 ft when the crew saw a large dark object and six smaller ones keeping pace a few miles off the port side. They held station for 18 minutes as the crew and passengers watched. Goose Bay sent up a USAF F-94. As it approached, the small objects seemed to merge into the large one, which shrank and disappeared. Captain Howard was interviewed on the BBC days later.

**Explanation:** Suggested explanations include a mirage or other optical effect in the evening sky; none has been generally accepted.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — UFO sightings in the United Kingdom (1954 BOAC entry)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO_sightings_in_the_United_Kingdom#1950s)

## The Nowra Sea Fury — two lights on the radar (1954)

- Date: 31 August 1954
- Place: South-west of Goulburn, New South Wales, on the way back to Naval Air Station Nowra (Australia)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Two very bright white lights, each on top of a large, vague dark mass
- Witnesses: Lt J. A. “Shamus” O’Farrell, RAN, the Sea Fury pilot; PO Keith Jessop on the Nowra radar; a ground witness
- Duration: Several minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/nowra-sea-fury-1954/
