On the evening of August 31, 1954, Lieutenant James O’Farrell of 723 Squadron was flying a Hawker Sea Fury home to Nowra at 220 knots after a night cross-country flight through Young, Temora and Yass. At about 7:10 p.m., south-west of Goulburn, he called Nowra and then saw a very bright light closing fast from one o’clock; it crossed ahead of him and took up station on his left, seeming to orbit. A second, similar light appeared at nine o’clock, passed about a mile in front and joined it. Close up he could make out only “a vague shape with the white light situated centrally on top”, a large dark mass with no other lights. He asked Nowra about other traffic; the radar operator, Petty Officer Keith Jessop, had two returns in company with the Sea Fury, and O’Farrell turned through 180 and then 360 degrees so that radar could pick out which return was his. The two lights re-formed and left to the north-east at great speed, and radar followed them for a while. O’Farrell landed at about 7:30 p.m., was examined by a surgeon commander and wrote a report that the Navy kept classified until 1982. J. Allen Hynek interviewed him in 1973.

**Explanation:** The Navy found no explanation. A minute paper at the Fleet Air Arm Museum records that no RAAF aircraft were nearby and that the only other aircraft in the area was a TAA Convair airliner, which does not account for two lights that crossed in front of the fighter and were painted beside it on radar. The Directorate of Naval Intelligence called the pilot “an entirely credible witness”.

Sources:
- [National Archives of Australia — Flying saucers: fact or fiction?](https://www.naa.gov.au/blog/flying-saucers-fact-or-fiction)
- [Bill Chalker — The “Sea Fury” encounter](https://www.project1947.com/forum/bcoz2.htm)
- [Ulladulla Times — Nowra had its own alleged UFO sighting](https://www.ulladullatimes.com.au/story/8295105/odd-history-nowra-had-its-own-alleged-ufo-sighting/)

## Quarouble railway encounter — Marius Dewilde (1954)

- Date: 10 September 1954
- Place: Quarouble, near Valenciennes, Nord, France
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Landing / trace case
- Evidence: Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil)
- Shape: Dark mass on the railway with two or more small figures
- Witnesses: Marius Dewilde, a 34-year-old metalworker
- Duration: Minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/quarouble-1954/

On the night of September 10, 1954, Marius Dewilde, living beside a level crossing on the Saint-Amand–Blanc-Misseron line, went into his yard after his dog barked. He saw a dark mass on the tracks and two small figures, about a metre tall with large heads like glass helmets, heading for it. When he approached, a bright light left him unable to move; the object rose and vanished to the west. Air police inspectors found symmetrical dents in the wooden sleepers at five places and displaced ballast, and one of them said the marks might fit landing struts. It became one of the best-known cases of the 1954 wave of sightings in France.

**Explanation:** The marks on the sleepers were real, and an investigator thought they could be landing struts. But there was one witness, who had suffered a head injury the year before and later had nervous disorders, and the air police and gendarmes found no footprints or other proof.

Sources:
- [UFOs at close sight — the 1954 French flap, Quarouble, 10 September](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/1954/10sep1954quarouble.htm)

## Salandin near-miss over Southend (1954)

- Date: 14 October 1954
- Place: Over Southend-on-Sea, Essex (United Kingdom)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses
- Shape: Two circular objects, one silver and one gold
- Witnesses: 1 (Flt Lt James Salandin, No. 604 Squadron)
- Duration: Seconds
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/salandin-1954/

Flt Lt James Salandin of the Royal Auxiliary Air Force was climbing through 16,000 ft over Southend in a Meteor F.8 from North Weald when two circular objects, one silver and one gold, came toward him. The silver one came head-on, filling his windscreen, and he only narrowly avoided a collision. He reported it on landing.

Sources:
- [The National Archives (UK) — MoD UFO files](https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/help-with-your-research/research-guides/ufos/)
- [Wikipedia — UFO sightings in the United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO_sightings_in_the_United_Kingdom)

## Gravataí Air Base — the Brazilian Air Force communiqué (1954)

- Date: 24 October 1954
- Place: Gravataí Air Base (today Canoas Air Force Base), near Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul (Brazil)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Military witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Circular objects of a dull silvery colour, moving erratically
- Witnesses: Air Force officers, sergeants and soldiers at the base, and civilians
- Duration: About two hours
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/gravatai-1954/

Between about 1 and 3 p.m. on October 24, 1954, officers, sergeants and soldiers at the Brazilian Air Force base then called Gravataí, near Porto Alegre, watched circular, dull-silver objects over the base. Two days later the base command issued a communiqué: the objects’ speed and height could not be measured but were far beyond those of anything known, their course was erratic and they returned to earlier positions, they could not be confused with known celestial bodies, and no weather balloons were in the area. The base reported to the Air Force general command, asked for an investigation and invited civilians to send in their own reports, while its commander forbade staff to talk to the press until experts had studied the evidence. On November 16, 1954, Brigadier Gervásio Duncan released summaries of five of sixteen reports selected by the Air Force, two of them about Gravataí, and declined to speculate on what the objects were beyond saying that the observers were well qualified. No explanation was published; the communiqué survives through contemporary press reports collected by the Brazilian researcher Olavo Fontes.

Sources:
- [Olavo Fontes in Flying Saucer Review, May 1956 — the Gravataí communiqué (Project 1947 transcription)](https://www.project1947.com/articles/fontes_fsrmay56.htm)
- [Canoas Air Force Base (formerly Gravataí Air Base) — Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canoas_Air_Force_Base)

## Florence stadium sighting (1954)

- Date: 27 October 1954
- Place: Stadio Comunale (Artemio Franchi), Florence (Italy)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil)
- Shape: Egg- or cigar-shaped objects; falling silvery filaments
- Witnesses: About 10,000 spectators and the players
- Duration: A few minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/florence-stadium-1954/

During a match between Fiorentina and Pistoiese, the crowd and players stopped to stare at objects crossing the sky over the stadium. Witnesses described slow-moving "eggs" or fast "cigars" that stopped dead. Silvery filaments drifted down onto the ground and dissolved when touched. The same day two shining objects were reported over Venice, and sightings followed across Tuscany.

**Explanation:** Proposed explanations include migrating spiders' silk (angel hair) catching the sunlight. A sample analysed by University of Florence chemists was reported to contain boron, silicon, calcium and magnesium, which does not fit spider silk. The sample was not preserved.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — UFO sightings in Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO_sightings_in_Italy)

## Kelly–Hopkinsville encounter (1955)

- Date: 21 August 1955
- Place: Sutton farm, Kelly, Kentucky (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Light in the sky; small, glowing "goblins"
- Witnesses: 11 members of the Sutton and Lankford households
- Duration: About 10 hours
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/kelly-hopkinsville-1955/

Around 7 p.m. Billy Ray Taylor said he saw a bright light land in a gully behind the Sutton farmhouse. Over the next hours the family reported small, silvery creatures with large eyes and ears approaching the house, and they fired guns at them repeatedly. At about 11 p.m. they drove to the Hopkinsville police. Officers found bullet holes but nothing else. The family said the creatures came back after the police left.

**Explanation:** Project Blue Book listed the case as a hoax. Investigators have since suggested great horned owls, which defend their nests aggressively at night and have eyes that shine in torchlight, seen by frightened people after a meteor passed overhead.

## Lakenheath–Bentwaters radar-visual case (1956)

- Date: 13 August 1956
- Place: RAF Bentwaters & RAF Lakenheath, Suffolk (United Kingdom)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Fast radar targets; luminous objects
- Witnesses: USAF radar operators and ground crew; RAF Venom crews
- Duration: About 6 hours
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/lakenheath-bentwaters-1956/

Radar at USAF-run RAF Bentwaters tracked targets at thousands of miles per hour coming in from the sea. Lakenheath’s ground personnel then saw luminous objects, and RAF de Havilland Venom night fighters were scrambled. One pilot reported locking on before the target appeared behind him; radar showed it following the fighter.

**Explanation:** The Condon Report judged "the probability that at least one genuine UFO was involved appears to be fairly high"; others propose anomalous radar propagation, meteors and stars.

## West Freugh radar incident (1957)

- Date: 4 April 1957 (time approximate)
- Place: RAF West Freugh, near Stranraer, Scotland (United Kingdom)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Radar echo "as large as a ship"
- Witnesses: Radar operators at West Freugh and Ardwell
- Duration: About 30 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/west-freugh-1957/

Radar at West Freugh tracked a very large target hanging almost stationary at about 50,000 ft over the Irish Sea for ten minutes. It then rose vertically to about 70,000 ft and moved off. A second radar at Ardwell tracked it too. Operators said it made a turn no aircraft could make and gave an echo bigger than a normal aircraft, like a ship.

Sources:
- [The National Archives (UK) — MoD UFO files](https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/help-with-your-research/research-guides/ufos/)
- [Wikipedia — UFO sightings in the United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO_sightings_in_the_United_Kingdom)

## Milton Torres — ordered to fire on a UFO (1957)

- Date: 20 May 1957 (time approximate)
- Place: Over East Anglia, from RAF Manston (United Kingdom)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Radar return the size of an aircraft carrier
- Witnesses: 1 (Lt Milton Torres, USAF); ground-control radar
- Duration: Minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/milton-torres-1957/

Lt Milton Torres, a USAF F-86D pilot at RAF Manston, was scrambled after ground radar tracked a large target over East Anglia. He was ordered to fire a full salvo of 24 rockets at it and got a radar lock at 32,000 ft. He said the return was as big as an aircraft carrier. Before he could fire, it accelerated off his scope at an estimated Mach 10 or more. He said a man in civilian clothes later warned him not to talk. His account was published in the UK National Archives UFO files in 2008.

**Explanation:** One suggestion is that the target was a radar-spoofing test by U.S. electronic-warfare units (Project Palladium). This has not been confirmed, and the MoD found no record of the incident.

Sources:
- [The National Archives (UK) — MoD UFO files](https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/help-with-your-research/research-guides/ufos/)

## Marfa lights (1957)

- Date: 1 July 1957 (time approximate)
- Place: Mitchell Flat, east of Marfa, Texas (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Recurring lights
- Evidence: Video / film footage; Photographs; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Glowing orbs that split, merge and drift
- Witnesses: Visitors to the viewing area, nightly
- Duration: Recurring
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/marfa-lights/

Lights seen on the desert toward the Chinati Mountains, south-west of the Marfa Lights Viewing Area on U.S. 90, are said to bob, split, merge and change colour. Local lore traces them to a cowhand in 1883, but the first published account is a 1957 Coronet magazine article. The town now promotes them to tourists.

**Explanation:** Observers from the University of Texas at Dallas (2004) and a study over 2000–2008 concluded that most lights are car headlights on U.S. 67, distorted by layers of warm and cool desert air, along with ranch lights and campfires.

## RB-47 radar–ECM–visual encounter (1957)

- Date: 17 July 1957
- Place: Gulf Coast to Oklahoma (United States)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Infrared or other sensor data; Military witnesses; Pilot / aircrew witnesses
- Shape: Intense white / red light; 2.8–3 GHz radar-like signal
- Witnesses: 6-man USAF RB-47H crew; ground radar operators
- Duration: Over 1 hour, ~700 miles
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/rb-47-1957/

An RB-47H electronic-reconnaissance jet of the 55th Strategic Reconnaissance Wing was paced across Mississippi, Louisiana and Texas by a source seen visually by the pilots, detected by the ECM operators’ direction-finding gear, and painted by ground radar at the same position. The source blinked off on all three channels at once, then reappeared.

**Explanation:** Condon Report Case 5 concluded the crew’s recollections were "not adequate to allow identification"; skeptics have proposed a mix of airliner lights and ground radar. Physicist James McDonald considered it among the strongest cases.

Sources:
- [Condon Report — Case 5](https://files.ncas.org/condon/text/case05.htm)
- [J. E. McDonald — the 1957 Gulf Coast RB-47 incident (1970)](http://kirkmcd.princeton.edu/JEMcDonald/mcdonald_fsr_16_3_2_70.pdf)

## Portuguese Air Force F-84s — the Lemos Ferreira sighting (1957)

- Date: 4 September 1957 (time approximate)
- Place: Over the Portuguese–Spanish border region, returning to Ota air base (Portugal)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: A yellowish sphere that swelled and shrank, turned red and “sausage-shaped”, and released four smaller yellow spheres
- Witnesses: Capt. José Lemos Ferreira and the pilots of three other F-84G Thunderjets
- Duration: About 35 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/portugal-f84-1957/

On the night of September 4, 1957, four Portuguese Air Force F-84G Thunderjets from Ota were on a night navigation exercise into Spain, led by Capt. José Lemos Ferreira, who later became Chief of Staff of the Air Force (1977–1984). At about 9,000 m the pilots saw a yellowish sphere just above the horizon that “was not a star, a planet or a comet”; it grew and shrank, “in seconds, turning from a billiard ball into a basketball”, became intense red and elongated, and four smaller yellow spheres separated from it and took up positions around it. When one pilot felt the objects were closing on them fast, the formation broke up; when it re-formed, nothing was visible. The pilots wrote a joint report, which Ferreira believed was passed to NATO; it has not been published. Accounts disagree on the route (towards Córdoba and Cáceres, or back from Granada over Portalegre and Coruche). Ferreira, who never offered an explanation, noted that hunters near Coruche saw “a dance of lights” at the same time, and that the Coimbra geophysical institute recorded magnetic disturbances.

Sources:
- [RTP / Lusa — General Lemos Ferreira recalls the encounter 50 years later (in Portuguese)](https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/pais/general-lemos-ferreira-recorda-encontro-nos-ceus-50-anos-depois_n46796)
- [Sábado — José Lemos Ferreira, the general who swore he saw a UFO, has died (in Portuguese)](https://www.sabado.pt/vida/detalhe/morreu-jose-lemos-ferreira-o-general-que-jurou-ter-visto-um-ovni)

## Ubatuba magnesium fragments (1957)

- Date: 14 September 1957 (time approximate)
- Place: Ubatuba, São Paulo, Brazil
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Landing / trace case
- Evidence: Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Official government document or case file
- Shape: Disc that exploded over the sea (as told)
- Witnesses: A fisherman and friends (reported in a letter)
- Duration: Seconds
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/ubatuba-1957/

On September 14, 1957 the Rio de Janeiro columnist Ibrahim Sued printed a letter, with three small pieces of white metal, from a reader who said he had watched a disc explode over the sea near Ubatuba and had picked up fragments. A laboratory of Brazil’s Ministry of Agriculture and a second spectrographic analysis found the metal to be extremely pure magnesium. Ufologists, among them James Harder, argued that purity that high was hard to make at the time; later analyses of the isotopes gave normal Earth ratios, and the origin of the pieces remains unproven.

**Explanation:** The fragments are real and were analysed, but the story of their origin rests on a letter from an unnamed reader. Later isotope analyses found ordinary terrestrial magnesium, and sceptics regard the tale as a hoax.

Sources:
- [UFO Evidence — The Ubatuba, Brazil fragments](http://www.ufoevidence.org/cases/case829.htm)

## Antônio Vilas-Boas abduction claim (1957)

- Date: 16 October 1957 (time approximate)
- Place: São Francisco de Sales, Minas Gerais, Brazil
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Documented physiological effects
- Shape: Circular or egg-shaped craft with a rotating cupola
- Witnesses: Antônio Vilas-Boas, a 23-year-old farmer (the only witness)
- Duration: About four hours (as told)
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/vilas-boas-1957/

Antônio Vilas-Boas, a farmer working at night in a field, said that on the night of October 15–16, 1957 a circular craft landed near him and that five-foot beings in grey coveralls seized him, took him aboard, took blood from his chin and exposed him to an unknown gas. He also described a sexual encounter with a female being, and said the whole episode lasted about four hours. In February 1958 Dr. Olavo Fontes of Brazil’s National School of Medicine examined him and concluded he had been exposed to a large dose of radiation, with mild radiation sickness: pains, nausea, headaches, loss of appetite and skin lesions that appeared over the following months. It is often cited as one of the earliest well-known abduction stories, and it is widely doubted.

**Explanation:** It is one account by one man, first told months afterwards. The researcher Peter Rogerson doubts it, noting that a similar story ran in the magazine O Cruzeiro in November 1957, before Vilas-Boas first reported his, and arguing that he may have borrowed details from it and from the contactee George Adamski.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — Antônio Vilas-Boas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B4nio_Vilas-Boas)

## Levelland vehicle-stopping reports (1957)

- Date: 2 November 1957
- Place: Levelland, Texas (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Police witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Reported electromagnetic effects (engines, instruments); Official government document or case file
- Shape: Glowing egg-shaped object, 100–200 ft
- Witnesses: 15+ motorists, sheriff, fire chief
- Duration: About 3 hours
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/levelland-1957/

Over roughly three hours, motorists on several highways around Levelland independently reported a glowing, egg-shaped object on or over the road; each said their engine and headlights died until it left. Sheriff Weir Clem and Fire Chief Ray Jones saw lights as well.

**Explanation:** Project Blue Book attributed the reports to ball lightning / an electrical storm; weather records showed drizzle but little lightning.

## White Sands military police patrols (1957)

- Date: 3 November 1957
- Place: White Sands Proving Ground (up-range), New Mexico (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Reddish-orange, egg-shaped light
- Witnesses: Two U.S. Army military police patrols
- Duration: 3 to 25 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/white-sands-patrols-1957/

Hours after the Soviet Union launched Sputnik 2, and on the same night as the Levelland sightings in Texas, two Army MP patrols in jeeps reported lights up-range. At about 2:30 a.m. the first saw a brilliant, reddish-orange egg-shaped light hover for about three minutes, then descend and disappear. That evening a second patrol saw a glowing object that climbed until it looked like a star. The reports reached the newspapers during the November 1957 wave. Air Force investigators found the young soldiers had talked over their sightings before reporting them.

**Explanation:** Project Blue Book concluded the first patrol saw the half-full Moon through broken cloud, with the drifting cloud creating the apparent motion, and the second saw Venus, then near its greatest brilliance.

Sources:
- [NICAP — White Sands, 3 November 1957 (case index)](http://www.nicap.org/571103whitesands_dir.htm)

## Fort Itaipu sentries burned (1957)

- Date: 4 November 1957
- Place: Fort Itaipu, Praia Grande, São Paulo (Brazil)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Military witnesses; Documented physiological effects; Reported electromagnetic effects (engines, instruments)
- Shape: Bright orange light descending from the sky
- Witnesses: 2 sentries; garrison woken by the power failure
- Duration: About 3 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/itaipu-fort-1957/

In the early hours, the day after Sputnik 2, two sentries at the coastal Fort Itaipu saw a bright orange light descend and stop above the fort. They said a wave of intense heat followed and both collapsed with burns. The fort's electricity failed, including the emergency circuits. Brazilian military investigators interviewed the soldiers, and American officials were reported to have joined them.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — UFO sightings in Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO_sightings_in_Brazil)

## Kirtland Air Force Base tower sighting (1957)

- Date: 4 November 1957
- Place: Kirtland Air Force Base, New Mexico (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Egg-shaped object, 15–20 ft tall, with a single white light at its base
- Witnesses: CAA tower controllers R. M. Kaser and E. G. Brink
- Duration: About a minute in view; about 20 minutes on radar
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/kirtland-1957/

At about 10:45 p.m. on November 4, 1957, in the week of the Levelland sightings, two Civil Aeronautics Administration controllers in the tower at Kirtland AFB saw a white light cross the airfield eastward. A dark object then came down steeply near the end of runway 26 and crossed the field a few tens of feet up. Through binoculars it looked egg-shaped, 15 to 20 feet tall, with one white light at its base. It hovered within 3,000 feet of the tower for up to a minute, moved east to the base boundary and climbed fast into the overcast. Albuquerque Radar Approach Control tracked a target that turned south, circled near the low-frequency range station, hovered over the outer marker, then followed a departing C-46 for about 14 miles before returning to the marker and fading. Radar contact lasted about 20 minutes.

**Explanation:** Capt. Shere of Ent AFB, who interviewed the controllers for Project Blue Book, found nothing a small private aircraft could not do and concluded that was what they saw; the radar returns matched a small plane. The Condon Report agreed, suggesting a pilot who had strayed onto the military field by mistake. The physicist James McDonald, who later spoke to the controllers, said they found the explanation amusing.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — Kirtland AFB UFO sighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirtland_AFB_UFO_sighting)
- [NICAP — Kirtland AFB, November 4, 1957 (case index)](https://www.nicap.org/kirtland57dir.htm)

## Coast Guard cutter Sebago — radar contacts in the Gulf of Mexico (1957)

- Date: 5 November 1957
- Place: USCGC Sebago, about 200 miles south of the mouth of the Mississippi, Gulf of Mexico (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Radar targets; one brilliant light “like a planet” crossing for three seconds
- Witnesses: The cutter’s radar operators and four men on deck
- Duration: 27 minutes on radar; the light three seconds
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/sebago-1957/

At 5:10 a.m. on November 5, 1957, during the wave of sightings that followed Levelland and the launch of Sputnik 2, the Coast Guard cutter Sebago was steaming north about 200 miles south of the mouth of the Mississippi when its radar picked up a target 14 miles off, moving north to south. Over the next 27 minutes the log records a string of contacts: one closing to two miles and passing up the port side, then lost, others at 22 and 55 miles, one stationary at seven miles, and the last at 175 miles. At 5:21 four men on deck saw a brilliant light, like a planet, cross part of the sky to the north-west for three seconds. The navigator’s estimates of the target’s speed, from 1,000 to 3,300 mph, made the papers, which described one object circling the ship. Blue Book and later the Condon study treated the light as a meteor and the radar targets as unrelated echoes.

**Explanation:** Blue Book evaluated the radar contacts as false targets from anomalous propagation and the visual sighting as a meteor. The Condon study’s radar analyst agreed that the visual object was a meteor and the echoes most likely anomalous propagation, with the first target possibly an aircraft. The news reports of a single craft circling the ship were built from separate, unrelated contacts.

Sources:
- [Project Blue Book file, Gulf of Mexico, 5 November 1957 (Internet Archive)](https://archive.org/details/1957-11-7230993-Approx200MisouthofNewOrleans-Louisiana)
- [Washington Post, November 7, 1957 (transcribed)](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/press/washingtonpost7nov1957.htm)
- [SUNlite review of the Sebago case (German translation)](https://www.hjkc.de/_blog/9425-ufo-forschung-unzureichende-informationen-in-nicap-dokument-als-ufo-beweis-teil-31/)

## Trindade Island photographs (1958)

- Date: 16 January 1958
- Place: Trindade Island, South Atlantic (Brazil)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Saturn-like disc with a ring
- Witnesses: Crew and scientists aboard the Almirante Saldanha
- Duration: Under a minute
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/trindade-1958/

As the Navy survey ship Almirante Saldanha prepared to leave Trindade during the International Geophysical Year, people on deck saw a ringed disc approach from the east, pass over Desejado Peak, turn sharply and leave to the north-west. Photographer Almiro Baraúna took four frames; President Kubitschek allowed their release.

**Explanation:** The Brazilian Navy examined the negatives and did not declare a hoax; skeptics argue photographer Almiro Baraúna faked them.

## American Airlines Captain Peter Killian’s three lights (1959)

- Date: 24 February 1959 (time approximate)
- Place: Over central and northern Pennsylvania, between Philipsburg and Bradford (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Three bright lights in a line, changing from yellow to orange, sometimes in the spacing of Orion’s belt
- Witnesses: Capt. Peter Killian and his crew, stewardesses and passengers; the crews of two other American Airlines and two United Airlines flights
- Duration: About 40 to 45 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/killian-1959/

On the evening of February 24, 1959, Capt. Peter Killian, a pilot with 20,000 hours, was flying an American Airlines DC-6 from Newark to Detroit by way of Philipsburg, Bradford and Erie when he noticed three bright lights in a line off the left side of the airliner, to the south. At first he took them for the belt of Orion, then saw Orion as well. For about 45 minutes the lights stayed with the DC-6, changing colour and brightness, sometimes coming forward and sometimes falling back. Killian called two other American Airlines captains on the radio, who said they saw the lights too, and two United Airlines crews reported them in the same area; passengers and stewardesses watched. Killian filed a CIRVIS report and told the press the next day. The Air Force first mentioned Orion and then, in March, concluded that the crew had seen three B-47 bombers refuelling at night from a KC-97 tanker, a formation of lights that can last over an hour. Killian rejected it, and the case became a long-running argument between NICAP and the Air Force.

**Explanation:** The Air Force first mentioned the belt of Orion, then concluded that the crew had watched three B-47s refuelling at night from KC-97 tankers, which its records placed in the area flying east to west at about 17,000 ft and 210 knots. Critics, among them NICAP and later Brad Sparks, argued that the timing and geometry do not match and that a military transport saw the lights well to the south.

Sources:
- [Project Blue Book file, Pennsylvania, February 1959 (Internet Archive)](https://archive.org/details/1959-02-9079193-Pennsylvania)
- [New York Times, February 26, 1959 (transcribed)](https://ufology.patrickgross.org/press/nyt26fev1959.htm)
- [The Killian case: accounts and the Air Force’s answers (transcribed)](https://ufology.patrickgross.org/htm/killian59.htm)

## Father Gill’s sightings at Boianai (1959)

- Date: 26 June 1959
- Place: Boianai Mission, Papua (Papua New Guinea)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Disc with figures on top; bright lights
- Witnesses: Rev. William Booth Gill and some 38 others, most of them villagers
- Duration: Hours, over two nights
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/boianai-1959/

On the evening of June 26, 1959 the Anglican missionary William Booth Gill saw a bright white light to the north-west of the Boianai Mission. About 38 other people, mostly staff and villagers of the mission, joined him as a large disc appeared above the station, with four figures seen moving on top of it. Gill waved and, he said, the figures waved back. The sightings continued the next night. Gill wrote a report signed by 25 witnesses, and the case was studied by the Royal Australian Air Force and by J. Allen Hynek, who counted it among the best close encounters of the third kind of its time.

**Explanation:** Sceptics, among them Donald Menzel, identified the first bright light as Venus and later lights as other celestial objects. Several witnesses and Gill’s own written report, signed by 25 of them, describe more than a distant light.

Sources:
- [UFOs at close sight — Father Gill, Papua New Guinea, 1959](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/htm/papua59report.htm)

## Redmond, Oregon — an FAA station reports a hovering light (1959)

- Date: 24 September 1959 (time approximate)
- Place: Redmond Airport, Redmond, Oregon (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Police witnesses; Radar tracking; Official government document or case file
- Shape: A bright, round, flat light that changed from white to reddish-orange, with tongues of red, yellow and green light
- Witnesses: Patrolman Robert Dickerson of the Redmond police; FAA flight service specialists at the airport
- Duration: Minutes in sight; the radar reports lasted about two hours
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/redmond-1959/

Before dawn on September 24, 1959, a Redmond police officer, Robert Dickerson, saw what he first took for a falling meteor stop and hover a few hundred feet up north of the airport. FAA staff at the Redmond flight service station watched it move off to the north-east, project “long tongues of red, yellow and green light”, and, when a fast aircraft approached, rise into the clouds, then reappear to the south. The station reported it to Seattle Air Route Traffic Control Center at 1310 GMT; Seattle’s log said the Klamath Falls ground-controlled intercept radar had it, and F-102s were scrambled from Portland. Seattle later passed on radar reports of an object 25 miles from Redmond at altitudes up to 52,000 ft. The FAA’s logged account, sent to NICAP, made the case famous; the Air Force’s answers changed from a balloon to insufficient data to Venus, and in 1960 Blue Book concluded that the light was Venus and that no radar track had been confirmed.

**Explanation:** The Air Force first called it a balloon, then said there was insufficient information, and in 1960 Blue Book concluded that the light was the planet Venus, very bright and low in the east, distorted by refraction, possibly with Regulus. It found no evidence that the Klamath Falls radar had tracked it or that the fighters had seen anything, and a later review suggests the radar return was a false target over a gap-filler site during a temperature inversion. NICAP held that the FAA log shows radar contact and an attempted intercept.

Sources:
- [Project Blue Book file, Redmond, September 1959 (Internet Archive)](https://archive.org/details/1959-09-6958382-Redmond-Oregon)
- [FAA Redmond Communication Station letter, January 15, 1960 (transcribed)](https://ufology.patrickgross.org/htm/redmond59faaletter.htm)
- [A review of the Redmond case: Venus and a false radar target (German translation)](https://www.hjkc.de/_blog/25464-ufo-forschung-weeding-out-the-weinstein-catalog-september-24-1959-redmond-oregon1/)

## Red Bluff — California Highway Patrol sighting (1960)

- Date: 13 August 1960
- Place: Red Bluff area, Tehama County, California (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Recurring lights
- Evidence: Police witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file; Reported electromagnetic effects (engines, instruments)
- Shape: Football-shaped object with red lights at each end
- Witnesses: CHP officers Charles Carson and Stanley Scott; sheriff's deputies
- Duration: More than 2 hours
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/red-bluff-1960/

Two California Highway Patrol officers thought they were about to see an airliner crash when a large object dropped toward the road ahead of them. At about 100–200 ft it stopped, reversed and climbed. They watched it for more than two hours as it moved about the sky, swept a red beam over the area and caused radio interference. Deputies at the Tehama County sheriff's office also saw lights. Similar reports came from across northern California that week.

**Explanation:** The Air Force concluded the Red Bluff sightings were due to atmospheric refraction, most probably of the planet Mars rising, with a strong temperature inversion and a layer of forest-fire smoke adding to the effect.

Sources:
- [NICAP — Red Bluff, 13 August 1960](https://www.nicap.org/600813.htm)
- [UFOs at close sight — the Red Bluff case, August 1960](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/htm/clarb60.htm)

## Betty and Barney Hill (1961)

- Date: 19 September 1961
- Place: U.S. Route 3, Franconia Notch to Indian Head, New Hampshire (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Pancake-shaped craft with windows and lights
- Witnesses: 2 (Betty and Barney Hill)
- Duration: Sighting ~1 hour; about 2 hours unaccounted for
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/hill-abduction-1961/

Driving home to Portsmouth from Montreal, the Hills saw a light moving near the Moon south of Lancaster. It followed them through Franconia Notch, passing near the Cannon Mountain tramway. South of Indian Head it came down to about 100 ft over the road, and Barney saw figures at the windows through binoculars. They reached home around dawn, about two hours later than expected. Under hypnosis in 1964 both described being taken aboard, in the first widely publicised "alien abduction".

**Explanation:** The Air Force file notes that Jupiter was low in the south-west and would have set about when the object disappeared, and that there was a strong temperature inversion. The abduction story emerged only under hypnosis in 1964. The psychiatrist, Dr. Benjamin Simon, believed it was a fantasy that grew out of Betty's dreams.

## Bahía Blanca and Espora air base sightings (1962)

- Date: 11 May 1962 (time approximate)
- Place: Bahía Blanca and Espora Naval Air Base (Argentina)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs; Military witnesses; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Lighted "railroad car"; ball of light
- Witnesses: Base personnel, truck drivers, a newspaper photographer
- Duration: Two weeks
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/bahia-blanca-1962/

In May 1962 objects were reported at the Espora naval air base on May 11 and 18. On May 12, three truck drivers on Route 35 said an illuminated object like a railway carriage rose from a field, crossed the road at about 4 m and split in two. On May 21, La Nueva Provincia photographer Miguel Tohmé photographed an object over the city, and the photo made the front page. Sightings at the Puerto Belgrano naval base followed.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — UFO sightings in Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO_sightings_in_Argentina)

## Trancas — lights over the Moreno farm (1963)

- Date: 21 October 1963 (time approximate)
- Place: Finca of the Moreno family beside the Belgrano railway, Trancas, Tucumán (Argentina)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Official government document or case file
- Shape: Several luminous objects, some over the railway line and one near the gate; a beam of light that turned violet
- Witnesses: The sisters Argentina and Yolie Moreno, the house worker Dora Martínez Guzmán, and others in the household
- Duration: About 40 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/trancas-1963/

At about 10 p.m. on October 21, 1963, the women of the Moreno family at their farm near Trancas, in Tucumán, saw several bright lights over the Belgrano railway line beside the property and one close to the gate. A beam from one was turned on them; it changed from white to violet, surrounded by a fog, and they felt intense heat. Figures seemed to move around the lights on the tracks. After about forty minutes the lights left in formation towards the Medina hills. The police report described a white mist with a strong smell of sulphur lasting forty minutes, and small white balls and a powder found by the tracks were later analysed as mostly calcium carbonate. The case was widely reported at the time and is one of the classic Argentine close encounters. Later local accounts add burns to the worker’s face and arm and bare ground where nothing grew; these are not in the contemporary record. La Gaceta notes that soldiers from Tucumán regiments were being moved along those tracks for exercises at the time, which could account for figures seen walking there; nobody has explained the lights.

Sources:
- [La Gaceta (Tucumán) — Caso Trancas: the last living witness remembers (2023)](https://www.lagaceta.com.ar/nota/1010882/sociedad/caso-trancas-unica-testigo-viva-recuerda-ovnis.html)
- [La Liberté de l’Est, 25 October 1963 (transcribed)](https://ufology.patrickgross.org/press/lalibertedelest25oct1963.htm)
- [Contexto Tucumán — Caso Trancas](https://www.contextotucuman.com/nota/361770/caso-trancas-uno-de-los-eventos-ovni-mas-famosos-en-el-mundo-sucedio-en-tucuman-en-1963.html)

## Socorro landing (Lonnie Zamora) (1964)

- Date: 24 April 1964
- Place: Socorro, New Mexico (United States)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Landing / trace case
- Evidence: Police witnesses; Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Official government document or case file
- Shape: Shiny egg / "O" shape on legs; red insignia
- Witnesses: Police Sgt. Lonnie Zamora
- Duration: A few minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/socorro-zamora-1964/

Chasing a speeder south of Socorro, Sgt. Lonnie Zamora heard a roar and saw flame, drove toward it and saw a whitish oval object in a gully with two small figures in white beside it. The object rose on a blue-orange flame and left. Investigators found scorched brush and four depressions.

**Explanation:** Project Blue Book listed the case as "unknown" — one of its best-known. Proposed explanations include a lunar-lander test and a student hoax; none is confirmed.

## The Solway Firth “spaceman” photograph (1964)

- Date: 23 May 1964 (time approximate)
- Place: Burgh Marsh, near Burgh by Sands, Cumberland (United Kingdom)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs
- Shape: A tall white figure in what looks like a space suit and helmet, behind the child
- Witnesses: Jim Templeton, a Carlisle fireman and photographer, his wife and their five-year-old daughter
- Duration: One photograph in a sequence of three
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/solway-firth-spaceman-1964/

On May 23, 1964, Jim Templeton photographed his five-year-old daughter Elizabeth sitting on Burgh Marsh, overlooking the Solway Firth. He said that no one else was in sight, but when the film came back the middle of three frames showed a tall white figure apparently in a space suit standing behind her. Kodak said the picture had not been tampered with, the Carlisle police found nothing suspicious, and the photograph went round the world. Templeton later told of two men claiming to be from the government who quizzed him at the marsh, and repeated a story that a Blue Streak launch at Woomera had been stopped by two similar figures. In 2014 David Clarke proposed the explanation now generally given: Templeton’s wife had walked into the background, her back to the camera, outside the part of the scene the viewfinder showed, and the overexposed blue dress turned white.

**Explanation:** In 2014 the researcher David Clarke concluded that the “spaceman” is most likely Templeton’s wife, Annie, who was there that day: seen from behind, her pale blue dress overexposed to white, standing beyond what the camera’s viewfinder showed. Darkened and straightened, the figure looks like a person seen from the back.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — Solway Firth Spaceman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solway_Firth_Spaceman)

## Big Sur — Atlas "Buzzing Bee" film (1964)

- Date: 15 September 1964 (time approximate)
- Place: Anderson Peak, Big Sur, and Vandenberg AFB, California (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Motion-picture film; Military witnesses
- Shape: Object circling a missile warhead
- Witnesses: 1369th Photographic Squadron team
- Duration: Seconds, on film
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/big-sur-atlas-1964/

In 1964 an Air Force team on Anderson Peak used a telescope borrowed from Boston University to film Atlas missile launches from Vandenberg. In 1982, Robert Jacobs, the officer in charge on the mountain, said the film of one launch, nicknamed "Buzzing Bee", showed an object fly around the warhead and hit it with beams of light, and that the film had been confiscated. The project engineer said it showed decoy deployment.

**Explanation:** Project engineer Kingston George wrote in 1993 that the film showed the re-entry vehicle releasing decoy warheads and chaff, a classified technology at the time, which Jacobs was not cleared to know about.

## Valensole landing (1965)

- Date: 1 July 1965
- Place: Lavender field, Valensole, Alpes-de-Haute-Provence (France)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Landing / trace case
- Evidence: Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Official government document or case file
- Shape: Egg-shaped craft on legs; two small beings
- Witnesses: Farmer Maurice Masse
- Duration: A few minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/valensole-1965/

Lavender farmer Maurice Masse said he found a rugby-ball-shaped craft on six legs in his field and two small beings beside it; one pointed a tube at him and he was paralysed. The craft left marks in the soil where lavender failed to grow for years.

**Explanation:** Investigated by the Gendarmerie; the ground marks and the effect on lavender plants were documented but never explained.

## Deception Island — the Antarctic sightings (1965)

- Date: 3 July 1965
- Place: Argentine station, Deception Island, South Shetland Islands (Antarctica)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Military witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file; Reported electromagnetic effects (engines, instruments)
- Shape: Lens-shaped object, mostly red and green, changing to yellow, blue, white and orange
- Witnesses: Seventeen people at the Argentine station; nine at the Chilean station; five at the British base; two meteorologists on Laurie Island
- Duration: 15–20 minutes (Navy statement)
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/antarctica-1965/

Over two winter nights in July 1965, the staff of three stations on Deception Island and of the Argentine station on Laurie Island, in the South Orkneys, reported a coloured, manoeuvring light. On July 2 five British observers saw a green and red light zig-zag, hover and speed up. On the evening of July 3, nine Chilean observers watched a light change colour and leave a steam-like trail, and at 19:42 seventeen people at the Argentine station, three Chilean visitors among them, watched a lens-shaped object. In a statement on July 6, the Argentine Navy described “a giant, lens-shaped flying object, solid in appearance, mostly red and green in color”, moving on a zig-zag course toward the east with changes of speed and direction, without sound, 10 to 15 km away. On Laurie Island, two variometers registered “sudden and strong disturbances of the magnetic field” during a 15-second sighting.

**Explanation:** The Argentine Navy said in an official statement that its observers had seen a solid, lens-shaped flying object, and Lt. Daniel Perisse, at the Argentine station, said a weather balloon, a plane or a star had been ruled out. No explanation was ever published, and the photographs said to have been taken have not been released.

Sources:
- [NICAP — Antarctica, July 1965: the reports and the Argentine Navy statement](https://nicap.org/docs/antarctica/650703rep.htm)
- [UFOs at close sight — Deception Island, Antarctica, 1965](http://ufologie.patrickgross.org/htm/decepcion.htm)

## Buenos Aires — Meteors scrambled (1965)

- Date: 16 July 1965 (time approximate)
- Place: Buenos Aires (Argentina)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Photographs; Many independent witnesses; Military witnesses
- Shape: Two bright discs
- Witnesses: Many residents; Argentine Air Force
- Duration: About 10 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/buenos-aires-meteors-1965/

Two bright discs hung motionless over Buenos Aires for about ten minutes, then flew off at high speed. With calls pouring in, the Seventh Air Brigade scrambled three Gloster Meteor jets from Morón air base, which found nothing.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — UFO sightings in Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO_sightings_in_Argentina)

## August 1965 — lights over Oklahoma, Kansas and Texas (1965)

- Date: 1 August 1965 (time approximate)
- Place: Oklahoma City and across Oklahoma, Kansas, Texas and New Mexico (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Police witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Radar tracking; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Coloured lights, red, white and blue-green, reported hovering and moving
- Witnesses: Oklahoma Highway Patrol and police officers, weather observers and thousands of residents
- Duration: From about 8 p.m. to 3 a.m., and again the following nights
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/midwest-wave-1965/

On the night of August 1, 1965, from about 8 p.m. until 3 a.m., a steady stream of reports came in from Oklahoma, Kansas, Texas and New Mexico of coloured lights moving in the sky, some in formation. The Oklahoma Highway Patrol said officers in several towns had seen them and that Tinker Air Force Base had as many as four on radar at once at about 22,000 ft. Tinker would neither confirm nor deny the radar contacts, and its approach-control radar reported none during the height of the local sightings. The reports continued for several nights, and Blue Book received dozens from the region. The Air Force answered first that people were seeing the Delta Aquarid meteors, then that they were seeing bright stars and planets, which led to public objections from planetarium staff that the planets named were not in view.

**Explanation:** The Air Force first suggested a meteor shower, then said the lights were stars and planets made to change colour by scintillation, naming Jupiter among them. Planetarium directors in Oklahoma objected that Jupiter was not in the evening sky at that season; one suggested Antares or Vega. The reported radar contacts were never confirmed: a Tinker AFB spokesman would neither confirm nor deny them, and the base’s approach-control radar reported no contacts at the peak.

Sources:
- [Oklahoma Journal, August 2, 1965 (transcribed)](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/press/oklahomajournal2aug1965.htm)
- [Oklahoma City Times, August 3, 1965 (transcribed)](https://ufology.patrickgross.org/press/oklahomacitytimes3aug1965.htm)
- [Daily Oklahoman, August 4, 1965 (transcribed)](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/press/dailyoklahoman4aug1965.htm)

## Heflin Polaroids — Santa Ana (1965)

- Date: 3 August 1965
- Place: Myford Road near Santa Ana, California (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Hat-shaped disc; a smoke ring
- Witnesses: 1 (Rex Heflin, highway traffic investigator)
- Duration: About 20 seconds
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/heflin-santa-ana-1965/

Orange County highway traffic investigator Rex Heflin was photographing road signs from his work van when he saw a hat-shaped object cross the road ahead. He took three Polaroid pictures through the windshield and side window, then a fourth of a smoke ring it seemed to leave behind. The photos were printed in the Santa Ana Register and studied by the Air Force and the Condon Committee.

**Explanation:** Project Blue Book classed the photographs as a hoax. Analysts argued the "UFO" was a small object hung or thrown near the van. Supporters point out that Heflin's originals were never shown to be faked.

Sources:
- [Condon Report, case 52 — Santa Ana, California, photographs](https://files.ncas.org/condon/text/case52.htm)
- [UFOs at close sight — the Rex Heflin photographs, 1965](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/htm/heflin65.htm)

## Incident at Exeter (1965)

- Date: 3 September 1965
- Place: Kensington, near Exeter, New Hampshire (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Police witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Row of five pulsing red lights
- Witnesses: Norman Muscarello; officers Bertrand and Hunt
- Duration: About an hour in total
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/exeter-1965/

Hitchhiker Norman Muscarello saw five pulsing red lights hover over a field on Route 150 and rushed to the Exeter police station. Returning with Officer Eugene Bertrand, both — and then Officer David Hunt — watched the lights rise from behind trees and move over the field.

**Explanation:** The Air Force first blamed a military exercise and twinkling stars, then changed the case to "unidentified". A 2011 Skeptical Inquirer analysis proposed a KC-97 refuelling tanker.

## Kecksburg fireball (1965)

- Date: 9 December 1965
- Place: Kecksburg, Pennsylvania (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Tracked object event
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Photographs; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Fireball; later claims of an acorn-shaped object
- Witnesses: Thousands across six states
- Duration: Seconds (fireball)
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/kecksburg-1965/

A brilliant fireball crossed the sky over the Detroit–Windsor area and was reported from Ontario to Pennsylvania. Residents of Kecksburg said something fell into the woods; state police and military personnel searched and reported finding nothing.

**Explanation:** Astronomers identified a bright bolide seen from six states and Ontario; no object was found at Kecksburg. Claims of a recovered acorn-shaped craft are unsupported, and the Soviet Kosmos 96 re-entry was ruled out by timing.

## Tully "saucer nest" (1966)

- Date: 19 January 1966
- Place: Horseshoe Lagoon near Tully, Queensland (Australia)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Landing / trace case
- Evidence: Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Police witnesses
- Shape: Grey saucer rising from the lagoon
- Witnesses: Banana grower George Pedley
- Duration: Seconds
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/tully-1966/

George Pedley heard a hissing sound and saw a saucer-shaped object rise from a lagoon and climb away. In its place was a floating circle of flattened, clockwise-swirled reeds about 9 m across — the original "saucer nest".

**Explanation:** Police and the RAAF suggested a willy-willy (whirlwind) flattened the reeds; others considered it unexplained.

## Michigan "swamp gas" sightings (1966)

- Date: 20 March 1966
- Place: Dexter and Hillsdale, Michigan (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Police witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Photographs; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Football-shaped object with lights; glowing lights over a swamp
- Witnesses: Farm family, a dozen police officers, 87 college students
- Duration: Two nights
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/michigan-swamp-gas-1966/

On March 20, 1966, Frank Mannor and his son near Dexter said they walked toward a glowing, football-shaped object hovering over a swamp. About a dozen police officers reported lights. The next night 87 women at Hillsdale College watched a light hover over the campus arboretum for hours. Congressman Gerald Ford called for hearings, which led to the Condon Committee.

**Explanation:** J. Allen Hynek, the Air Force's scientific consultant, suggested that burning marsh gas might explain some of the lights over the swamps, and Blue Book filed the flap as "marsh gas". The explanation was widely ridiculed. Hynek later said he regretted how it was presented.

## Westall school sighting (1966)

- Date: 6 April 1966
- Place: Westall High School, Clayton South, Melbourne (Australia)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil)
- Shape: Silvery disc; descended into a paddock
- Witnesses: 200+ students and teachers
- Duration: ~20 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/westall-1966/

Students and staff watched a silvery disc descend behind trees into a paddock known as The Grange, then rise and leave while light aircraft circled. Several students said they saw a flattened circle in the grass.

**Explanation:** Researchers have proposed a stray HIBAL cosmic-ray research balloon launched from Mildura, trailed by light aircraft.

## Portage County police chase (1966)

- Date: 17 April 1966
- Place: Ravenna, Ohio → Conway, Pennsylvania (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Police witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file; Audio recording / radio transcript
- Shape: Bright disc-shaped light, "as big as a house"
- Witnesses: Deputies Dale Spaur & Wilbur Neff, officers in three towns
- Duration: ~1 hour; ~85 miles
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/portage-county-1966/

Portage County sheriff’s deputies Dale Spaur and Wilbur Neff, checking an abandoned car on Route 224, saw a brilliantly lit object rise from the woods. Told by radio to follow it, they chased it east at up to 100 mph for about 85 miles into Pennsylvania, joined by officers from East Palestine and Conway, PA, who also saw it before it shot straight up.

**Explanation:** Project Blue Book (Maj. Hector Quintanilla) concluded the officers first saw the Echo satellite and then Venus; the officers and Rep. William Stanton rejected this.

Sources:
- [NICAP — Portage County chase documents](https://www.nicap.org/660417ravenna_dir.htm)

## Paulding Light (1966)

- Date: 1 July 1966 (time approximate)
- Place: Robbins Pond Road, near Paulding, Michigan (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Recurring lights
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Photographs
- Shape: A light that brightens, dims, changes colour and seems to sway
- Witnesses: Visitors to the viewing spot, nightly since the 1960s
- Duration: Recurring
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/paulding-light/

From the end of Robbins Pond Road in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula, visitors look north along a power-line cut and see a light rise, brighten, change colour and seem to sway before going out. Teenagers first reported it in 1966, and legends grew around it, the best known being the lantern of a railway brakeman killed on the line. In 2010 a group of Michigan Tech students set up a telescope at the spot and could make out pairs of headlights, then recreated the light on cue with a car on U.S. 45, the highway that crosses the line of sight about 4.5 miles away.

**Explanation:** In May 2010 students from the optics society (SPIE) chapter at Michigan Technological University watched the light through a telescope, saw that it was a pair of car headlights, and recreated it on cue by having one of them drive U.S. 45, about 4.5 miles away, with his hazard lights on.

Sources:
- [Michigan Tech — Students solve mystery of the Paulding Light (2010)](https://www.mtu.edu/news/2010/10/just-time-for-halloween-michigan-tech-students-solve-mystery-paulding-light.html)
- [Wikipedia — Paulding Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paulding_Light)

## The lead masks of Vintém Hill (1966)

- Date: 17 August 1966 (time approximate)
- Place: Morro do Vintém, Niterói, Rio de Janeiro (Brazil)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Official government document or case file
- Shape: A round orange light rising and falling over the hill (one resident’s report)
- Witnesses: A boy who found the bodies; police; a local resident who reported an orange light
- Duration: Unknown
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/lead-masks-1966/

On August 17, 1966, two electronics technicians from Campos dos Goytacazes, Manoel Pereira da Cruz and Miguel José Viana, travelled to Niterói, bought raincoats and a bottle of water, and were last seen in a bar, one of them nervously checking his watch. On August 20 a boy flying a kite on Morro do Vintém found their bodies side by side, dressed in suits and raincoats, with crude lead eye-masks beside them. There were no signs of violence. A notebook held the instructions “16:30 be at the specified place. 18:30 swallow capsules, after the effect protect metals, await signal, mask”. The autopsy came weeks late and no toxicology was done, so the cause of death was never established. Days after the discovery, Rio newspapers reported that a resident had seen a round orange object rising and falling over the hill on the night the men went up, and the case entered UFO literature through Flying Saucer Review in 1967. There is no evidence linking the light to the deaths; a friend told police the men belonged to a group of “scientific spiritualists” who tried to contact other beings, which points to drugs taken in a ritual.

**Explanation:** The likeliest account is an accidental overdose during an attempt at contact: a friend said the men were “scientific spiritualists”, their notebook told them to take capsules and wait for a signal, and mask-making materials were found at their homes. No toxicology was ever done, so the cause of death is officially unknown.

Sources:
- [Skeptoid #398 — Solving the Lead Masks of Vintém Hill](https://skeptoid.com/episodes/4398)
- [Wikipedia — Lead masks case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_masks_case)

## Malmstrom AFB Echo Flight shutdown (1967)

- Date: 16 March 1967
- Place: Echo Flight, Malmstrom AFB missile field, Montana (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Reported glowing red object (1990s testimony)
- Witnesses: Launch crew; security guards (later testimony)
- Duration: —
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/malmstrom-echo-flight-1967/

All ten Minuteman I missiles of Echo Flight dropped off strategic alert almost simultaneously. Decades later, former missile officers said guards had reported a glowing red object hovering at the gate. The Air Force’s contemporaneous report found no UFO involvement.

**Explanation:** The 1967 Air Force report found no UFO link and rumours "disproven". A 2025 Pentagon report stated the shutdown was caused by a classified electromagnetic-pulse test. Later accounts by former officers (Robert Salas) described a red glowing object over the gate.

## Falcon Lake incident (1967)

- Date: 20 May 1967
- Place: Falcon Lake, Whiteshell Provincial Park, Manitoba (Canada)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Landing / trace case
- Evidence: Documented physiological effects; Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Official government document or case file
- Shape: Two glowing oval objects; one landed
- Witnesses: Stefan Michalak
- Duration: About 30 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/falcon-lake-1967/

Amateur prospector Stefan Michalak said two glowing craft descended near him; one landed on a rock outcrop. When he touched it, a blast of hot gas from a grid-like vent burned his chest. CBC has called it Canada’s best-documented UFO case.

**Explanation:** RCMP, RCAF and the Condon Committee could not explain it; some soil samples were mildly radioactive, possibly from radium paint. Later marks on Michalak’s body were judged self-inflicted.

## UMMO — the San José de Valderas photographs (1967)

- Date: 1 June 1967 (time approximate)
- Place: San José de Valderas, Alcorcón, near Madrid (Spain)
- Status: IDENTIFIED — Object positively identified
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs
- Shape: A circular craft with the UMMO sign, )+(, on its underside
- Witnesses: Anonymous photographers (“Antonio Pardo”); no credible eyewitnesses were found
- Duration: A few minutes, according to the photographers
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/ummo-valderas-1967/

In June 1967 photographs of a round craft marked underneath with the sign )+( reached the Madrid newspaper Informaciones and Spanish UFO researchers, left anonymously at a photo shop in Carabanchel and sent by a man signing himself “Antonio Pardo”. They were said to have been taken on June 1 at San José de Valderas, outside Madrid. The sign was that of UMMO, a planet whose inhabitants had been writing long typed letters to Spanish enthusiasts since the mid-1960s, and the pictures made UMMO famous. No reliable witness of the flight was ever found; the negatives that were later analysed had gaps in their sequence, and a police laboratory study in the 1990s, while finding no thread, noted lighting that suggested artificial light and could not rule out fraud. In the 1990s José Luis Jordán Peña, a Madrid engineer with an interest in parapsychology, admitted that he had created UMMO, that he had written the letters with the help of a few friends, and that the photographs showed a model hung from a thread. Believers still defend the case.

**Explanation:** A hoax. José Luis Jordán Peña, the main witness of the 1966 Aluche “landing”, admitted in the 1990s that he had invented UMMO as an experiment in credulity and that the photographs showed a small model hung from nylon thread; a stylistic study of the letters signed “Antonio Pardo” pointed to him, and in 1996 Manuel Carballal reproduced the pictures with a model on a fishing line.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia (Spanish) — Ummo](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ummo)
- [Patrick Gross — The UMMO affair: the San José de Valderas photographs and their analysis](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/ummo/guardiacivil01.htm)

## Cussac — two children and four small black beings (1967)

- Date: 29 August 1967 (time approximate)
- Place: Cussac, Cantal, Auvergne, France
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Official government document or case file
- Shape: Round craft about 4.6 m across, with four small black beings
- Witnesses: François (13) and his sister Anne-Marie (9)
- Duration: Minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/cussac-1967/

On August 29, 1967 a 13-year-old boy, François, and his 9-year-old sister, Anne-Marie, told the local police that while watching cows in a field at Cussac they had seen four small black beings, about 120 cm tall, with a shiny, silk-like look. The beings seemed to rise in the air and enter a round craft about 4.6 metres across that hovered over the field. The police noted a smell of sulphur and dried grass at the spot the craft was said to have left. The file is one of those that the French government put online in March 2007, and one of the children was later said to have suffered lasting health effects.

**Explanation:** No explanation has been agreed. The two children, aged 13 and 9, gave the same account to the police, and the police recorded a smell of sulphur and dried grass where the sphere was said to have stood. There were no other witnesses.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — Close encounter of Cussac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Close_encounter_of_Cussac)
- [UFO Evidence — The Cussac encounter, 29 August 1967](http://www.ufoevidence.org/cases/case705.htm)

## Six “flying saucers” across southern England (hoax) (1967)

- Date: 4 September 1967 (time approximate)
- Place: A line of six sites from the Isle of Sheppey, Kent, to Clevedon, Somerset (United Kingdom)
- Status: IDENTIFIED — Object positively identified
- Kind: Landing / trace case
- Evidence: Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Police witnesses; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Smooth, metallic-looking saucers about 1.4 m long, emitting a bleeping noise
- Witnesses: Members of the public who found them; four police forces, army bomb-disposal teams, the RAF and the MoD
- Duration: One day
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/saucer-hoax-1967/

On the morning of Monday, September 4, 1967, people in southern England began finding small “flying saucers”, six in all, set out along a nearly straight line at about 51.5° N: on a housing estate near Queenborough on the Isle of Sheppey, on a golf course in Bromley, in a paddock at Winkfield near Ascot, at Welford near Newbury, at Chippenham, and on Dial Hill at Clevedon. Each was about 1.4 m long, weighed about 45 kg and gave out an eerie electronic sound. Police cordoned them off; army bomb-disposal teams, RAF helicopters and the Ministry of Defence’s intelligence staff were called in; the army blew up the Chippenham saucer, one was lifted from Sheppey by helicopter, and one was sent to the Atomic Weapons Research Establishment at Aldermaston. When one was drilled into, a foul-smelling paste burst out over the police. By the evening the makers, apprentices from the Royal Aircraft Establishment at Farnborough, had owned up: it was a stunt for their Rag Week. The MoD’s file on the day was released by The National Archives.

**Explanation:** A Rag Week hoax by aircraft engineering apprentices at the Royal Aircraft Establishment, Farnborough, led by Christopher Southall and Roger Palmer: fibreglass shells with an oscillator and loudspeaker inside, filled with fermenting flour paste. They owned up the same day and raised money for charity.

Sources:
- [The National Archives (UK) — MoD UFO files](https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/help-with-your-research/research-guides/ufos/)
- [Wikipedia — 1967 British flying saucer hoax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_British_flying_saucer_hoax)

## Shag Harbour crash-landing (1967)

- Date: 4 October 1967
- Place: Shag Harbour, Nova Scotia (Canada)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Tracked object event
- Evidence: Police witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file; Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil)
- Shape: Row of 4 orange lights; object floating on the sea
- Witnesses: RCMP officers, fishermen, residents
- Duration: About an hour
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/shag-harbour-1967/

Residents and three RCMP officers watched orange lights descend at an angle and hit the water off Shag Harbour. Rescue boats found a patch of yellow foam but no aircraft; no plane was missing. Earlier that evening an Air Canada crew and a fishing boat’s radar also reported unusual objects.

**Explanation:** The RCMP, Canadian Coast Guard and Navy divers found no aircraft; the Condon Committee listed it as unexplained. No debris was recovered beyond a yellowish foam on the water.

## Devon "flying cross" police chase (1967)

- Date: 24 October 1967
- Place: A3072, Holsworthy to Hatherleigh, Devon (United Kingdom)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Recurring lights
- Evidence: Police witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Star-spangled cross of light
- Witnesses: PCs Roger Willey and Clifford Waycott; a motorist; two BBC engineers
- Duration: About an hour
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/devon-flying-cross-1967/

Two police constables driving from Holsworthy to Hatherleigh saw a bright, cross-shaped light at treetop height. They followed it for about 14 miles, at up to 80 mph, and said it was like "looking through wet glass". A second object joined it at 04:23. A Land Rover driver saw it too. It faded at about 5 a.m. The case was raised in Parliament during the autumn 1967 "flying cross" wave.

**Explanation:** The Ministry attributed it to the planet Venus, as it did several similar sightings that month.

Sources:
- [The National Archives (UK) — MoD UFO files](https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/help-with-your-research/research-guides/ufos/)
- [Wikipedia — UFO sightings in the United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO_sightings_in_the_United_Kingdom)

## Zond IV re-entry — the “craft with windows” (1968)

- Date: 3 March 1968
- Place: Across the sky from Kentucky through Ohio to Pennsylvania (United States)
- Status: IDENTIFIED — Object positively identified
- Kind: Tracked object event
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Two or three fiery objects with golden-orange tails; some witnesses described a cigar-shaped craft with lit windows
- Witnesses: Hundreds of people along a line from Kentucky to Pennsylvania; about 78 written reports
- Duration: About two minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/zond-4-reentry-1968/

At about 9:45 p.m. EST on March 3, 1968, hundreds of people along a line from Kentucky to Pennsylvania saw a slow procession of fiery objects with golden-orange tails cross the sky to the north-east. Most saw two or three main pieces; some described a single long, wingless craft, said that “many windows seemed to be lit up from the inside”, or put it at treetop level. NORAD identified the objects as pieces of the Soviet Zond IV probe, launched on March 2, or of its rocket, and Project Blue Book recorded “satellite decay”; a contractor even estimated where surviving pieces might have fallen in north-central Pennsylvania. For the Condon study, William Hartmann compared about 30 detailed reports with the known event: many put the objects within a few miles and below 10,000 ft, when the debris was burning up tens of kilometres high, and the joining of separate lights into one windowed hull became his textbook case of the “airship effect”.

**Explanation:** NORAD identified the objects as fragments of the Soviet Zond IV probe or its rocket re-entering the atmosphere; Blue Book closed the case as satellite decay. The Condon study used it as its standard example of how honest witnesses turn a re-entry into a structured craft.

Sources:
- [Project Blue Book file, “Northeastern U.S.”, March 1968 (Internet Archive)](https://archive.org/details/1968-03-6958071-NortheasternU-S)
- [Condon report, Section VI, Chapter 2: Perceptual problems — the re-entry of Zond IV debris](http://files.ncas.org/condon/text/s6chap02.htm)
- [Wikipedia — Zond 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zond_4)

## Minot AFB — B-52 radar and missile-field sightings (1968)

- Date: 24 October 1968
- Place: Minot AFB and missile field, North Dakota (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Military witnesses; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Photographs; Official government document or case file; Reported electromagnetic effects (engines, instruments)
- Shape: Large glowing orange object
- Witnesses: Missile maintenance and security teams; B-52 crew
- Duration: About 3 hours
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/minot-afb-1968/

Before dawn, maintenance and security teams at several Minuteman sites reported a large glowing object. A B-52 returning to Minot was asked to look for it. Its radar navigator painted a target that stayed about a mile off the bomber, and radarscope photographs were taken. The UHF radio dropped out when the object was closest. After landing, the crew described a bright light near the ground. Blue Book closed it within weeks. It is one of the best-documented military cases in the files.

**Explanation:** Blue Book's conclusion: ground sightings were probably the B-52 and the star Sirius; the radar contact and the B-52's temporary loss of UHF radio were "possibly plasma", similar to ball lightning; the crew's sighting could have been the star Vega or a light on the ground.

Sources:
- [A Narrative of UFO Events at Minot Air Force Base](https://minotb52ufo.sohp.us/narrative.php)
- [Shough report on the Minot events (abstract)](https://minotb52ufo.com/shough/ms_sec1.php)

## Jimmy Carter’s light at Leary, Georgia (1969)

- Date: 6 January 1969
- Place: Outside the Lions Club meeting, Leary, Georgia (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses
- Shape: A bright light, as bright as the Moon, changing from white to blue to red and back
- Witnesses: Jimmy Carter, then a Georgia state senator and Lions Club district governor, and about ten others
- Duration: 10 to 12 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/carter-leary-1969/

At about 7:15 one evening in 1969, Jimmy Carter was waiting outside a school lunchroom in Leary, Georgia, to speak to the local Lions Club, when one of the men pointed out a light in the west, about 30 degrees above the horizon. Carter said it seemed to come closer, stopped beyond the pine trees, changed from white to blue, then red, then white, and then receded, after 10 to 12 minutes. As governor, in September 1973, he filled in a sighting report for the International UFO Bureau, dating it October 1969; the Lions Club’s own records show his Leary speech was on January 6, 1969, and the club had disbanded before October. Investigators in 1976 found that most of those present did not remember the event. On January 6, Venus was a brilliant evening star in the direction Carter gave, which is the accepted explanation; Carter said later that he took it for something unexplained, not for a spacecraft.

**Explanation:** Robert Sheaffer and Allan Hendry identified it as Venus, which was near its greatest brilliancy in the western sky that evening; a later analysis proposed a barium-cloud release from a rocket fired at Eglin AFB. Carter himself said he never thought it was an alien craft.

Sources:
