- [Carter’s report to the International UFO Bureau (NICAP copy)](http://www.nicap.org/waves/CarterSightingRptOct1969.pdf)
- [Robert Sheaffer — President Carter’s “UFO” is identified as the planet Venus (1977)](http://www.debunker.com/texts/carter_ufo.html)
- [Wikipedia — Jimmy Carter UFO incident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter_UFO_incident)

## Fort Beaufort — police fire at an object (1971)

- Date: 26 June 1971 (time approximate)
- Place: Braeside farm near Fort Beaufort, Eastern Cape (South Africa)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Police witnesses; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Fireball that changed colour
- Witnesses: Farmer Bennie Smit, farmhands and police officers
- Duration: Morning
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/fort-beaufort-1971/

Farmer Bennie Smit said he, his workers and local police fired shots at a fireball-like object that changed colour as it hovered among the trees on his farm. The story went around the world. Rumours said the army investigated the site but no records were produced. The town's "UFO Bar" and hotel clippings kept the story alive.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — UFO sightings in South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO_sightings_in_South_Africa)

## Lake Cote aerial survey photograph (1971)

- Date: 4 September 1971
- Place: Laguna de Cote, Costa Rica
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Metallic disc over the lake
- Witnesses: None at the time (found on the negative)
- Duration: Single survey frame
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/lake-cote-1971/

An Instituto Geográfico Nacional aerial-survey camera flying at about 10,000 ft photographed Lake Cote for mapping. One frame shows a disc-like object over the water that the crew never saw; the adjacent frames do not show it.

**Explanation:** Taken by the government’s Instituto Geográfico Nacional mapping aircraft; the object was not noticed at the time. Analyses have not produced an accepted identification.

## Delphos ring (1971)

- Date: 2 November 1971
- Place: Delphos, Kansas (United States)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Landing / trace case
- Evidence: Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Mushroom-shaped, with multicoloured lights
- Witnesses: Ronnie Johnson (16) and his parents
- Duration: Minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/delphos-1971/

While doing evening chores on his family’s farm near Delphos, 16-year-old Ronnie Johnson saw a mushroom-shaped object, lit in many colours, hovering about 25 yards away. His parents came out to a glowing ring on the ground where it had been. It was still visible the next day. Investigators found that the soil in the ring was dry beside damp ground and would not let water through, and that it held more calcium and soluble salts and was more acidic, with a white deposit of calcium oxalate. Both calcium oxalate and oxalic acid irritate skin and eyes, and Ronnie’s parents said touching the ring numbed their fingers. It is one of the classic UFO “landing trace” cases.

**Explanation:** No official body reached a conclusion. The soil results are the main physical evidence; sceptics note that the account rests on one family, and that fungi can leave rings of altered, water-repelling soil.

Sources:
- [The Black Vault — Analysis of soil samples, Delphos, Kansas](https://www.theblackvault.com/casefiles/analysis-soil-samples-related-delphos-kansas-november-2-1971/)

## Pascagoula encounter (1973)

- Date: 11 October 1973 (time approximate)
- Place: Pascagoula River, Pascagoula, Mississippi (United States)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Audio recording / radio transcript
- Shape: Oval object with flashing blue lights
- Witnesses: Charles Hickson (45) and Calvin Parker (17)
- Duration: Not recorded
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/pascagoula-1973/

Charles Hickson and his young colleague Calvin Parker said that while fishing from a pier on the west bank of the Pascagoula River they heard a whirring noise, saw two flashing blue lights and an oval object about 30–40 feet across, and were taken aboard by three creatures with claw-like hands, examined and returned. They went to the Jackson County sheriff’s office around 11 p.m. Officers who suspected a prank left the two alone in a room with a hidden recorder; the men’s talk matched their story. The case set off a wave of 1973 reports along the Gulf Coast and made Hickson a long-time public speaker; Parker published his own account in 2018.

**Explanation:** No physical evidence was found beyond the two men’s testimony. Sceptics see a hoax or a hallucination; the witnesses stuck to their story, including when they were secretly recorded at the sheriff’s office.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — Pascagoula incident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pascagoula_incident)

## Coyne helicopter incident (1973)

- Date: 18 October 1973
- Place: Near Mansfield, Ohio (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Military witnesses; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Reported electromagnetic effects (engines, instruments); Official government document or case file
- Shape: Grey cigar-shaped body, red nose light, white tail light, green beam
- Witnesses: Four-man Army Reserve crew; a family on the ground
- Duration: About 5 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/coyne-1973/

An Army Reserve Bell UH-1H (tail number 68-15444) on its way from Columbus to Cleveland was cruising at 2,500 feet near Mansfield when the crew saw a red light closing on the helicopter from the east. Capt. Lawrence Coyne took the controls and began an emergency descent, expecting a collision. They then saw a cigar-shaped grey object hover over the helicopter, with a red light at the nose, a white light at the tail and a green beam that lit the cockpit. After it left, the crew found the helicopter at about 3,500 feet in a climb of 1,000 feet a minute, with the collective still fully down, and the compass spinning. The Army Reserve’s report is among the best-known official records of an aircrew encounter.

**Explanation:** The sceptic Philip Klass argued that the crew first saw a bright fireball of the Orionid meteor shower and then misjudged what followed. Investigators for CUFOS and others reject this: by their timeline the object was in view for several minutes, and a family on the ground reported lights too.

Sources:
- [NICAP — Mansfield, Ohio, October 18, 1973](http://www.nicap.org/731018mansfield_dir.htm)
- [J. Zeidman — A helicopter–UFO encounter over Ohio (CUFOS)](https://cufos.org/PDFs/books/A%20Helicopter-UFO%20Encounter%20Over%20Ohio.pdf)

## Berwyn Mountains "crash" (1974)

- Date: 23 January 1974
- Place: Cadair Berwyn, North Wales (United Kingdom)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Tracked object event
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Infrared or other sensor data
- Shape: Glowing light on the hillside
- Witnesses: Villagers across the Dee valley; a nurse who drove up the mountain
- Duration: Evening
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/berwyn-1974/

At 20:38 a loud bang and tremor shook villages around the Berwyn Mountains, and people saw lights on the hillside. A local nurse drove up and described a glowing sphere. Police searched and found nothing. The event was later retold as a UFO crash with a secret military recovery, sometimes called "the Welsh Roswell". Seismographs recorded an earthquake, and meteor observers logged a fireball at the same moment.

**Explanation:** A small earthquake shook the area at the same moment that a bright fireball was seen across northern England and Wales. The lights on the hillside were most likely poachers' lamps. Investigators found no crash and no recovery.

## Coyame “crash” — Chihuahua (1974)

- Date: 25 August 1974 (time approximate)
- Place: Coyame, Chihuahua, Mexico
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Tracked object event
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Disc-shaped object (as told)
- Witnesses: Local residents (reported)
- Duration: Not recorded
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/coyame-1974/

According to ufologists, residents near Coyame, in the Chihuahuan desert, reported a mid-air collision between a UFO and a small aeroplane on August 25, 1974, followed by a military recovery and a cover-up. The best-known version says U.S. air-defence radar followed a fast, high object from the Gulf of Mexico until it vanished near Coyame, and that a light aircraft that had left El Paso collided with it. Historians point instead to the real 1974 crash and recovery of a Cessna that had been carrying drugs, which they believe gave rise to the story. It is sometimes called Mexico’s Roswell. The case is listed because it is so often cited, not because the account is documented.

**Explanation:** Historians say the reports were most likely prompted by the crash and military recovery of a Cessna used for drug smuggling. The radar story that circulates in UFO literature is known only from later retellings.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — UFO sightings in Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO_sightings_in_Mexico)
- [Mexico Unexplained — The flying saucer crash at Coyame](https://mexicounexplained.com/flying-saucer-crash-coyame-mexican-roswell/)

## Langenburg rings (1974)

- Date: 1 September 1974
- Place: Langenburg, Saskatchewan (Canada)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Landing / trace case
- Evidence: Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Official government document or case file; Reported electromagnetic effects (engines, instruments)
- Shape: Five domed discs
- Witnesses: 1 (farmer Edwin Fuhr)
- Duration: About 15 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/langenburg-1974/

Farmer Edwin Fuhr was swathing a rapeseed field when he saw five metallic, dome-shaped objects spinning just above the ground near a slough. He sat frozen for about 15 minutes until they rose silently in formation and left, trailing grey vapour. He said his swather would not restart. The RCMP found five rings of flattened, swirled crop matching his description, with no tracks leading in.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — UFO sightings in Canada: Langenburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO_sightings_in_Canada#1974,_Langenburg,_Saskatchewan)

## Billy Meier’s “beamship” photographs (1975)

- Date: 28 January 1975 (time approximate)
- Place: Zürcher Oberland, around Hinwil, canton of Zürich (Switzerland)
- Status: IDENTIFIED — Object positively identified
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs; Motion-picture film
- Shape: Disc-shaped “beamships” with domes and rings
- Witnesses: Eduard “Billy” Meier alone; no independent witness of any contact
- Duration: Claimed contacts from 1975 onwards
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/billy-meier-1975/

Eduard “Billy” Meier, from the canton of Zürich, says that on January 28, 1975, he met Semjase, a woman from the Pleiades, beside her spacecraft, and that contacts which had begun in his childhood went on for years. From 1975 he produced hundreds of sharp colour photographs and some film of saucer-shaped “beamships” over the fields and woods of the Zürcher Oberland, later the basis of books, a following and the 1987 film Contact. Scientists, sceptics and most ufologists regard them as fraudulent. Investigators such as Kal Korff argued that models had been photographed close up or combined with landscapes; Meier’s former wife Kalliope said in 1997 that she had seen the models and that the stories were invented; Meier conceded that he had used models to re-create scenes; and pictures he presented as the aliens Asket and Nera were traced to performers on American television.

**Explanation:** A hoax. Meier’s former wife said in 1997 that the “beamships” were models made from household objects such as dustbin lids and carpet tacks; Meier admitted to Gary Kinder that he had used models to “recreate scenes”; and photographs of two “Pleiadian” women turned out to show dancers from the Golddiggers troupe on The Dean Martin Show.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — Billy Meier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Meier)

## Loring Air Force Base intrusions (1975)

- Date: 27 October 1975
- Place: Loring Air Force Base, Limestone, Maine (United States)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Military witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Low aircraft with a red light and a white strobe
- Witnesses: Security police, including S/Sgt Danny Lewis
- Duration: About 40 minutes the first night; repeated for days
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/loring-1975/

On the evening of October 27, 1975 a security patrol at Loring Air Force Base, a Strategic Air Command base that held nuclear weapons, saw an aircraft with a red light and a white strobe approaching the north perimeter at about 300 feet. The base was put on alert and a ground sweep began. Over the next 40 minutes the object came within 300 yards of the restricted weapons storage area at about 150 feet, moving in ways described as helicopter-like, and no one could get a fix on it before it left toward Grand Falls, New Brunswick. Similar reports came from the base, and from other bases, for more than a week; Air Force messages about them were released under the Freedom of Information Act.

**Explanation:** The Air Force never identified the object; its messages from the base describe an unidentified, helicopter-like aircraft that evaded the ground sweep. No conventional aircraft was found.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — Loring Air Force Base alert area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loring_Air_Force_Base_Alert_Area)

## Wurtsmith Air Force Base and the KC-135 chase (1975)

- Date: 30 October 1975
- Place: Wurtsmith Air Force Base, Oscoda, Michigan (United States)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Military witnesses; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Radar tracking; Official government document or case file
- Shape: One white light pointing down and two red lights at the rear
- Witnesses: Base security police and the six-man crew of a KC-135 tanker
- Duration: About an hour
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/wurtsmith-1975/

At about 10:10 p.m. on October 30, 1975, guards at Wurtsmith, a Strategic Air Command base on Lake Huron, saw an object with a white light pointing downward and two red lights at the rear. Minutes later security police reported an “unidentified helicopter” hovering low over the weapons storage area, and the base radar approach control picked up a target about 35 miles to the south-east. A KC-135 tanker flying nearby was asked to look. Its six-man crew, among them Maj. Frederick Pappas, saw lights and painted the object on their radar for about ten seconds, and followed it at about 2,000 feet north over Lake Huron and then south toward Saginaw Bay; each time they closed in it sped away, and Capt. Myron Taylor put its final speed at about 1,000 knots. Low on fuel, they broke off. The NORAD log recorded that the tanker “made both visual sighting and radar skin paint” and that contact was lost 25 nautical miles south-east over Lake Huron.

**Explanation:** The NORAD log called it a helicopter over the weapons storage area, but no helicopter was identified, and the tanker crew described an object that pulled away each time they closed on it. It is one of a series of intrusions at northern Strategic Air Command bases that autumn, including Loring and Malmstrom.

Sources:
- [NICAP — Wurtsmith AFB, October 30, 1975 (report)](https://www.nicap.org/reports/751030wurtsmith_rep.htm)
- [UFOs at close sight — the 1975 SAC base intrusions](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/htm/sac.htm)

## Travis Walton disappearance (1975)

- Date: 5 November 1975
- Place: Apache–Sitgreaves National Forest near Heber, Arizona (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Glowing disc hovering over a clearing
- Witnesses: 7 (the logging crew)
- Duration: 5 days missing
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/travis-walton-1975/

A seven-man logging crew led by Mike Rogers was driving out of the forest after sunset when they saw a glowing disc over a clearing. Travis Walton got out and walked toward it, and the crew said a beam of light knocked him to the ground. They drove off in panic. When they came back he was gone. Police searched for five days. Walton then called his sister from a phone booth in Heber, saying he had been taken aboard. His story became the 1993 film Fire in the Sky.

**Explanation:** The crew passed some polygraph tests and Walton failed one. Philip Klass and Michael Shermer argued it was a hoax, with a motive: the crew was behind on a Forest Service contract, and an "act of God" could excuse the penalty. Walton maintains it happened.

## Malmstrom AFB — objects over the missile fields, November 1975 (1975)

- Date: 7 November 1975 (time approximate)
- Place: Malmstrom Air Force Base and its Minuteman missile fields, Montana (United States)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Lights over the launch facilities; on radar, slow targets that sounded like a jet
- Witnesses: Missile-site security teams, Air Defense radar operators and F-106 crews
- Duration: Several nights in early November 1975
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/malmstrom-1975/

In the first weeks of November 1975, after the intrusions at Loring and Wurtsmith, NORAD’s logs and messages record a run of reports from the Minuteman fields around Malmstrom AFB in Montana. Security teams at several launch facilities reported lights and objects; Malmstrom’s search and height-finder radars carried a target between about 9,000 and 15,600 ft moving at only seven knots; witnesses said it sounded like a jet, and the FAA said no jets were in the area. F-106 interceptors scrambled from Malmstrom could not make contact because of the darkness and the target’s low altitude. The NORAD messages, released under the Freedom of Information Act by 1979, give no explanation. Later accounts add a security alarm at launch facility K-7, a glowing disc “the size of a football field” and tampered warheads; those details come from interviews years afterwards, not from the released records.

Sources:
- [The Black Vault — records on objects over Malmstrom AFB, November 1975 (FOIA)](https://www.theblackvault.com/documentarchive/unidentified-flying-objects-over-malmstrom-afb-november-1975/)
- [CIA Reading Room — “U.F.O. files: the untold story” (1979), quoting the NORAD messages](https://www.cia.gov/readingroom/document/cia-rdp88-01315r000300070001-4)

## CFS Falconbridge — the NORAD message from Ontario (1975)

- Date: 11 November 1975
- Place: 30 nautical miles south-south-west of Canadian Forces Station Falconbridge, near Sudbury, Ontario (Canada)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: A circular, brilliantly lit object with two black spots in the centre
- Witnesses: Four members of the station (a major, a captain, a corporal and a master corporal); many reports to the Ontario Provincial Police in Sudbury
- Duration: 14 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/falconbridge-1975/

At 11:15 UTC (6:15 a.m. local) on November 11, 1975, personnel at CFS Falconbridge, a Pinetree Line radar station north-east of Sudbury, saw and tracked an object bearing 210 degrees magnetic, 30 nautical miles from the station. 22nd NORAD Region Headquarters passed the report to the National Research Council in Ottawa: a “circular object, brilliantly lighted with two black spots in the center”, moving straight up “at high speed from 42,000 ft. to 72,000 ft.” with no horizontal movement, for 14 minutes, under broken cloud. The major who was the prime witness took photographs but did not know if they would come out. The same observers saw a similar object bearing 270 degrees, too far away for detail, and the Ontario Provincial Police in Sudbury received many other reports. The station’s history adds that two F-106 interceptors were scrambled from Selfridge Air National Guard Base in Michigan and saw nothing.

**Explanation:** No explanation was given. The sighting came in the autumn of 1975, when bases along the northern U.S. border were also reporting lights and radar targets. The radar fixed only a bearing and range; the height and the vertical climb are the observers’ estimates.

Sources:
- [NORAD 22nd Region message to the National Research Council, November 11, 1975 (transcription)](https://ufology.patrickgross.org/htm/offica04.htm)
- [Pinetree Line history — Falconbridge, Ontario](https://www.candemuseum.org/sites/default/files/archives/Pinetreeline/other/other15/other15e.html)
- [Wikipedia — CFS Falconbridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CFS_Falconbridge)

## Canary Islands sphere (1976)

- Date: 22 June 1976
- Place: Canary Islands (Gran Canaria, Tenerife, Fuerteventura) (Spain)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Photographs; Military witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Light rising from the sea, then a huge glowing sphere
- Witnesses: Several hundred, including the crew of the Spanish Navy corvette Atrevida
- Duration: Over 40 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/canary-islands-1976/

The crew of the corvette Atrevida saw a light rise from the sea, then a vast, luminous sphere spread out in the sky. Hundreds of people across Tenerife, La Palma, La Gomera and Gran Canaria saw it. A doctor near Gáldar said he saw two tall figures inside a transparent sphere. The Spanish Air Force investigation was leaked in 1977 and officially declassified in 1994.

**Explanation:** Spanish researcher Ricardo Campo matched the 1976 sighting, and similar Canary Islands events of the period, to U.S. Navy submarine-launched Poseidon missile tests in the Atlantic, whose exhaust clouds glow in sunlight at high altitude. The Spanish Air Force report left it unexplained.

## Tehran F-4 Phantom intercepts (1976)

- Date: 19 September 1976
- Place: Tehran, Iran
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file; Reported electromagnetic effects (engines, instruments)
- Shape: Brilliant flashing lights; object released a smaller one
- Witnesses: Controllers, two F-4 crews, a general, civilians
- Duration: ~3.5 hours
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/tehran-1976/

After civilian reports of a bright object over Tehran’s Shemiran district, the Imperial Iranian Air Force scrambled two F-4 Phantoms from Shahrokhi AB. Both crews said their instruments and communications failed near the object; the second pilot, Maj. Parviz Jafari, reported a radar lock and that his weapons panel died as a smaller object came toward him.

**Explanation:** A U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency report called it "an outstanding report" meeting all criteria for a valid study. Skeptic Philip Klass proposed Jupiter plus coincidental equipment failures.

## The Moroccan coast “UFO” — a Soviet rocket part re-entering (1976)

- Date: 19 September 1976
- Place: Along the Atlantic coast of Morocco, from Agadir to Kenitra and inland to Meknes and Fez
- Status: IDENTIFIED — Object positively identified
- Kind: Tracked object event
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: A silvery, luminous flattened ball or a large luminous tube, shedding bright sparks from the rear
- Witnesses: People in Agadir, Kalaa Sraghna, Essaouira, Casablanca, Rabat, Kenitra, Meknes and around Fez, including Maj. Mohamed Lissaoui of the Royal Gendarmerie
- Duration: Minutes; most reports between 01:00 and 01:30
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/morocco-reentry-1976/

Between 1 and 2 a.m. on September 19, 1976, the Royal Gendarmerie took calls from Agadir, Marrakech, Casablanca, Rabat, Kenitra and other towns describing the same thing: a silent, silvery, luminous object, disc-shaped to some and tube-shaped to others, moving slowly from south to north parallel to the Atlantic coast and giving off intermittent trails of bright sparks and fragments. Major Mohamed Lissaoui of the Gendarmerie saw it himself at about 1:15 a.m. on his way back from Kenitra, flying low and slowly “as if it were an aircraft preparing to land”. King Hassan II sent the Gendarmerie’s commander, Col. Housni Benslimane, to the U.S. embassy on September 23 to ask what the Americans knew; the defence attaché was shown witnesses’ drawings and cabled Washington. The State Department answered that it knew of no U.S. aircraft or satellite activity and that a meteor or a decaying satellite was possible. The cables became public through WikiLeaks in 2013.

**Explanation:** In 2012 the satellite tracker Ted Molczan matched the time and track to the re-entry of a piece of a Soviet Molniya rocket (an ullage-motor assembly from the third stage that orbited Molniya 1-35 in July 1976), an object catalogued by U.S. space tracking. The State Department’s 1976 reply had already said the sightings “could conceivably be compatible with a meteor, or a decaying satellite”. The witnesses’ estimate of 1,000 m was far too low, as estimates of a re-entry’s height usually are.

Sources:
- [U.S. embassy Rabat cable 1976RABAT05209 (WikiLeaks)](https://wikileaks.org/plusd/cables/1976RABAT05209_b.html)
- [State Department reply, cable 1976STATE247538 (WikiLeaks)](https://wikileaks.org/plusd/cables/1976STATE247538_b.html)
- [Foreign Policy — The Soviet space junk that became a Moroccan UFO](https://foreignpolicy.com/2013/04/11/wikileaked-the-soviet-space-junk-that-became-a-moroccan-ufo/)

## Talavera la Real air base sentries (1976)

- Date: 12 November 1976
- Place: Talavera la Real Air Base, Badajoz (Spain)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Intense light; tall luminous figure
- Witnesses: 3 soldiers on guard duty
- Duration: About 30 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/talavera-1976/

Two soldiers on night patrol at Talavera la Real air base heard a sound like radio interference that became a piercing whistle. When it stopped they saw an intense light in the sky for about 15 seconds. With a third guard and a guard dog they searched the perimeter. The dog came back cowering, and they said they saw a tall, glowing figure and fired their rifles at it before it vanished. The Spanish Air Force investigated and later released its file.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — UFO sightings in Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO_sightings_in_Spain)

## Broad Haven schoolchildren — the Welsh Triangle (1977)

- Date: 4 February 1977 (time approximate)
- Place: Broad Haven, Pembrokeshire, Wales (United Kingdom)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Yellow cigar-shaped craft; later an “upside-down saucer”
- Witnesses: 14 schoolchildren, then teachers and a hotel owner
- Duration: Lunchtime on Feb 4; further reports to April
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/broad-haven-1977/

At lunchtime on February 4, 1977 a group of 14 children at Broad Haven Primary School reported a yellow, cigar-shaped craft that landed in a field beyond the school grounds, and a silver creature with pointed ears. The headmaster had them draw what they saw, and the drawings agreed closely. On February 17 teachers and others said they saw the same craft, and on April 19 the owner of the Haven Fort Hotel in nearby Little Haven reported an “upside-down saucer” and two figures in a field. The wave of sightings in the area became known as the Dyfed or Welsh Triangle. A Ministry of Defence investigator found nothing to show a landing. The events were revisited in a 2023 Netflix documentary and a 2024 BBC series.

**Explanation:** A Ministry of Defence investigator found no physical evidence that anything had landed and suggested that “a local prankster” might have been responsible. The children’s drawings agreed closely, which is why the case is still told.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — Broad Haven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broad_Haven)
- [Herald.Wales — The Welsh Triangle: what was seen in the sky in 1977?](https://herald.wales/west-wales/pembrokeshire/the-welsh-triangle-what-was-seen-in-the-sky-back-in-1977/)
- [SUFON — Broad Haven, the Welsh Triangle](https://www.sufon.co.uk/post/broad-haven-the-welsh-triangle)

## Corporal Valdés — the patrol at Pampa Lluscuma (1977)

- Date: 25 April 1977 (time approximate)
- Place: Pampa Lluscuma, near Putre, Arica (Chile)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Military witnesses; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Bright violet lights descending from the sky
- Witnesses: Corporal Armando Valdés Garrido and seven conscripts of a Chilean Army patrol
- Duration: About 15 minutes (Valdés’s absence)
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/valdes-putre-1977/

In the early hours of April 25, 1977, a Chilean Army patrol of a corporal and seven conscripts camped on the Pampa Lluscuma, in the altiplano near Putre, said two bright lights came down near them. Corporal Armando Valdés walked towards one and disappeared; about fifteen minutes later he came back, collapsed and said, “You don’t know who we are or where we come from, but I assure you we will return.” The soldiers said his face now carried several days’ beard and his digital watch showed a date five days ahead. The story reached the press across the world, from Chilean papers to French ones, and became Chile’s best-known UFO case. It was never investigated under the military government: no statement was taken officially and the watch was neither photographed nor studied. Later reporting found that the group was guarding army horses rather than patrolling, and some soldiers said Valdés had a beard before that night. Valdés has given contradictory accounts since, at times calling it a prank that got out of hand.

**Explanation:** Valdés himself said in later interviews (reported for 2004, 2009 and 2013) that it was a joke among the patrol that got out of hand, with the watch set forward and the beard explained away to avoid punishment for not shaving, though at other times he has said it happened. The army never investigated and the watch was never examined.

Sources:
- [The Clinic — the supposed UFO sightings in Chile (2012)](https://www.theclinic.cl/2012/05/18/los-supuestos-avistamientos-de-ovnis-en-chile/)
- [Diario Uno — the controversial Chilean case that still raises doubts](https://www.diariouno.com.ar/chile/ovnis-extraterrestres-y-abduccion-el-polemico-caso-chile-que-aun-genera-dudas-n1325227)

## Petrozavodsk phenomenon (1977)

- Date: 20 September 1977
- Place: Petrozavodsk, Karelia, USSR (Russia)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file; Radar tracking
- Shape: Glowing "jellyfish" showering rays
- Witnesses: Thousands, from Helsinki to Vladivostok
- Duration: ~12 minutes over Petrozavodsk
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/petrozavodsk-1977/

In the early hours, residents of Petrozavodsk saw a glowing object spread over the city like a jellyfish, "raining" shafts of light. Reports came from across the Soviet Union and Finland. The event prompted the Soviet research programme Setka.

**Explanation:** Usually attributed to the launch of Kosmos-955 from Plesetsk, but the 1977 Academy of Sciences report said the phenomenon could not be satisfactorily understood.

## Colares "chupa-chupa" & Operação Prato (1977)

- Date: 15 October 1977 (time approximate)
- Place: Colares Island, Pará (Brazil)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Photographs; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file; Documented physiological effects; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Beams of light, "chupa-chupa" lights
- Witnesses: Islanders; Brazilian Air Force team
- Duration: Months in 1977
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/colares-1977/

Residents of Colares reported lights that fired beams and left burn-like marks. The mayor asked for help, and the Brazilian Air Force ran Operação Prato under Capt. Uyrangê Hollanda, photographing lights over several months. Hollanda gave a dramatic interview two decades later.

**Explanation:** The Brazilian Air Force closed Operação Prato after about four months, reporting no unusual phenomena; its files and photos are in the Arquivo Nacional.

## The object that fell near Bermejo — Bolivia’s 1978 search (1978)

- Date: 6 May 1978 (time approximate)
- Place: El Taire hill above the Bermejo River, Tarija department, on the Argentine border (Bolivia)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Tracked object event
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: A luminous cylinder or egg with a flaming tail
- Witnesses: Many people along the border; Bolivian Air Force pilots who searched the slope
- Duration: Seconds (the fall), followed by an explosion
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/bermejo-1978/

In the afternoon of May 6, 1978 (some reports say the Sunday evening, May 7), people on both sides of the Bermejo River, where Bolivia’s Tarija department meets Argentina, saw a luminous object with a fiery tail fall towards the El Taire hill and heard an explosion and a sonic boom. The Bolivian army and police searched, scientists from the University of Tarija went to the area, Argentina sent border police, and newspapers in Buenos Aires carried a police chief’s description of a dull metal cylinder about four metres long. The U.S. Embassy in La Paz reported the fall to Washington, and two U.S. Air Force attachés flew to Tarija; the embassy denied any secret recovery. A CIA-released bulletin of May 17, 1978 is headed “Bolivia reports conflict on details of fallen object”. The searches, slowed by the terrain and weather, recovered nothing anyone published. Explanations at the time ranged from a meteorite to space debris; no country reported losing a satellite, no meteorite fall is catalogued there for that date, and the object was never identified.

Sources:
- [CIA reading room — “Bolivia reports conflict on details of fallen object” (May 17, 1978)](https://www.cia.gov/readingroom/document/0005515665)
- [Nice-Matin, 17 May 1978, and NOSTRA (transcribed)](https://ufology.patrickgross.org/press/nicematin17mai1978.htm)
- [Nick Redfern — the lesser-known UFO crash in Bolivia](https://www.planet-today.com/2021/03/lesser-known-ufo-crash-in-bolivia.html)

## Emilcin abduction report (1978)

- Date: 10 May 1978 (time approximate)
- Place: Emilcin, Lublin Voivodeship (Poland)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Documented physiological effects
- Shape: White, hovering, humming craft
- Witnesses: 1 (farmer Jan Wolski)
- Duration: About an hour
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/emilcin-1978/

Jan Wolski, a 71-year-old farmer, said that while driving his horse-drawn cart through the woods near Emilcin, two short beings with greenish faces invited him aboard a white craft hovering over a clearing. There they examined him. He was later interviewed by investigators, who found him sincere. A monument now stands near the site, one of the few UFO memorials in the world.

## Gujan-Mestras — the light that put out the street lamps (1978)

- Date: 19 June 1978
- Place: Gujan-Mestras, Arcachon basin, Gironde (France)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Reported electromagnetic effects (engines, instruments); Official government document or case file
- Shape: An orange, oval luminous object
- Witnesses: Several residents; motorists on the RN113 near La Réole
- Duration: About 23:00 to 00:45
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/gujan-mestras-1978/

On the night of June 19, 1978, several people in Gujan-Mestras, on the Arcachon basin, heard a loud, dull noise and then saw an orange, oval light over the town. While it was there the street lighting faltered; the light faded from view as it climbed. Motorists on the road to Bordeaux near La Réole also saw a light moving slowly in the stormy sky. The gendarmerie took statements and GEPAN, the French space agency’s UFO office, investigated. GEIPAN classes the case B: probably a weather phenomenon connected with the storm. The two sightings could not be shown to be the same thing.

**Explanation:** GEIPAN class B: the witnesses probably saw an atmospheric phenomenon linked to the thunderstorm threatening the area. The gendarmerie and GEPAN could not link the town sighting to a light seen by motorists near La Réole.

Sources:
- [GEIPAN case 1978-06-00525, Gujan-Mestras (in French)](https://www.cnes-geipan.fr/fr/cas/1978-06-00525)

## Disappearance of Frederick Valentich (1978)

- Date: 21 October 1978
- Place: Bass Strait, off Cape Otway, Victoria (Australia)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Audio recording / radio transcript; Official government document or case file
- Shape: "Long shape" with four bright lights, orbiting above
- Witnesses: Pilot (radio transcript); later ground reports
- Duration: ~6 minutes of radio contact
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/valentich-1978/

Twenty-year-old Frederick Valentich, flying a Cessna 182L from Moorabbin to King Island, told Melbourne Flight Service a large lit aircraft was orbiting over him. His last words were "It is not an aircraft", followed by 17 seconds of metallic noise. No trace of him or the aircraft was ever found.

**Explanation:** The Department of Transport could not determine the cause. Theories include disorientation (seeing his own lights reflected while inverted), a staged disappearance and suicide.

## Clarenville — RCMP constable watches object over the water (1978)

- Date: 26 October 1978 (time approximate)
- Place: Clarenville and Random Island, Newfoundland (Canada)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Recurring lights
- Evidence: Police witnesses; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Oval with a fin, lights
- Witnesses: 12, including RCMP Constable James Blackwood
- Duration: 1–2 hours
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/clarenville-1978/

In the early morning a dozen people in Clarenville called the RCMP about an object hovering over the water toward Random Island. Constable James Blackwood watched it for one to two hours through a surveillance telescope. He described an oval with a fin at the back, hanging about 100 ft above the water. When he flashed his headlights, the object seemed to flash back. It then vanished and left no trace.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — UFO sightings in Canada: Clarenville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO_sightings_in_Canada#1978,_Clarenville,_Newfoundland_and_Labrador)

## Kuwait’s oil-field sightings and the pumps that stopped (1978)

- Date: 9 November 1978 (time approximate)
- Place: Kuwait Oil Company fields around Umm al-Aish, near the satellite earth station, northern Kuwait
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file; Reported electromagnetic effects (engines, instruments)
- Shape: A dazzling light; close up, a domed disc the size of a jumbo jet with a red light on top
- Witnesses: Staff of a Kuwait Oil Company pumping station, including an American, and of the nearby satellite station
- Duration: About seven minutes on the ground; the series of sightings ran for five weeks
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/kuwait-oil-fields-1978/

On the night of November 9–10, 1978, according to the Kuwaiti dailies Al-Qabas and Al-Watan, employees of the Kuwait Oil Company and of the satellite station near Umm al-Aish saw a dazzling light come down nearby. Four oil-company workers, one of them an American, went to within about 250 metres and saw a disc as big as a jumbo jet, with a cupola and a red light on top, which stayed on the ground for about seven minutes while telephone and radio links in the area were cut, then rose vertically at great speed. Sightings over the oil fields went on until December 14. The U.S. embassy’s cable to Washington in January 1979, “UFO sightings cause security concern in Kuwait”, reported that the government had set up a committee of experts from the Kuwait Institute for Scientific Research, and that a senior Kuwait Oil Company official said the oil-pumping equipment had shut down automatically during one sighting and started again by itself when the object left, although it could normally be restarted only by hand.

**Explanation:** The government’s committee of experts from the Kuwait Institute for Scientific Research ruled out spy aircraft but gave no explanation, and its report was never published. The U.S. embassy reported the stop and restart of the pumping equipment as a Kuwait Oil Company official described it; nothing else about the landing is documented beyond press accounts.

Sources:
- [U.S. embassy Kuwait, “UFO sightings cause security concern in Kuwait”, January 1979 (FOIA copy)](https://ufology.patrickgross.org/htm/foia59.htm)
- [Le Méridional, November 13, 1978 (translated press archive)](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/press/lemeridional13nov1978.htm)

## Zanfretta — the Torriglia night patrol (1978)

- Date: 6 December 1978
- Place: Marzano di Torriglia, Genoa, Italy
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file; Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil)
- Shape: Red oval craft over 10 m across; later a triangular craft
- Witnesses: Pier Fortunato Zanfretta (a security guard); 52 other statements
- Duration: Under an hour
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/zanfretta-1978/

At about 11:30 p.m. on December 6, 1978 the 26-year-old security guard Pier Fortunato Zanfretta, on patrol at Marzano, in the municipality of Torriglia, noticed four lights in the garden of a mansion called Casa Nostra and then a red oval object more than ten metres across. He radioed his supervisor that “they are not men”, then contact was lost; he was found unconscious and in shock. He described three-metre beings with mottled skin, yellow triangular eyes and clawed feet. A semicircular imprint of flattened grass was found in the garden, and Carabinieri Brigadier Antonio Nucchi collected 52 statements from people who had seen strange lights that night. A neurologist found no mental disturbance in January 1979. Zanfretta later described further abductions, eleven in all between 1978 and 1981, which are the most disputed part of the story.

**Explanation:** Sceptics say the grass imprint matched the place where the owners tied a horse, that regression hypnosis can create false memories, that the beings resembled characters in popular 1978 Italian TV and comics, and that the “footprints” were puddles. Italy’s national UFO centre (CUN) judged the case unreliable.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — Zanfretta UFO Incident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zanfretta_UFO_Incident)

## Kaikōura lights (1978)

- Date: 31 December 1978
- Place: Kaikōura coast, New Zealand
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Motion-picture film; Radar tracking; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Audio recording / radio transcript
- Shape: Bright white lights with a red tinge; pulsing orb
- Witnesses: Safe Air crew, TV crew, Wellington radar
- Duration: Two flights on Dec 30–31
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/kaikoura-1978/

After a Safe Air crew reported lights tracked by Wellington radar on 21 December, an Australian TV crew rode along on the Argosy newspaper run. On the night of 30–31 December they filmed lights pacing the aircraft off the Kaikōura coast in colour on 16 mm film, with Wellington controllers reporting matching radar returns.

**Explanation:** Explanations offered include Venus and Jupiter, squid-fishing boat lights, and meteors; none accounts for the radar returns to everyone’s satisfaction.

## Cecconi G.91R photographs over Treviso (1979)

- Date: 18 June 1979
- Place: Treviso Sant'Angelo air base, Veneto (Italy)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Photographs; Radar tracking; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Dull black, capsule-shaped, with a milky dome
- Witnesses: Maresciallo Giancarlo Cecconi; Istrana radar; Treviso tower
- Duration: About 5 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/cecconi-treviso-1979/

Returning from a photo-reconnaissance sortie in a G.91R, Italian Air Force pilot Giancarlo Cecconi was asked to identify an object tracked by Istrana radar over Treviso air base. He found a dull black, capsule-shaped object about 6–8 m long at about 1,300 m. He made passes within about 100 m and took more than 80 photographs with the aircraft's reconnaissance cameras. Then radar and the tower both lost it.

**Explanation:** The Italian Defence Ministry later said its photo interpreters had identified the object as a cylindrical balloon made of black plastic bags (a "solar balloon"). Cecconi rejected this, noting the object did not move in his jet's wake.

Sources:
- [The Black Vault — The UFO case of Maresciallo Cecconi, 18 June 1979](https://www.theblackvault.com/casefiles/the-ufo-case-of-maresciallo-cecconi-june-18-1979/)

## Pranles — the yellow light with a turning blue beam (1979)

- Date: 21 July 1979
- Place: Pranles, near Les Ollières-sur-Eyrieux, Ardèche (France)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: A stationary yellow-orange light projecting a blue beam that turned through 360°
- Witnesses: Two couples in neighbouring houses; the first witness a scientist who worked on light and colour
- Duration: About 45 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/pranles-1979/

From 22:45 to 23:28 on July 21, 1979, a couple at Pranles, in the Ardèche, watched a stationary yellow-orange light on top of a ridge towards the Serre de Pieroulet, like a lighthouse, projecting a blue beam that turned steadily through 360° and swept the ground. No sound was heard. As the husband, a scientist who worked on light and colour, prepared to take a photograph, it went out. Their neighbours had seen the same light in the same direction before closing their shutters at about 23:00. He reported it to the gendarmerie the next day. Re-examining the case decades later, GEIPAN found that a helicopter with a searchlight was the only plausible explanation, but a blue beam from a yellow source, turning continuously for no purpose, did not fit it. The case stays class D, unexplained, though GEIPAN notes it is near the line between unexplained and unusable because no field investigation was made at the time.

Sources:
- [GEIPAN case 1979-07-00644, Pranles (in French)](https://www.cnes-geipan.fr/fr/cas/1979-07-00644)

## Val Johnson — deputy's patrol car struck by a light (1979)

- Date: 27 August 1979
- Place: Near Stephen, Marshall County, Minnesota (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Police witnesses; Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Reported electromagnetic effects (engines, instruments); Documented physiological effects
- Shape: Beam of bright light just above the road
- Witnesses: 1 (Deputy Sheriff Val Johnson)
- Duration: Seconds; ~39 minutes unconscious
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/val-johnson-1979/

Deputy Val Johnson was patrolling rural roads when he saw a bright light just above the road. It rushed toward his car, the car was engulfed in light, and he heard glass breaking. He said he was unconscious for 39 minutes. Deputies found the car skewed across the road. The windshield was cracked, a headlight and the roof light were broken, and an aerial was bent. Both his watch and the car's clock were 14 minutes slow. A doctor compared his eye irritation to "welder's burns".

**Explanation:** UFO researchers (Allan Hendry, Jerome Clark) consider it significant. Skeptic Philip Klass argued it was a hoax and that Johnson damaged the car himself. The patrol car is on display at the Marshall County museum.

## Dechmont Law — Robert Taylor (1979)

- Date: 9 November 1979
- Place: Dechmont Law, Livingston, West Lothian (United Kingdom)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Documented physiological effects; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Dome-shaped object; two spiked spheres
- Witnesses: 1 (forester Robert Taylor)
- Duration: About 20 minutes unconscious
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/dechmont-law-1979/

Forestry worker Robert Taylor walked into a clearing on Dechmont Law and saw a large dome-shaped object hovering. He said two smaller spiked spheres rolled out, grabbed his trousers and dragged him toward it, and he passed out. He came to with torn trousers, grazes and a headache, and staggered home. Police recorded the case as an assault and found marks in the ground. It is often described as the only UFO event police have investigated as a crime. A marker now stands at the site.

## Manises — airliner diversion & Mirage intercept (1979)

- Date: 11 November 1979
- Place: Over Ibiza → Valencia-Manises Airport, Spain
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file; Reported electromagnetic effects (engines, instruments)
- Shape: Red lights on a collision course; truncated cone
- Witnesses: TAE crew, 109 passengers, controllers, Mirage pilot
- Duration: ~1.5 hours
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/manises-1979/

TAE flight JK-297 from Salzburg (via Palma) to Las Palmas saw red lights approach on a collision course near Ibiza and track the aircraft after it changed altitude. The captain diverted to Valencia — the first airliner diverted by a UFO. A Mirage F1 from Los Llanos then chased lights that accelerated away.

**Explanation:** Spanish Air Force files declassified in the 1990s did not confirm an anomalous object; researchers attribute the lights to refinery flare stacks and bright stars/planets.

## Cergy-Pontoise “abduction” (hoax) (1979)

- Date: 26 November 1979 (time approximate)
- Place: Cergy-Pontoise, Val-d’Oise, France
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Official government document or case file
- Shape: A light over the road that wrapped the car in fog and small flashing spheres
- Witnesses: Three young men; the police and gendarmes arrived after the call
- Duration: One week (the claimed disappearance)
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/cergy-pontoise-1979/

Before dawn on November 26, 1979, a young man telephoned the police at Cergy-Pontoise to say his friend had been “abducted by a UFO”. Three friends said they had been loading jeans to sell at a market when a light appeared over the road; the driver went towards it, it wrapped the car in fog and small flashing spheres, and when the fog cleared he was gone. Seven police officers and gendarmes searched; the story became national news. The missing man reappeared at a friend’s flat on December 3, with a journalist present, saying he had woken in a cabbage field. GEPAN’s technical note found that the witnesses’ accounts diverged from the start, that a blood test gave no sign of time in weightlessness, and that cabbages said to have been dried by the light had been left to rot as fertiliser by their owner. GEIPAN classes the affair as a hoax.

**Explanation:** A hoax. GEIPAN, which reviewed the police and gendarmerie inquiry and its own analyses, calls it “a hoax whose course discredits the scientific work”; one of the friends is reported to have admitted years later that he made the story up.

Sources:
- [GEIPAN case 1979-11-00685, Cergy-Pontoise (in French)](https://www.cnes-geipan.fr/fr/cas/1979-11-00685)
- [Sud-Ouest, November 29, 1979 (translated press archive)](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/press/sudouest29nov1979.htm)

## La Joya air base pursuit (1980)

- Date: 11 April 1980
- Place: La Joya air base, Arequipa, Peru
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Military witnesses; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Large balloon-shaped object
- Witnesses: Lt Oscar Santa María Huertas; some 1,800 people at the base
- Duration: About 22 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/la-joya-1980/

On the morning of April 11, 1980 about 1,800 people at the La Joya base saw a large, balloon-shaped object hanging still at around 500 metres. Lt Oscar Santa María Huertas, 23, took off in a Sukhoi Su-22 and fired 64 rounds at it without effect. He reported that it climbed away at up to 950 km/h, reaching about 19,200 metres, and stopped so suddenly that he had to swerve to avoid it. Peruvian army radar was said to show only his aircraft, while operators saw the object by eye. The engagement is said to have lasted 22 minutes, until his fuel ran low. The Peruvian Air Force kept the matter classified for decades; U.S. defence documents titled “UFO sighted in Peru” have since been released.

**Explanation:** Peru’s air force kept the case quiet for decades; no explanation has been published. Peru has since set up an office (now DIFAA) for aerial anomalies, and U.S. documents on the case were later released.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia (es) — Incidente ovni de La Joya](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incidente_ovni_de_la_Joya_-_Arequipa)

## Todmorden — PC Alan Godfrey (1980)

- Date: 29 November 1980
- Place: Burnley Road, Todmorden, West Yorkshire (United Kingdom)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Police witnesses; Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil)
- Shape: Diamond-shaped object hovering over the road
- Witnesses: PC Alan Godfrey; other officers saw a light that night
- Duration: Minutes; ~15 minutes unaccounted for
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/todmorden-godfrey-1980/

Before dawn, PC Alan Godfrey was driving his patrol car along Burnley Road looking for missing cattle when he found a large, diamond-shaped object hovering about 5 ft above the road, blocking it. He sketched it from the car. The next thing he knew, he was farther down the road and some time had passed. He said the road surface under the object was dry though the rest was wet. Other officers reported a light in the sky that night. Later hypnosis sessions produced an abduction account.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — UFO sightings in the United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO_sightings_in_the_United_Kingdom)

## Rendlesham Forest (1980)

- Date: 26 December 1980
- Place: Rendlesham Forest, outside RAF Woodbridge, Suffolk (United Kingdom)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Military witnesses; Official government document or case file; Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Audio recording / radio transcript
- Shape: Metallic lit object in the forest; star-like lights
- Witnesses: USAF security police; Lt. Col. Charles Halt
- Duration: Two nights
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/rendlesham-1980/

USAF security patrols at the east gate of RAF Woodbridge saw lights descend into the forest and went in to investigate. Two nights later deputy base commander Lt. Col. Charles Halt led a team that took radiation readings at three ground depressions and recorded his observations on a micro-cassette. His memo to the MoD is one of the most famous UFO documents in Britain.

**Explanation:** The Ministry of Defence found no threat and did not investigate further. Skeptics attribute the lights to a fireball, the Orford Ness lighthouse (visible through the trees in the same direction) and bright stars.

Sources:
- [The National Archives (UK) — MoD UFO files](https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/help-with-your-research/research-guides/ufos/)

## Cash–Landrum incident (1980)

- Date: 29 December 1980
- Place: FM 1485 near Huffman, Texas (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Documented physiological effects; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Diamond-shaped object venting flame; escorted by ~23 helicopters
- Witnesses: Betty Cash, Vickie & Colby Landrum; other motorists
- Duration: ~20 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/cash-landrum-1980/

Driving home through the pine woods north-east of Houston, Betty Cash and Vickie Landrum with her grandson said a blazing diamond-shaped object hovered over the road, radiating heat. As it rose, they counted about two dozen helicopters, many resembling CH-47 Chinooks. All three reported injuries afterwards, and they sued the U.S. government.

**Explanation:** Army and Air Force inquiries found no helicopters or craft that matched; the witnesses’ lawsuit against the U.S. government was dismissed in 1986. Skeptics question the medical and helicopter claims.

## Trans-en-Provence landing trace (1981)

- Date: 8 January 1981
- Place: Trans-en-Provence, Var (France)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Landing / trace case
- Evidence: Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Official government document or case file
- Shape: Lead-grey disc, two stacked saucers
- Witnesses: Renato Nicolaï
- Duration: Under a minute
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/trans-en-provence-1981/

Renato Nicolaï heard a whistle and saw an object land briefly on his terrace and fly off. The Gendarmerie took samples within a day; GEPAN’s laboratory analysis of the 2.4 m circular mark reported soil heated to 300–600 °C and chlorophyll changes in alfalfa leaves.

**Explanation:** The French government’s GEPAN (now GEIPAN, part of CNES) analysed soil and plant samples and reported heating and biochemical changes it could not attribute to a known cause. Skeptics suggest a vehicle or the witness.

Sources:
- [GEIPAN — French government UAP case archive (CNES)](https://www.cnes-geipan.fr/)

## The spiral over south-west China (1981)

- Date: 24 July 1981
- Place: Sichuan and Yunnan, and across south-west, north-west and south-central China
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: A star-like point that brightened and grew a spinning, silver, spiral-shaped band of light
- Witnesses: Very many people across several provinces; the Hangtian article claims ten million
- Duration: Six or seven minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/china-spiral-1981/

At 10:38 p.m. on July 24, 1981, on a clear, moonless night, people across Sichuan, Yunnan, Gansu and neighbouring provinces saw a bright, star-like point grow brighter, begin to oscillate and develop a cloud-like band of light that turned into a huge silver spiral, spinning as it crossed the sky slowly from east to west. It was in view for six or seven minutes. The sighting started a nationwide craze for UFOs in the newly opened China; the U.S. Air Force’s Foreign Technology Division translated a Hangtian article about it, “UFO incident causes sensation throughout half of China”, which weighed a meteor, an aircraft and a flying saucer. Liu Yan, the Purple Mountain Observatory astronomer who handled many of the letters the public sent about UFOs in the 1980s, made it the subject of his first article on them and concluded it was man-made.

**Explanation:** Newspapers first quoted astronomers blaming a meteor shower; the astronomer Liu Yan of the Purple Mountain Observatory, who analysed the eyewitness reports, concluded it was a man-made object about 650 km up, and an article in the space magazine Hangtian put it at about 500 km and rejected the meteor idea. A slowly turning spiral of light seen from half a country is what a rocket stage venting propellant in sunlight looks like (compare the Norwegian and Australian spirals), but no launch has been matched to this one.

Sources:
- [“UFO incident causes sensation throughout half of China” (FTD translation, DTIC ADA133326)](https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/FOID/Reading%20Room/UFOsandUAPs/ADA133326_UFOsandUAPs.pdf)
- [The Black Vault — the translated Hangtian article](https://www.theblackvault.com/casefiles/?p=2457)
- [Sixth Tone — The astronomer who calmed China’s UFO craze](https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1012934)

## Hannah McRoberts’ photograph — Vancouver Island (1981)

- Date: 8 October 1981 (time approximate)
- Place: A provincial park by the Eve River bridge on Highway 19, near Kelsey Bay, Vancouver Island, British Columbia (Canada)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs
- Shape: A sharply focused, domed disc against clear blue sky above a mountain peak
- Witnesses: None saw the object; the photographer, Hannah McRoberts, her husband and daughter were present
- Duration: One frame of 35 mm colour film
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/mcroberts-1981/

At about 11 a.m. on October 8, 1981, Hannah McRoberts photographed a mountain peak from a provincial park off Highway 19 near Kelsey Bay, on the north-east coast of Vancouver Island, while travelling with her husband and young daughter. Nobody noticed anything in the sky. When the film was developed days later, one frame showed a sharply focused, dark, domed disc above the peak. Richard Haines, a perception scientist at NASA Ames, examined the original negative with micro-densitometry and computer enhancement, visited the site and interviewed the family; he found no evidence of a hoax, concluded the object was three-dimensional and at least 30 feet away, and presented the photograph to the 1997 Sturrock panel on UFO evidence. It is still one of the most reproduced UFO photographs, and one of the most argued over.

**Explanation:** The NASA scientist Richard Haines examined the negative in 1987 and found no sign of tampering or a support thread; his measurements put the disc at least 30 feet from the camera, and interviews and a site survey supported the family’s account. Because nobody saw the object, a thrown object (a Frisbee, a hubcap or a pan lid have been suggested) cannot be ruled out, and later re-analyses from prints rather than the negative leave the case open.

Sources:
- [Patrick Gross — the McRoberts photograph and Haines’s analysis](https://ufology.patrickgross.org/htm/picamaca2.htm)
- [Metabunk — Hannah McRoberts’ 1981 UFO revisited](https://www.metabunk.org/threads/hannah-mcroberts-1981-ufo-revisited.10940/)

## Brest-Guipavas airport — the fireball by the runway (1981)

- Date: 22 November 1981
- Place: Brest-Guipavas airport, Finistère (France)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: A red-orange ball, low on the horizon, that seemed to drop into a field by the runway
- Witnesses: Seven people in four independent groups: joggers, airport firefighters and a man waiting for a bus
- Duration: Seconds (15 s or less, by most accounts)
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/guipavas-1981/

At about 7:55 on the morning of November 22, 1981, in early light, people in four separate groups near Brest-Guipavas airport saw a red-orange ball low over the horizon that seemed to fall into a field beside a runway and vanish; some saw sparks or a short trail. The airport’s firefighters, who watched it come down as if landing, alerted the control tower. The gendarmes, contacted the next day by the air traffic controller, took eight statements and searched; no trace was found. GEPAN’s original file recorded a radar echo at the time, which made the case a class D, unexplained. GEIPAN’s re-examination found that the radar centre had treated the echoes as insignificant and that the controllers had seen nothing abnormal, and reclassified it B: a meteoroid on a grazing path, seen almost head-on.

**Explanation:** GEIPAN class B: probably a meteoroid entering the atmosphere on a shallow path, seen nearly head-on, which explains the red-orange ball, the short, slow descent and the sudden disappearance. A radar “spot” first cited in the file was not supported: the controllers noted nothing abnormal.

Sources:
- [GEIPAN case 1981-11-00900, Guipavas (in French)](https://www.cnes-geipan.fr/fr/cas/1981-11-00900)

## Trancrainville — gendarmes on the A10 and the lit-up ground (1982)

- Date: 23 January 1982
- Place: A10 motorway near Trancrainville, Eure-et-Loir, north of Orléans (France)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Police witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: An indistinct bright mass in the sky, and a strongly lit patch on the ground
- Witnesses: Two gendarmes of the motorway patrol
- Duration: About 20 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/trancrainville-1982/

Between 4:35 and 4:55 a.m. on January 23, 1982, two gendarmes of the motorway patrol, driving south on the A10, saw an indistinct bright mass in the sky and a strongly lit area on the ground beneath it, which moved across pylons and hangars. They followed it for about 30 km, driving and stopping, losing and finding it again, and heard nothing even with the engine off; at the end only a glow remained to the east over the trees. The Orléans air base, 7 km away, had nothing flying and its radar had been off since the evening before, and the motorway operator’s staff had seen nothing. Re-examining the case, GEIPAN rejected planets (they cannot light the ground) and judged a helicopter with a searchlight above the cloud, then at 1,200–1,500 m, too unlikely for the equipment of the time. It is class D, unexplained, with the caveat that no field interview could be made.

Sources:
- [GEIPAN case 1982-01-00913, Trancrainville (in French)](https://www.cnes-geipan.fr/fr/cas/1982-01-00913)

## VASP flight 169 — the light that paced a Boeing 727 (1982)

- Date: 8 February 1982
- Place: Night flight from Fortaleza to Rio de Janeiro, first seen near Petrolina, Pernambuco (Brazil)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Radar tracking
- Shape: A bright light changing from red to orange, with a white and bluish centre
- Witnesses: Captain Gérson Maciel de Britto, his co-pilot and many passengers; crews of two other airliners
- Duration: About two hours
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/vasp-169-1982/

VASP’s night flight 169, a Boeing 727 (PP-SNG) under Captain Gérson Maciel de Britto, left Fortaleza at 01:50 on February 8, 1982 for Rio de Janeiro. About half an hour later, near Petrolina, the captain saw a light approach on the left and pace the aircraft. It changed colour between red and orange around a white and bluish centre, seemed to move above and below the airliner, and stayed with it past Belo Horizonte; at 31,000 ft the crew said a bluish light filled the cabin. Britto called the air-traffic and air-defence centre CINDACTA in Brasília, which had no traffic there, dimmed his lights and flashed his landing lights at it, and woke the passengers; one compared it to a mercury street lamp. CINDACTA later said its radar showed a return about eight miles from the aircraft, and crews of a Transbrasil and an Aerolíneas Argentinas flight reported seeing something. The light was lost in cloud over the Serra do Mar a few minutes before landing at Galeão. The case was examined in the Journal of Scientific Exploration in 2014, which concluded that the “object” was Venus, very bright in the eastern pre-dawn sky.

**Explanation:** A study in the Journal of Scientific Exploration (2014) concluded the light was the planet Venus, rising brilliantly before dawn and possibly distorted by an atmospheric mirage. The captain rejected that, saying he knew Venus and the Moon; a radar return the air-traffic centre reported near the airliner has never been documented in detail.

Sources:
- [The VASP-169 flight Brazilian episode revisited — Journal of Scientific Exploration 27(4) (PhilArchive record)](https://philarchive.org/rec/DASUAP)
- [Patrick Gross — VASP 169, February 8, 1982](https://ufology.patrickgross.org/htm/pp-sng1982.htm)

## Morenão stadium sighting (1982)

- Date: 6 March 1982 (time approximate)
- Place: Estádio Morenão, Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul (Brazil)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Unidentified lights
- Witnesses: More than 24,000 spectators, players and the referee
- Duration: Minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/morenao-stadium-1982/

During a Brazilian championship match between Operário and Vasco da Gama, a crowd of more than 24,000 saw unidentified objects over the stadium. Players, including Cocada, and referee José de Assis Aragão described them. Among the spectators was Ademar José Gevaerd, who went on to become one of Brazil's best-known UFO researchers.

Sources:
