## Hessdalen lights (1984)

- Date: 1 February 1984 (time approximate)
- Place: Hessdalen valley, Norway
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Recurring lights
- Evidence: Photographs; Video / film footage; Radar tracking; Infrared or other sensor data; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: White, yellow or red floating lights
- Witnesses: Residents and scientists
- Duration: Ongoing since ~1981
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/hessdalen-lights/

Lights have appeared over the 12-km Hessdalen valley since at least the early 1980s, peaking at up to 20 per week in 1981–84. Unusually, they have been measured: radar, spectra, magnetometers and a permanent camera station have recorded them, but their cause is still debated.

**Explanation:** Studied since 1983 by Project Hessdalen with an automated measurement station; hypotheses include combustion of dust from the valley’s ores, plasma, and piezoelectric effects.

## Hudson Valley "Westchester boomerang" (1984)

- Date: 24 July 1984 (time approximate)
- Place: Brewster, Putnam County, New York (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Video / film footage; Many independent witnesses; Police witnesses
- Shape: V / boomerang of coloured lights
- Witnesses: Thousands across Westchester, Putnam, Dutchess and Fairfield counties
- Duration: Recurring, 1983–1984
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/hudson-valley-1983/

For over a year residents of the Hudson Valley reported a silent boomerang or V of bright lights, sometimes "the size of a football field". Guards at the Indian Point nuclear plant reportedly saw it in June and July 1984, and a Brewster resident videotaped the lights on 24 July.

**Explanation:** State police and the New York Power Authority attributed the sightings to pilots flying Cessna 152s in tight formation from Stormville Airport with coloured lights — a hoax the pilots reportedly enjoyed.

## Aeroflot Tu-134 over Minsk — the light that became a cloud (1984)

- Date: 7 September 1984 (time approximate)
- Place: Over Minsk, Byelorussian SSR, on the flight to Tallinn (Belarus)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Radar tracking; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: A yellow light that threw out rays, became concentric circles and then a green cloud
- Witnesses: Captain Igor Cherkashin and co-pilot Gennady Lazurin of an Aeroflot Tu-134, and the crew of a second airliner
- Duration: Several minutes; the cloud is said to have stayed with the aircraft for hundreds of kilometres
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/minsk-aeroflot-1984/

At about 4 a.m. on September 7, 1984, the crew of an Aeroflot Tu-134 flying from Tbilisi via Rostov to Tallinn saw a bright yellow light appear to their right over Byelorussia. It threw out beams strong enough, by one account, to light up the houses and roads below, changed into concentric circles and then into a glowing green cloud that seemed to follow the airliner. Co-pilot Gennady Lazurin sketched it, and Captain Igor Cherkashin called air traffic control, which reported a “double” return on radar; a second airliner flying the opposite way also saw it. The newspaper Trud published the story in early 1985, a rare UFO report in the Soviet press. Rumours that crew members of the second aircraft later died of illnesses caused by the encounter have never been substantiated. Western analysts matched the sketches to the plume of a missile launched that night.

**Explanation:** Western analysts tied it to a Soviet missile launch that night, whose rising plume and glowing exhaust cloud look much like the crew’s sketches: Jonathan McDowell’s launch catalogue lists a submarine-launched R-29R test on September 7, 1984, with a note (after James Oberg) naming it as the source of the sighting. The Soviet army newspaper Krasnaya Zvezda suggested light refracted by floating space debris.

Sources:
- [Le Figaro, 28 February 1985, reporting Trud (transcribed by Patrick Gross)](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/press/lefigaro28feb1985.htm)
- [PBS, Life Beyond Earth — Minsk, U.S.S.R. (September 7, 1984)](https://www.pbs.org/lifebeyondearth/listening/minskpop.html)
- [Jonathan McDowell — General Catalog of Artificial Space Objects (launch list)](https://planet4589.org/space/gcat/)
- [Wikipedia — UFO sightings in Belarus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO_sightings_in_Belarus)

## Dalnegorsk “Height 611” crash (1986)

- Date: 29 January 1986
- Place: Dalnegorsk, Primorsky Krai, Russia
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Landing / trace case
- Evidence: Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Reddish sphere about 3 m across
- Witnesses: Residents of Dalnegorsk
- Duration: A few minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/dalnegorsk-1986/

On the evening of January 29, 1986 residents of the mining town of Dalnegorsk saw a reddish, silent sphere about three metres across flying from the south-east at some 700–800 metres, at about 15 m/s. It crossed part of the town and came down on Izvestkovaya mountain, known as Height 611, burning on the slope. Investigators reported tiny metallic droplets 2–5 mm across, and fibres in a tangle of metal, quartz and gold-coloured threads. In Russia it is often called the best-documented UFO crash, although the technical findings come mainly from the group that investigated it.

**Explanation:** Ball lightning and other plasma phenomena have been proposed. The reports of unusual metal fragments come mostly from the investigating group and have not been independently confirmed.

Sources:
- [Roswell UFO Museum — The Height 611 UFO incident](https://www.roswellufomuseum.com/post/the-height-611-ufo-incident)

## Brazil’s "Official UFO Night" (1986)

- Date: 19 May 1986
- Place: São José dos Campos – Rio de Janeiro – Goiás (Brazil)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Red, white and green lights; 21 radar plots
- Witnesses: Controllers, F-5E and Mirage pilots, Embraer founder Ozires Silva
- Duration: ~5 hours
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/brazil-ufo-night-1986/

Controllers at São José dos Campos and radar across south-east Brazil tracked about 21 unknown contacts. Embraer’s founder, flying in, saw red lights; the Air Force scrambled F-5Es from Santa Cruz and Mirage IIIs from Anápolis. Pilots reported lights that kept their distance and targets that appeared behind them.

**Explanation:** The Air Force commander said "we have no explanation". The report declassified in 2009 described objects with speeds from hovering to supersonic and 90° turns.

## Torpo film (1986)

- Date: 13 July 1986 (time approximate)
- Place: Mountain farm near Torpo, Hallingdal (Norway)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Video / film footage; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Two bright objects, one flashing and throwing sparks
- Witnesses: A family and friends at a mountain farm
- Duration: Minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/torpo-1986/

A couple at a mountain farm near Torpo, with their son and friends, watched two bright objects in the evening sky, one moving dramatically, flashing and throwing off sparks. The husband filmed them. Ground Saucer Watch found no sign of a hoax, but said the apparent motion could come from camera shake and that the lack of reference points made the film inconclusive.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — UFO sightings in Norway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UFO_sightings_in_Norway)

## Japan Air Lines Flight 1628 (1986)

- Date: 17 November 1986
- Place: Over north-east Alaska (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Two small lights and a huge "mothership"
- Witnesses: Capt. Kenji Terauchi and crew
- Duration: ~50 minutes, ~400 miles
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/jal-1628-1986/

A JAL Boeing 747 freighter on the Reykjavík–Anchorage leg reported three objects pacing it at 35,000 ft, including one Terauchi described as enormous. Anchorage controllers reported returns near the aircraft; the objects stayed with the plane through turns and descents until near Talkeetna.

**Explanation:** The FAA’s radar returns were later dismissed as clutter / a split image; Philip Klass argued the crew saw Jupiter and Mars. The FAA found the crew professional and rational.

## Gulf Breeze photographs (1987)

- Date: 11 November 1987 (time approximate)
- Place: Gulf Breeze, Florida (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs; Video / film footage; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Cylindrical craft with a ring of portholes and a glowing base
- Witnesses: Ed Walters; other residents later came forward
- Duration: Six months
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/gulf-breeze-1987/

Contractor Ed Walters gave the Gulf Breeze Sentinel five Polaroids of a glowing craft he said hovered near his home. Over six months he produced dozens more photos and video, and described being hit by a blue beam and seeing aliens. Researchers such as Bruce Maccabee backed the photos, and other residents reported sightings. After the model was found in 1990 and a reporter recreated the pictures, the case became a textbook example of a UFO photo hoax.

**Explanation:** Considered a hoax. In 1990 the new owners of Ed Walters's former house found a styrofoam model UFO in the attic that a reporter used to reproduce the photos almost exactly. A local teenager also said he had helped fake them. Walters said the model was planted.

## Ilkley Moor photograph (1987)

- Date: 1 December 1987 (time approximate)
- Place: Ilkley Moor, West Yorkshire, England (United Kingdom)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs
- Shape: Small green humanoid; two-part silver craft
- Witnesses: Philip Spencer, a retired police officer (a pseudonym)
- Duration: Minutes; about two hours unaccounted for
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/ilkley-moor-1987/

On the morning of December 1, 1987 Philip Spencer, a retired police officer, was walking across Ilkley Moor, between Ilkley and Keighley, when he said he met a small dark-green figure about 1.2 metres tall, with a large head and long thin arms. He took one photograph before it ran off, then saw a whitish, two-part craft rise from the moor with a loud hum. About two hours were missing from his journey, and his compass pointed the wrong way. A wildlife photographer said the figure matched no known animal and Kodak found no signs of tampering, but the US Navy optics specialist Bruce Maccabee called the image too grainy to test. Under hypnosis in March 1988 his story changed to one of being taken aboard and examined.

**Explanation:** Critics say the blurry photograph could show a person or a cardboard cutout, and ask why no picture of the craft was taken. Kodak experts found no sign of tampering, but the image is too grainy for firm conclusions, and the account changed under hypnosis.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — Ilkley Moor UFO incident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilkley_Moor_UFO_incident)
- [UFOs at close sight — the Ilkley Moor encounter, 1987](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/htm/ilkleymoor.htm)

## Knowles family encounter (1988)

- Date: 20 January 1988
- Place: Nullarbor Plain, between Madura and Mundrabilla, Western Australia
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil)
- Shape: Large glowing ball
- Witnesses: Faye Knowles and her sons Patrick, Sean and Wayne
- Duration: About 90 minutes (as told)
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/mundrabilla-1988/

In the early hours of January 20, 1988, the Knowles family were driving across the Nullarbor Plain in their station wagon when a bright light appeared ahead. They said a large glowing object pursued the car for a long time and finally came down on the roof; the car seemed to be lifted off the road, and the engine and voices changed as if time were slowing. Mrs Knowles said she reached out of the rear window, felt something soft and warm on the roof, and found her hand covered in black dust. When the car dropped back onto the road a rear tyre burst. The family reported it at Mundrabilla. It is one of Australia’s best-known close-encounter stories.

**Explanation:** No explanation has been established. The account rests on the four family members’ testimony and the physical details they described, and has been widely reported in Australia.

Sources:
- [UFO Evidence — Knowles family encounter, Mundrabilla](http://www.ufoevidence.org/cases/case1090.htm)

On Christmas Day 1988 a silver object crossed the Villa Urquiza neighbourhood of Buenos Aires, watched by thousands of people. The city airport reported an object heading west toward Avenida General Paz. It is often called Argentina's most spectacular UFO sighting.

## Kapustin Yar — the KGB file on a night of lights over a missile depot (1989)

- Date: 28 July 1989
- Place: Military sites 30–45 km from Kapustin Yar, Astrakhan oblast (Russia)
- Status: UNASSESSED — Released without an official determination
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Military witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: A disc 4–5 m across with a dome, glowing dim green, with a bright flashing light and a beam
- Witnesses: Officers and soldiers of military units near Kapustin Yar, among them Ensign V. N. Voloshin, Capt. Chernikov and Sr Lt Klimenko
- Duration: About three and a half hours
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/kapustin-yar-1989/

Between 22:10 on July 28 and 01:30 on July 29, 1989, soldiers and officers at military sites 30 to 45 km from the Kapustin Yar missile range, described in the reports as a transmission centre and a rocket-weapons depot, reported unidentified objects. At the depot, Ensign Valery Voloshin and a private watched through binoculars for about two hours as a disc some 4–5 m across with a dome, glowing a dim phosphorescent green, hovered 20 to 70 m above the warehouses, flashed a bright light and swept a beam, moved silently in sudden jerks, and finally left towards Akhtubinsk. Other officers described flashes like electric welding, a “flying plate” or a cigar-shaped object, and an aircraft was said to have been sent up but kept at a distance. The written statements, with unit names blacked out, were among 124 pages of military and civilian reports that the KGB passed in October 1991 to Pavel Popovich, president of a Soviet ufological association; Komsomolskaya Pravda published them in 2003. They are first-hand military reports, but nothing shows that anyone examined them.

**Explanation:** The reports are in a package of 124 pages that the KGB sent to the cosmonaut Pavel Popovich in October 1991, with a covering letter saying that the KGB did not study UFO reports but passed on what it received. No investigation or conclusion accompanies them, and the original file was later said to have gone missing.

Sources:
- [Komsomolskaya Pravda, 4 February 2003: the KGB reports (translated by Patrick Gross)](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/htm/kp05022003.htm)

## Voronezh park landing (1989)

- Date: 27 September 1989
- Place: Voronezh, RSFSR (Russia)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil)

TASS reported that children in a Voronezh park saw a large red ball land and tall beings emerge. Soviet reporting of the case — unusual at the time — made headlines worldwide.

**Explanation:** Reported by the Soviet news agency TASS; later widely regarded as a children’s story amplified by the press.

## Pereslavl-Zalessky — the Soviet air defence report (1990)

- Date: 21 March 1990
- Place: Pereslavl-Zalessky region, north-east of Moscow (Russia)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Military witnesses; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: A disc 100–200 m across with two pulsing lights on its sides
- Witnesses: More than 100 observers reported by air-defence units of the Moscow Military District; interceptor pilots Lt Col A. A. Semenchenko and others; radar crews
- Duration: Evening into the night
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/pereslavl-zalessky-1990/

On the night of March 21, 1990, air-defence units of the Moscow Military District reported more than 100 visual sightings of an object near Pereslavl-Zalessky. At 21:38 Lt Col A. A. Semenchenko was scrambled to identify a target at about 2,000 m; he saw two flashing white lights and a dim silhouette against the lights of the town, and the target did not answer his identification interrogation. Other pilots and radar posts gave times, bearings and distances; one ground radar post reported a fast-moving shining object with red lights, followed by another with white lights. In Rabochaya Tribuna on April 19, Colonel General Igor Maltsev, chief of the Main Staff of the Soviet Air Defence Forces, published excerpts: a disc 100 to 200 m across with two pulsing lights, flying silently between 1,000 and 7,000 m, at two to three times the speed of a modern fighter, rotating and hovering. Maltsev said he was “not a specialist on UFOs” and could only correlate the data. It was the first time a Soviet commander of that rank described such a case in public; the underlying reports have not been released, and no explanation was published.

Sources:
- [New York Tribune, 21 June 1990: Soviet general describes UFO (transcribed by Patrick Gross)](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/press/nytribune21jun1990.htm)
- [Arizona Republic, 15 July 1990: Soviet air defence and UFOs (transcribed by Patrick Gross)](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/press/arizonarepublic15jul1990.htm)

## Belgian UFO wave — F-16 intercepts (1990)

- Date: 30 March 1990
- Place: Brussels – Wavre – Gembloux, Belgium
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Military witnesses; Police witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Dark triangle with bright corner lights
- Witnesses: ~13,500 reports in the wave; gendarmes; Air Force
- Duration: Wave: Nov 1989 – Apr 1990
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/belgian-wave-1990/

Beginning with a sighting by two gendarmes at Eupen on 29 November 1989, thousands of Belgians reported large, slow triangles with lights. On the night of 30–31 March 1990, after ground and radar reports, two Belgian Air Force F-16s from Beauvechain made nine interception attempts and obtained brief radar locks; the Air Force published its report openly.

**Explanation:** The Belgian Air Force report left the radar contacts unexplained; critics attribute the F-16 lock-ons to the other fighter and to Bragg scattering. The famous Petit-Rechain triangle photo was admitted to be a hoax in 2011.

## Calvine photograph (1990)

- Date: 4 August 1990
- Place: Moors above Calvine, Perthshire (United Kingdom)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Large diamond hovering; a Harrier jet nearby
- Witnesses: Two unidentified walkers
- Duration: ~10 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/calvine-1990/

Two men walking above Calvine photographed a large, silent diamond-shaped object hovering while a military jet flew past. Their negatives went from the Daily Record to the Ministry of Defence and vanished. A surviving print surfaced in 2022 and was published worldwide.

**Explanation:** The MoD never explained it; proposed explanations include a rock reflected in water and a hoax. The photographers have never been identified.

Sources:

## The “immense triangle” over France — a Proton re-entry (1990)

- Date: 5 November 1990 (time approximate)
- Place: From the Bay of Biscay across France to Alsace
- Status: IDENTIFIED — Object positively identified
- Kind: Tracked object event
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Three main lights in a group, read by many as an immense luminous triangle, with sparks and smoke trailing
- Witnesses: Thousands, including CNES astronaut Jean-Pierre Haigneré and balloon technicians at Aire-sur-Adour
- Duration: A minute or two
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/proton-reentry-france-1990/

At about 7 p.m. on November 5, 1990, a slow procession of bright lights crossed France from the Bay of Biscay to Alsace. Gendarmerie stations were flooded with calls, and for more than a week SEPRA, the CNES unit then in charge, answered witnesses describing “an immense luminous triangle”; the astronaut Jean-Pierre Haigneré was among them, and technicians at the CNES balloon base at Aire-sur-Adour held a launch to watch. On November 8 NASA identified the re-entry of object 20925, the third stage of the Proton rocket that had put the Gorizont 21 satellite into orbit, and CNES confirmed its track across France. The case, which fell in the middle of the Belgian wave, is a standard example of how a known re-entry is reported as a structured craft.

**Explanation:** The re-entry of the third stage of the Soviet Proton rocket that launched Gorizont 21 (catalogue object 20925, 1990-094C), identified by NASA on November 8 and confirmed by CNES orbit specialists; GEIPAN classes the case A, fully explained.

Sources:
- [GEIPAN case 1990-11-01225, re-entry of a Proton stage (in French)](https://www.cnes-geipan.fr/fr/cas/1990-11-01225)
- [ALSACAT — witness reports from Alsace, November 5, 1990](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/alsacat/1990-11-05-rixheim.htm)

## Montreal — lights over the Bonaventure Hotel (1990)

- Date: 7 November 1990
- Place: Hôtel Bonaventure, downtown Montreal, Quebec (Canada)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Police witnesses
- Shape: Ring of 8–10 bright lights; a huge round form
- Witnesses: Hotel guests and staff, passers-by, police officers
- Duration: 3 hours
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/montreal-bonaventure-1990/

From 7:20 to 10:20 p.m., people on the rooftop pool deck of the Bonaventure Hotel and in the streets below watched 8 to 10 lights hanging in a circle above them, sending down bright white rays. Some described a huge round object behind the lights. Police officers attended, and the next day La Presse reported the sighting. It drifted slowly north and was never identified.

Sources:

## Alitalia MD-80 near miss over Kent (1991)

- Date: 21 April 1991 (time approximate)
- Place: Near Lydd, Kent, England (United Kingdom)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Radar tracking; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Brown, missile-shaped object
- Witnesses: Capt. Achille Zaghetti, with 57 people aboard
- Duration: Seconds
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/alitalia-lydd-1991/

At about 8 p.m. on April 21, 1991, an Alitalia MD-80 flying from Milan to Heathrow with 57 people aboard was at 22,000 feet over the army ranges at Lydd, on the Kent coast, when Capt. Achille Zaghetti saw a brown, missile-shaped object pass about 1,000 feet above the airliner and shouted “Look out, look out”. The London control centre told him it had an unknown target on radar 10 nautical miles behind him. The Ministry of Defence and the Civil Aviation Authority investigated as an airmiss, ruled out a missile, a weather balloon and a rocket, and closed the case unsolved.

**Explanation:** The Civil Aviation Authority and the Ministry of Defence looked at missiles, weather balloons and rockets and ruled each one out, then closed the inquiry without an answer. The files were released by the National Archives in October 2008.

Sources:
- [Irish Examiner — Pilot reported “missile” near miss, MoD files show (2008)](https://www.irishexaminer.com/world/arid-30382660.html)

## Mexico City eclipse videos (1991)

- Date: 11 July 1991
- Place: Mexico City, Mexico
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Video / film footage; Photographs; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Metallic disc or bright point, sometimes with a wavy haze
- Witnesses: Dozens of video and photo recordings by different people
- Duration: Minutes, during totality
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/mexico-city-eclipse-1991/

Millions in Mexico watched the total solar eclipse of July 11, 1991, with totality in Mexico City at 13:24 and lasting more than six minutes. At least 16 photographers and videographers recorded a bright, disc-like object near the Sun in the sky, some with a wavy trail of haze behind it. The sightings were widely seen on television and the case is a classic in Mexican ufology. Astronomers pointed out that the darkness of totality shows Venus, which stood a few degrees from the star Regulus, and that other planets also come into view, which fits many of the videos but not necessarily the apparent motion some of them show.

**Explanation:** Astronomers identified the brightest object as Venus (with Mars and Regulus nearby), made visible by the darkness of totality. Reflections in glass, camera artefacts and hoaxes account for others; not every video has been explained.

Sources:
- [Tim Printy — The July 11, 1991 Mexico City UFOs](https://astronomyufo.com/UFO/mexico.htm)

## Crop circles — Doug Bower and Dave Chorley own up (1991)

- Date: 9 September 1991 (time approximate)
- Place: The fields of Hampshire and Wiltshire; their first circles near Cheesefoot Head, Winchester (United Kingdom)
- Status: IDENTIFIED — Object positively identified
- Kind: Landing / trace case
- Evidence: Physical traces (ground marks, debris, soil); Photographs
- Shape: Circles of flattened cereal crop, later rings and complex patterns
- Witnesses: Doug Bower and Dave Chorley, and the journalists they demonstrated to
- Duration: 1978–1991
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/crop-circles-bower-chorley-1991/

From the late 1970s, circles of flattened wheat and barley appeared each summer in the fields of southern England, especially Hampshire and Wiltshire. By the late 1980s they were a national story, explained as UFO landing marks (“saucer nests”), as plasma vortices by the meteorologist Terence Meaden, and as messages by a new class of “cerealogists”. In September 1991 two men from Southampton, Doug Bower and Dave Chorley, told the newspaper Today that they had made circles since 1978, inspired by the 1966 Tully “saucer nest” in Australia, starting near Cheesefoot Head, and claimed more than 200 of them. They showed their tools, a plank, a rope and a cap with a wire loop to keep a straight line, and made a circle for journalists that the cerealogist Pat Delgado then declared authentic. Not every circle since is theirs, but none has been shown to have any cause other than people.

**Explanation:** Made by people. Doug Bower and Dave Chorley showed how they had made circles since 1978 with a plank, rope and a cap with a wire sighting loop, made one for journalists that a leading “cerealogist” declared genuine, and inspired the teams who make the elaborate designs today.

Sources:
- [Wikipedia — Crop circle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crop_circle)
- [Interview with Dave Chorley, CBC radio, 9 September 1991 (transcribed by Patrick Gross)](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/htm/chorley01.htm)

## Cosford incident (1993)

- Date: 30 March 1993
- Place: RAF Cosford and RAF Shawbury, Shropshire (United Kingdom)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Military witnesses; Police witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Triangular craft; lights in formation
- Witnesses: Police officers, RAF personnel, members of the public
- Duration: About 5 hours
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/cosford-1993/

Over the night of March 30–31, 1993, police officers, RAF personnel and the public across England and Wales reported lights in formation and a large triangular craft. A patrol at RAF Cosford saw it pass over the base. At RAF Shawbury a meteorological officer described a huge craft moving slowly across the airfield and sweeping a light beam over the ground. The MoD's Nick Pope pressed the case internally, and the files were later released to The National Archives.

**Explanation:** Most of the evening reports matched the re-entry of the rocket body that had launched the Russian satellite Cosmos 2238. The MoD found no threat. Nick Pope, who investigated for the MoD, argued that later reports, including a meteorological officer's at RAF Shawbury, were never explained.

Sources:
- [The National Archives (UK) — MoD UFO files](https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/help-with-your-research/research-guides/ufos/)

## Air France 3532 — radar-visual over Coulommiers (1994)

- Date: 28 January 1994
- Place: Near Coulommiers, Seine-et-Marne, France
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Radar tracking; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Huge brown or dark-red disc or bell that seemed to change shape
- Witnesses: Capt. Jean-Charles Duboc, First Officer Valérie Chauffour and a chief steward
- Duration: About one minute
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/air-france-3532-1994/

At 13:14 on January 28, 1994, the crew of Air France flight 3532, an Airbus A320 from Nice to London, was cruising at about 11,900 metres near Coulommiers, east of Paris, when the chief steward and both pilots saw a huge object, like a brown bell or disc, off to the left. It seemed to change shape, stayed in view for about a minute and then vanished abruptly. Reims air traffic control had no traffic there, but the military radar at Cinq-Mars-la-Pile recorded a track for about 50 seconds that crossed the airliner’s path and disappeared at the same moment the crew lost sight of the object. The radar return and the crew’s description do not agree on distance or side, which is part of why the case remains open.

**Explanation:** GEIPAN, the French space agency’s UAP office, classes the case as unexplained after investigation. The military radar track is real but does not match the crew’s account closely: the crew saw a stationary object far off to the left, while the radar target was about a mile to the right and moving. Both vanished at the same moment.

Sources:
- [GEIPAN — case 1994-01-01345, Coulommiers](https://www.cnes-geipan.fr/fr/cas/1994-01-01345)
- [UFOs at close sight — Air France 3532, January 28, 1994](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/ufology/af3532rt.htm)

## Lake Michigan lights — 911 calls and a weather radar (1994)

- Date: 8 March 1994 (time approximate)
- Place: The Lake Michigan shore of Ottawa and Muskegon counties, Michigan (Grand Haven to Holland) (United States)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Radar-visual case
- Evidence: Radar tracking; Police witnesses; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Five or six round or cylindrical objects with red, green, blue and white lights, like flickering Christmas lights
- Witnesses: Dozens of residents who called 911, police officers, and the meteorologist on duty at the Muskegon weather office
- Duration: Hours
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/lake-michigan-1994/

On the night of March 8, 1994, dozens of people along the Lake Michigan shore of western Michigan called 911 about lights over the lake: five or six objects with red, green, blue and white lights that hovered and moved erratically. Police officers saw them too. A dispatcher called the National Weather Service office at Muskegon County Airport, and the meteorologist on duty, Jack Bushong, turned the office’s WSR-74C weather radar on the area and saw several returns where none should be, which he said moved fast and changed direction; he reported it to the National UFO Reporting Center. Days later the Weather Service played the radar down, saying it was built to see rain, not aircraft. Over the following weeks more than 300 people in 42 Michigan counties reported sightings; MUFON investigators interviewed dozens and found no explanation. Bushong kept his account for decades, and the case stays one of the better-documented police and radar cases of the 1990s.

Sources:
- [MLive — the 1994 Lake Michigan UFO sightings](https://www.mlive.com/news/us-world/2017/03/ufo_1994.html)
- [WWMT — the retired meteorologist’s account of the 1994 sightings](https://wwmt.com/news/local/retired-meteorologist-shares-his-account-of-1994-west-michigan-ufo-sightings)
- [Wikipedia — 1994 Michigan UFO event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Michigan_UFO_event)

## Ariel School, Ruwa (1994)

- Date: 16 September 1994
- Place: Ariel School, Ruwa, Zimbabwe
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Silver craft landing in scrub; small beings
- Witnesses: 62 pupils aged 5–12
- Duration: ~15 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/ariel-school-1994/

During morning break, 62 children said a silver craft landed in bush beside the playground and one or two small figures in black watched them. Their drawings were collected within days, and Harvard psychiatrist John Mack interviewed them.

**Explanation:** Skeptics suggest mass suggestion after a meteor/re-entry seen across southern Africa two days earlier; many former pupils still stand by their accounts.

## British Airways 5061 near miss over the Pennines (1995)

- Date: 6 January 1995
- Place: About 8 nautical miles south-east of Manchester Airport (United Kingdom)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Wedge-shaped object with small white lights and a black stripe
- Witnesses: Capt. Roger Wills and First Officer Mark Stuart
- Duration: About 2 seconds
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/ba5061-manchester-1995/

At 18:48 on January 6, 1995, British Airways flight 5061, a Boeing 737 from Milan with 60 passengers aboard, was descending through about 4,000 feet over the Pennines toward Manchester when both pilots saw a lighted object pass very close down the right side, going the other way. They described it as wedge-shaped, with small white lights and a black stripe; the first officer ducked as it went by. Nothing showed on radar. The Joint Airmiss Working Group studied the report and, unable to identify the object, called it “unassessable”.

**Explanation:** The Civil Aviation Authority’s Joint Airmiss Working Group could not identify the object and rated the airmiss “unassessable”. No other aircraft or balloon was found, and no radar return was seen.

Sources:

## America West Flight 564 over the Texas Panhandle (1995)

- Date: 25 May 1995 (time approximate)
- Place: Over Bovina, Texas, near the New Mexico border (United States)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Audio recording / radio transcript; Radar tracking
- Shape: A row of white lights flashing in sequence; a long, dark, cigar-shaped silhouette against lightning
- Witnesses: The crew of a Boeing 757: the first officer, the captain and a flight attendant; Albuquerque Center controllers
- Duration: Several minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/america-west-564-1995/

On the night of May 25, 1995, America West Flight 564, a Boeing 757 flying west at 39,000 ft from Tampa to Las Vegas, was passing over Bovina in the Texas Panhandle when the first officer, John Waller, and a flight attendant saw a row of bright white lights off to the right and below, flashing in sequence from left to right. When lightning lit the thunderclouds behind it, the crew saw a dark, wingless, cigar-shaped silhouette, which they estimated at 300 to 400 ft long, though its distance was unknown. Waller asked Albuquerque Center about traffic; the controllers had nothing on their radar and called NORAD, which reported a track that later proved to be a small aircraft with a faulty transponder. The next morning a controller said NORAD had tracked another target that stopped and accelerated repeatedly, but that was never confirmed. Walter Webb investigated for the Fund for UFO Research, interviewed the crew and the controllers and obtained the FAA tapes, and found no explanation; the SETI astronomer Seth Shostak later remarked that bright planets fool trained pilots, without analysing this case.

Sources:
- [The America West case: Walter Webb’s investigation (transcribed)](https://ufology.patrickgross.org/htm/texas95.htm)
- [The Black Vault — America West Flight 564 case file](https://www.theblackvault.com/casefiles/america-west-airlines-flight-564-ufo-case/)

## Bariloche — the blackout and Aerolíneas Argentinas 674 (1995)

- Date: 31 July 1995
- Place: San Carlos de Bariloche airport, Río Negro, Argentina
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Reported electromagnetic effects (engines, instruments)
- Shape: A light between white and amber, like a star but much larger; later described as green and white, about 30 m across
- Witnesses: Capt. Jorge Polanco, his crew and passengers; the tower chief, Daniel García; the crew of a Gendarmería Cheyenne
- Duration: 15–17 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/bariloche-1995/

At about 8:15 p.m. on July 31, 1995, Aerolíneas Argentinas flight 674, a Boeing 727 from Buenos Aires under Capt. Jorge Polanco, was coming in to land at Bariloche when the airport lost power, and then the whole city went dark as the airliner neared the runway, forcing a go-around. A light “between white and amber”, like a star but much larger and brighter, then flew on a parallel course about 100 metres from the plane. When the power came back the 727 climbed to 3,000 metres, descended and landed, and the light left at full speed toward the south-east. The tower chief and the crew of a Gendarmería Cheyenne flying 600 metres higher saw it too, and the tower’s instruments swung from one direction to another for no clear reason. Interviewed in 2026, Polanco said: “It pursued us, accompanied us for 17 minutes.”

**Explanation:** No explanation was found. Carlos Angueira, president of a local astronomy association, rejected a meteorite or a refraction, saying such things cannot “stop in the middle of the sky”. The case drew new attention in 2026, when it appeared among the Latin American incidents in UAP files released by the Pentagon.

Sources:
- [Infobae — “It pursued us for 17 minutes” (2026, in Spanish)](https://www.infobae.com/estados-unidos/2026/05/11/nos-persiguio-durante-17-minutos-el-impactante-relato-del-piloto-argentino-que-vio-un-ovni-y-cuyo-caso-fue-desclasificado-por-eeuu/)
- [UFOs at close sight — Clarín, August 2, 1995 (translated)](https://ufologie.patrickgross.org/press/clarin2aug1995.htm)

## Varginha "ET" (1996)

- Date: 20 January 1996
- Place: Varginha, Minas Gerais (Brazil)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Close encounter
- Evidence: Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Crouching humanoid with red eyes
- Witnesses: 3 young women; later many rumours
- Duration: Seconds
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/varginha-1996/

Three young women said they saw a strange creature crouched near a wall, with vein-like marks on its skin, three bumps on its head and eyes like "two red balls". Rumours followed of military trucks carrying captured beings, bodies at hospitals, a police officer's death and animal deaths at the zoo. It became Brazil's best-known UFO story and a local tourist theme.

**Explanation:** A Brazilian Army inquiry concluded that the women had seen a local man with a mental disability, known as "Mudinho", and that the military movements were routine.

## Pretoria police helicopter chase (1996)

At 4 a.m., Sgt Nico Stander of the Adriaan Vlok police station in Pretoria reported lights in the sky, which were videotaped. Some 200 officers and a Bo-105 police helicopter followed them east. The helicopter gave up at about 10,000 ft over the Cullinan area when it ran low on fuel. The lights were seen again on the nights of August 31 and September 1.

## The Wash incident (1996)

In the early morning a police officer on the Lincolnshire coast reported a rotating, multicoloured object over The Wash. The Claxby air traffic control radar reported a return in the same area. The report went up through RAF Kinloss and MoD Northwood before the conventional explanation was accepted.

## Phoenix Lights (1997)

- Date: 13 March 1997
- Place: Henderson, NV → Phoenix → Tucson, Arizona (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Video / film footage; Photographs; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Huge V / carpenter’s square with five lights
- Witnesses: Thousands along a 300-mile corridor
- Duration: ~2.5 hours
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/phoenix-lights-1997/

A V-shaped formation of lights was reported moving south-east from the Nevada line, over Prescott Valley and Phoenix to Tucson. Later that night a stationary row of amber lights was widely filmed over Phoenix. The event remains one of the most-witnessed UFO events in U.S. history.

**Explanation:** The ~20:00–20:45 V-formation was traced to A-10 aircraft of Operation Snowbird returning to Davis-Monthan AFB; the ~22:00 row of lights filmed over Phoenix were LUU-2 flares dropped over the Barry Goldwater Range. Some witnesses, including then-governor Fife Symington, reject this.

## Howden Moor — sonic booms and the search for a crash (1997)

- Date: 24 March 1997
- Place: Howden Moors, Dark Peak, on the Derbyshire–South Yorkshire border (United Kingdom)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Mass sighting
- Evidence: Infrared or other sensor data; Police witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: A large low aircraft with lit windows, a dark triangle, two red lights, then an orange glow and smoke
- Witnesses: A special constable and her husband near Bolsterstone, gamekeepers, farmers, a Peak Park warden and others
- Duration: Booms at 21:52 and 22:06; a 15-hour search
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/howden-moor-1997/

Shortly before 10 p.m. on March 24, 1997, people around the moors north-west of Sheffield saw low aircraft and heard explosions. Near Bolsterstone, Special Constable Marie-France Tattersfield and her husband saw a large aircraft with all its windows lit cross in front of them at no more than about 500 ft; a farmer saw a low plane head towards the moor, then an orange glow and plumes of smoke; gamekeepers heard “a terrific explosion”; others described a dark triangle or two red lights. Seismic and acoustic instruments of the British Geological Survey recorded two sonic events, at 21:52 and 22:06. Fearing an air crash, South Yorkshire Police led one of the largest searches in the region’s history: police and RAF helicopters and about 141 mountain-rescue volunteers searched up to 50 square miles of moorland for some 15 hours and found nothing. The Ministry of Defence first said no RAF aircraft was responsible, then admitted that six Tornados had been on low-flying training until 21:30, denied that any had gone supersonic, and closed the case after an RAF Police inquiry with “no military link”. The booms remain unattributed.

**Explanation:** The British Geological Survey said the recorded signal was atmospheric, not an impact, and most likely a supersonic aircraft. The MoD admitted a low-flying exercise by six RAF Tornados that it said had ended at 21:30, and denied any supersonic flight; an RAF Police inquiry in 1998 found no military link and suggested a natural cause such as a re-entry. The researcher David Clarke argues that a covert military flight continued after the exercise.

Sources:
- [The National Archives (UK) — MoD UFO files](https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/help-with-your-research/research-guides/ufos/)
- [David Clarke — The Howden Moor incident](https://drdavidclarke.co.uk/secret-files/howden-moor-incident/)
- [David Clarke — Moorland UFO mystery revisited](https://drclarke.substack.com/p/moorland-ufo-mystery-revisited)

Before dawn, a store owner in Highland and then police officers in Lebanon, Summerfield, Shiloh and Dupo independently reported a large, low triangular object with bright lights moving south-west toward Scott AFB and the Mississippi.

**Explanation:** The FAA suggested an advertising blimp; the officers’ descriptions of speed and size are hard to reconcile with that.

A Mexican Air Force surveillance aircraft hunting drug flights recorded 11 bright objects on its infrared camera at about 11,500 ft. The Defence Department released the tape on 12 May 2004.

## Tinley Park lights (2004)

- Date: 21 August 2004
- Place: Tinley Park and Oak Forest, Illinois (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Recurring lights
- Evidence: Video / film footage; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Three to four red lights in a triangle
- Witnesses: Hundreds in the south suburbs of Chicago
- Duration: Up to 30 minutes, several nights
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/tinley-park-2004/

On the evening of August 21, 2004, hundreds of people in Chicago's south suburbs watched three large red lights in a triangle drift slowly and silently across the sky. Many filmed them. The lights returned on October 31, 2004 and on several nights in 2005 and 2006, and appeared on national television. They are a prominent "black triangle" style case with plenty of video.

**Explanation:** Commonly attributed to balloons or kites carrying lights or flares, which match the slow drift and the colour. No one has come forward, and the cause has not been confirmed.

Sources:

## USS Nimitz "Tic Tac" (2004)

- Date: 14 November 2004
- Place: Pacific Ocean ~100 mi SW of San Diego (International waters (off Baja California))
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Military encounter
- Evidence: Video / film footage; Infrared or other sensor data; Radar tracking; Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: White, smooth 40-ft "Tic Tac"
- Witnesses: 4 aircrew (Fravor, Dietrich + WSOs), USS Princeton radar operators
- Duration: ~5 minutes visual; radar over ~2 weeks
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/nimitz-tic-tac-2004/

For days the cruiser USS Princeton’s SPY-1 radar tracked objects appearing at about 80,000 ft, dropping rapidly toward the sea and hovering. On 14 November, Cdr. David Fravor and Lt. Cdr. Alex Dietrich were vectored to a contact and saw a white Tic Tac-shaped object above a churning patch of ocean. It mirrored Fravor’s descent, then accelerated away; seconds later Princeton reported it at the pilots’ CAP point ~60 miles away. A later sortie filmed the FLIR1 video.

**Explanation:** The Pentagon released the FLIR1 video in 2020 and describes the object as unidentified. Skeptics argue the FLIR clip shows a distant aircraft; the pilots’ visual account is independent of the video.

Sources:
- [DoD statement on the release of historical Navy videos (Apr 2020)](https://www.defense.gov/News/Releases/Release/Article/2165713/statement-by-the-department-of-defense-on-the-release-of-historical-navy-videos/)

## Río de la Plata — two airliners and a rising light (2005)

- Date: 4 April 2005
- Place: Over the Río de la Plata between Ezeiza (Buenos Aires) and Carrasco (Montevideo) (Uruguay / Argentina)
- Status: UNRESOLVED — No accepted explanation
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Military witnesses
- Shape: A luminous object moving upwards
- Witnesses: The pilot of an Aeromas cargo aircraft, a Lufthansa crew and a Uruguayan military pilot
- Duration: Brief
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/rio-de-la-plata-2005/

At about 4 a.m. on Monday, April 4, 2005, the pilot of a Uruguayan Aeromas cargo aircraft that had just left Ezeiza reported a luminous object near his aircraft over the Río de la Plata. The Ezeiza tower suggested it was an engine of a Lufthansa airliner in the area, but the Lufthansa pilot told him he had seen the light too, that it moved upwards and so could not be a meteorite, and called it a missile. A Uruguayan military pilot flying at the same time confirmed a fast luminous object. The reports went through the Carrasco and Ezeiza control towers; the Argentine Air Force recorded the report at Ezeiza, the Argentine armed forces said none of their aircraft or ships were in the area, and the Uruguayan Air Force opened an investigation. No result was published.

Sources:
- [La Nación — “Investigan un extraño incidente” (April 7, 2005)](https://www.lanacion.com.ar/sociedad/investigan-un-extrano-incidente-nid693949/)

## Chicago O’Hare disc (2006)

- Date: 7 November 2006
- Place: O’Hare International Airport, Gate C-17 (United States)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Aviation encounter
- Evidence: Pilot / aircrew witnesses; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Dark grey metallic disc, 6–24 ft
- Witnesses: ~12 United Airlines employees; people outside the airport
- Duration: ~5 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/ohare-2006/

A ramp worker pushing back United Flight 446 saw a dark disc hovering low over Gate C-17; pilots, supervisors and mechanics came out to watch. Witnesses said it shot straight up through the overcast, leaving a clear hole in the clouds that closed moments later. The story emerged via a Chicago Tribune FOIA request.

**Explanation:** The FAA called it a "weather phenomenon" and did not investigate; conditions suited a hole-punch cloud. Nothing appeared on radar.

Flying an Aurigny Trislander from Southampton to Alderney, Capt. Ray Bowyer saw two very large, brilliant yellow objects apparently stationary over the sea, confirmed by passengers and by the pilot of another aircraft. He filed an official report with the Civil Aviation Authority.

**Explanation:** Jersey radar showed only a faint primary return; proposed explanations include earthquake lights and sun dogs.

## Stephenville, Texas (2008)

Dozens of people around Stephenville, including a private pilot and a local constable, reported a very large, silent object with bright lights followed by fighter jets. FOIA radar records later analysed by MUFON showed unidentified returns in the area.

**Explanation:** The Air Force said F-16s from the 457th Fighter Squadron were training in the area. A MUFON analysis of FAA radar data claimed an untransponded target heading toward the Crawford ranch; this is not officially confirmed.

## Morristown lights (admitted hoax) (2009)

- Date: 5 January 2009
- Place: Morris County, New Jersey (United States)
- Status: EXPLAINED — Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
- Kind: Recurring lights
- Evidence: Video / film footage; Photographs; Many independent witnesses; Police witnesses
- Shape: Five red lights in a line and arc
- Witnesses: Dozens of residents, police, Morristown Airport tower staff
- Duration: About 45 minutes, five nights
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/morristown-hoax-2009/

Around 8:15 p.m. on January 5, 2009, residents of Hanover Township, Morristown and nearby towns saw five red lights hanging in the sky and called 9-1-1. Tower staff at Morristown Airport also saw them, but radar showed nothing. TV news and UFO groups covered the lights, and they returned on four more nights. The two men who launched the balloons had also given TV interviews posing as witnesses. They called it a social experiment to show how unreliable eyewitness claims can be.

**Explanation:** Hoax. Joe Rudy and Chris Russo tied road flares to helium balloons and released them on five nights, then revealed it on April 1, 2009 with video of the launches. They were fined for disorderly conduct.

## Norwegian spiral (2009)

- Date: 9 December 2009
- Place: Northern Norway and Sweden (seen from Troms and Finnmark)
- Status: IDENTIFIED — Object positively identified
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs; Video / film footage; Many independent witnesses; Official government document or case file
- Shape: Blue beam with an expanding white spiral
- Witnesses: Thousands across northern Norway and Sweden
- Duration: About 10 minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/norwegian-spiral-2009/

Before sunrise on December 9, 2009, people across northern Norway saw a blue-white light rise from behind the mountains, stop, and begin to spin. A glowing spiral grew outward and dissolved into a black hole-like disc. Photos and video went worldwide within hours. Astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell quickly suggested a failed Russian missile, and Moscow confirmed a Bulava test failure.

**Explanation:** A failed test of a Russian RSM-56 Bulava submarine-launched missile from the White Sea: the third stage malfunctioned, and the spinning missile sprayed fuel in a spiral lit by the Sun. The Russian Defence Ministry confirmed the failure the next day.

## Harbour Mille — the “missiles” over Fortune Bay (2010)

- Date: 25 January 2010 (time approximate)
- Place: Harbour Mille, Fortune Bay, Newfoundland (Canada)
- Status: DISPUTED — Explanation proposed but contested
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: Three large grey or silver “bullets” with fire behind them and trails of smoke
- Witnesses: Emmy Pardy, the postmaster, and two neighbours, one of whom, Darlene Stewart, took photographs
- Duration: Several minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/harbour-mille-2010/

At about sunset on Monday, January 25, 2010, Emmy Pardy and two friends in the small community of Harbour Mille, on Newfoundland’s south coast, saw three objects moving fast across the sky over Fortune Bay. Through binoculars Pardy described one as large and grey or silver with fire coming out of it; they trailed smoke. Darlene Stewart, who had been photographing the sunset, took pictures. When the photographs reached the news, the story became a small political puzzle: the RCMP first spoke of a missile launch and withdrew it, the Prime Minister’s Office said no rocket had been launched, the Defence Minister called the information “spotty”, and the French embassy said there had been no French military activity near Newfoundland or Saint-Pierre and Miquelon.

**Explanation:** Canada and France both said no missile or rocket had been launched; France’s M51 test from the submarine Le Terrible was on a different day and did not match the time or direction. A Royal Military College engineer judged the object subsonic and much smaller than a missile; federal officials suggested model rockets, which the witnesses rejected; and a television station later aired viewer video from the same time that showed a passing aircraft, whose contrail lit by the setting sun would look like a fiery trail. The RCMP closed the file as an unexplained sighting.

Sources:
- [The Globe and Mail — Was it a missile or a hoax?](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/national/was-it-a-missile-or-a-hoax/article4304061)
- [CBC — No evidence UFO was rocket: PMO](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/newfoundland-labrador/no-evidence-ufo-was-rocket-pmo-1.951800)
- [The Canadian Press — Woman who saw “missiles” says the area is not used by model hobbyists](https://www.reddeeradvocate.com/national-news/woman-who-claims-she-saw-missiles-says-area-not-used-by-model-hobbyists/)

## The spiral over eastern Australia — Falcon 9’s first flight (2010)

- Date: 5 June 2010 (time approximate)
- Place: Eastern Australia: New South Wales, the Australian Capital Territory and Queensland
- Status: IDENTIFIED — Object positively identified
- Kind: Photo / video case
- Evidence: Photographs; Video / film footage; Many independent witnesses
- Shape: A large white light with a spiral, “lollipop-type swirl”
- Witnesses: Dozens of people who sent photographs and videos to ABC News, among many others
- Duration: Minutes
- Page: https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/case/falcon9-spiral-australia-2010/

Before dawn on Saturday, June 5, 2010, people across New South Wales, the ACT and Queensland saw a large white light with a spiral around it, which seemed to hover briefly and then drift east out of sight. ABC News received dozens of photographs and videos. Astronomers first suggested space junk, a satellite or a rocket, and Sydney Observatory’s Geoffrey Wyatt suggested a rocket spun for stability. The answer came within a day: the Falcon 9 rocket, flying for the first time, had lifted off from Florida at 2:45 p.m. EDT on June 4 (4:45 a.m. in Sydney), and its second stage, with the Dragon qualification unit attached, was due over eastern Australia between about 5:30 and 5:45 a.m. The second stage had been rotating unexpectedly during the flight.

**Explanation:** The second stage of the first SpaceX Falcon 9, launched from Cape Canaveral at 18:45 UTC on June 4 with a test Dragon capsule, passed over eastern Australia about an hour later. The stage was rolling, and propellant or gas leaking from it formed a lit spiral, as the Bulava missile’s did over Norway six months earlier. Satellite observers matched the time and the ground track; Sydney Observatory also said it was the rocket.

Sources:
- [iTWire — UFO in Australia explained: Falcon 9](https://itwire.com/science-news/space/ufo-in-australia-explained-falcon-9)
- [Space.com — “UFO” spotted over Australia likely a private rocket](https://space.com/8546-ufo-spotted-australia-private-rocket.html)
